ākaraḥ sarvaratnānāṃ sarvasattvasamāśrayaḥ ..
tāpasānāmadhīvāsaḥ śrāddhaṃ tatrā'kṣayaṃ bhavet ..15..
1.144.d:
आकरः सर्वरत्नानां सर्वसत्त्वसमाश्रयः ॥
तापसानामधीवासः श्राद्धं तत्राऽक्षयं भवेत् ॥15॥
1.144.m: A mine of all jewels, a refuge of all beings, / and an abode of ascetics: there a śrāddha becomes imperishable.

1.144.s:
evamādiṣu tīrtheṣu parvateṣu saritsu ca ..
sarovareṣu mukhyeṣu ṛṣīṇāmāśrameṣu ca..16..
1.144.d:
एवमादिषु तीर्थेषु पर्वतेषु सरित्सु च ॥
सरोवरेषु मुख्येषु ऋषीणामाश्रमेषु च॥16॥
1.144.m: At such holy bathing places, on mountains, and by rivers, / at foremost lakes, and in the hermitages of the sages,

1.144.s:
nirjhareṣu tathāraṇye nadīnāṃ prabhaveṣu ca ..
saṅgameṣu ca mukhyeṣu pulineṣu viśeṣataḥ ..17..
1.144.d:
निर्झरेषु तथारण्ये नदीनां प्रभवेषु च ॥
सङ्गमेषु च मुख्येषु पुलिनेषु विशेषतः ॥17॥
1.144.m: at waterfalls, in the wilderness, and at the sources of rivers, / at foremost confluences, and especially on sandbanks,

1.144.s:
udyāneṣu vicitreṣu saikateṣu sameṣu ca..
śādvaleṣu ca ramyeṣu girīṇāṃ kandarāsu ca .. 18 ..
1.144.d:
उद्यानेषु विचित्रेषु सैकतेषु समेषु च॥
शाद्वलेषु च रम्येषु गिरीणां कन्दरासु च ॥ 18 ॥
1.144.m: in variegated gardens, on even sandy banks, / on delightful grassy lawns, and in mountain caves,

1.144.s:
gahvareṣu nitambeṣu cchāyāyāṃ kuñjarasya ca ..
mahīgatāntaranyastagajacchāyāsu pārthiva .. 19 ..
1.144.d:
गह्वरेषु नितम्बेषु च्छायायां कुञ्जरस्य च ॥
महीगतान्तरन्यस्तगजच्छायासु पार्थिव ॥ 19 ॥
1.144.m: in chasms, on mountain slopes, in the shade of an elephant, / and during the shadows of an elephant cast upon the earth, O king—

1.144.s:
yaḥ kuryādaparāhṇe tu sakṛcchrāddhaṃ prayatnataḥ ..
akṣayyamannapānaṃ tu pitṝṇāṃ copatiṣṭhate..1.144.20..
1.144.d:
यः कुर्यादपराह्णे तु सकृच्छ्राद्धं प्रयत्नतः ॥
अक्षय्यमन्नपानं तु पितॄणां चोपतिष्ठते॥1.144.20॥
1.144.m: he who, taking care, performs a śrāddha even once in the afternoon / provides the ancestors with inexhaustible food and drink.

1.144.s:
gomayenopalipteṣu śrāddhaṃ kāryaṃ gṛheṣu ca..
manojñeṣu vicitreṣu rucireṣūttameṣu ca..21..
1.144.d:
गोमयेनोपलिप्तेषु श्राद्धं कार्यं गृहेषु च॥
मनोज्ञेषु विचित्रेषु रुचिरेषूत्तमेषु च॥21॥
1.144.m: A śrāddha should also be performed in houses smeared with cow dung, / which are charming, diverse, pleasant, and of the best kind.

1.144.s: devāyatanagoṣṭheṣu śrāddhaṃ bahuphalaṃ bhavet ..22..
1.144.d: देवायतनगोष्ठेषु श्राद्धं बहुफलं भवेत् ॥22॥
1.144.m: In temples and in cowpens a śrāddha brings abundant fruit.

1.144.s:
tīrthāni yānīha narendracandra loke purāṇaiḥ parikīrtitāni ..
tīreṣu teṣāṃ vidhivatpradāya śrāddhaṃ na śocenmaraṇaṃ jitātmā .. 23 ..
1.144.d:
तीर्थानि यानीह नरेन्द्रचन्द्र लोके पुराणैः परिकीर्तितानि ॥
तीरेषु तेषां विधिवत्प्रदाय श्राद्धं न शोचेन्मरणं जितात्मा ॥ 23 ॥
1.144.m: Those holy bathing places here in the world, O moon among kings, that have been celebrated by the ancient ones— / having offered a śrāddha on their banks in accordance with rule, one of subdued self does not grieve over death.

1.145.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi pitṛbhiryāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ..
gāthāḥ pārthivaśārdūla kāmayadbhiḥ pure svake .. 1 ..
1.145.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि पितृभिर्याः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
गाथाः पार्थिवशार्दूल कामयद्भिः पुरे स्वके ॥ 1 ॥
1.145.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Hereafter I shall proclaim the verses sung by the ancestors, / O tiger among kings, as they wished [thus] in their own city:

1.145.s:
api syātsa kule'smākaṃ yo no dadyājjalāñjalim ..
nadīṣu bahutoyāsu śītalāsu viśeṣataḥ .. 2 ..
1.145.d:
अपि स्यात्स कुलेऽस्माकं यो नो दद्याज्जलाञ्जलिम् ॥
नदीषु बहुतोयासु शीतलासु विशेषतः ॥ 2 ॥
1.145.m: "May there be one in our lineage who would offer us a double handful of water, / especially in rivers carrying abundant, cool water!

1.145.s:
api syātsa kule'smākaṃ himamiśraṃ jalāñjalim ..
tilamākṣika saṃyuktaṃ yo no dadyātsamāhitaḥ .. 3 ..
1.145.d:
अपि स्यात्स कुलेऽस्माकं हिममिश्रं जलाञ्जलिम् ॥
तिलमाक्षिक संयुक्तं यो नो दद्यात्समाहितः ॥ 3 ॥
1.145.m: May there be one in our lineage who, collected in mind, would offer us / a double handful of water mingled with snow and accompanied by sesame and honey!

1.145.s:
api syātsa kule'smākaṃ yo no dadyācca bhaktitaḥ ..
pāyasaṃ madhusaṃmiśraṃ varṣāsu ca maghāsu ca ..4..
1.145.d:
अपि स्यात्स कुलेऽस्माकं यो नो दद्याच्च भक्तितः ॥
पायसं मधुसंमिश्रं वर्षासु च मघासु च ॥4॥
1.145.m: May there be one in our lineage who would devotedly offer us / milk-rice mixed with honey during the rains and under the Maghās!"

1.145.s:
dālbhya uvāca ..
patnyo nṛṇāṃ muniśreṣṭha yoṣitāṃ ca tathā narāḥ ..
tacchrotumicchāmi viprarṣe vidhavā strī na jāyate .. 5 ..
1.145.d:
दाल्भ्य उवाच ॥
पत्न्यो नृणां मुनिश्रेष्ठ योषितां च तथा नराः ॥
तच्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि विप्रर्षे विधवा स्त्री न जायते ॥ 5 ॥
1.145.m: Dālbhya said: / [How do] wives [not be parted from] their men, O best of sages, and likewise men from their women? / I wish to hear that, O brahmin sage, whereby a woman does not become a widow,

1.145.s:
upoṣitena yenāgrya patnyā na rahito naraḥ ..
pulasttya uvāca ..
aśūnyaśayanāṃ nāma dvitīyāṃ śṛṇu bho dvija ..6 ..
1.145.d:
उपोषितेन येनाग्र्य पत्न्या न रहितो नरः ॥
पुलस्त्त्य उवाच ॥
अशून्यशयनां नाम द्वितीयां शृणु भो द्विज ॥6 ॥
1.145.m: and whereby, when he has fasted, an excellent man is not deprived of his wife. / Pulastya said: / Hear, O twice-born, of the second lunar day named Aśūnyaśayanā,

1.145.s:
yāmupoṣya na vaidhavyaṃ prayāti strī dvijottama ..
patnīvimuktaśca naro na kadācitprajāyate .. 7 ..
1.145.d:
यामुपोष्य न वैधव्यं प्रयाति स्त्री द्विजोत्तम ॥
पत्नीविमुक्तश्च नरो न कदाचित्प्रजायते ॥ 7 ॥
1.145.m: having fasted on which, O best of the twice-born, a woman never undergoes widowhood, / and a man is never born bereft of his wife.

1.145.s:
śete jalanidhau kṛṣṇaḥ śriyā sārdhaṃ yadā dvija ..
aśūnyaśayanā nāma tadā śrāddhe hi sā tithiḥ .. 8 ..
1.145.d:
शेते जलनिधौ कृष्णः श्रिया सार्धं यदा द्विज ॥
अशून्यशयना नाम तदा श्राद्धे हि सा तिथिः ॥ 8 ॥
1.145.m: When Kṛṣṇa lies in the ocean together with Śrī, O twice-born, / then indeed that lunar day is named Aśūnyaśayanā for a śrāddha.

1.145.s:
kṛṣṇapakṣadvitīyāyāṃ śrāvaṇe munisattama ..
imamuccārayenmantraṃ praṇamya jagataḥ patim .. 9 ..
1.145.d:
कृष्णपक्षद्वितीयायां श्रावणे मुनिसत्तम ॥
इममुच्चारयेन्मन्त्रं प्रणम्य जगतः पतिम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.145.m: On the second lunar day of the dark fortnight in the month of Śrāvaṇa, O best of sages, / one should bow down to the Lord of the world and recite this mantra,

1.145.s:
śrīvatsadhāriṇaṃ śrīśaṃ bhaktyābhyarcya śriyā saha ..
śrīvatsadhāriñchrīkānta śrīdhāma śrīpate'cyuta .. 1.145.10 ..
1.145.d:
श्रीवत्सधारिणं श्रीशं भक्त्याभ्यर्च्य श्रिया सह ॥
श्रीवत्सधारिञ्छ्रीकान्त श्रीधाम श्रीपतेऽच्युत ॥ 1.145.10 ॥
1.145.m: having worshipped with devotion the Lord of Śrī, the bearer of the śrīvatsa mark, together with Śrī: / "O bearer of the śrīvatsa mark, O beloved of Śrī, O abode of Śrī, O Lord of Śrī, O Acyuta,

1.145.s:
gārhasthyaṃ mā praṇāśaṃ me yātu dharmārthakāmada..
agnayo mā praṇaśyantu mā praṇaśyantu devatāḥ .. 11 ..
1.145.d:
गार्हस्थ्यं मा प्रणाशं मे यातु धर्मार्थकामद॥
अग्नयो मा प्रणश्यन्तु मा प्रणश्यन्तु देवताः ॥ 11 ॥
1.145.m: may my householder life not go to ruin, O granter of dharma, wealth, and pleasure! / May the fires not perish, may the deities not perish,

1.145.s:
pitaro mā praṇaśyantu matto dāmpatyabhedataḥ ..
lakṣmyā viyujyate deva na kadācidyathā bhavān .. 12 ..
1.145.d:
पितरो मा प्रणश्यन्तु मत्तो दाम्पत्यभेदतः ॥
लक्ष्म्या वियुज्यते देव न कदाचिद्यथा भवान् ॥ 12 ॥
1.145.m: and may the ancestors not perish from me through the separation of husband and wife! / Just as You, O God, are never parted from Lakṣmī,

1.145.s:
tathā kalatrasaṃbandho deva me naiva bhidyatu ..
lakṣmyā hyaśūnyaṃ varada yathā te śayanaṃ sadā .. 13 ..
1.145.d:
तथा कलत्रसंबन्धो देव मे नैव भिद्यतु ॥
लक्ष्म्या ह्यशून्यं वरद यथा ते शयनं सदा ॥ 13 ॥
1.145.m: so may my union with my wife never be broken, O God! / For just as Your couch is always nonempty of Lakṣmī, O granter of boons,

1.145.s:
śayyā mamāpyaśūnyāstu tathaiva madhusūdana ..
evaṃ prasādya pūjāṃ ca kṛtvā lakṣmyāstathā hareḥ ..14..
1.145.d:
शय्या ममाप्यशून्यास्तु तथैव मधुसूदन ॥
एवं प्रसाद्य पूजां च कृत्वा लक्ष्म्यास्तथा हरेः ॥14॥
1.145.m: so also may my bed be nonempty, O Madhusūdana!" / Having thus propitiated and performed the worship of Lakṣmī and Hari,

1.145.s:
phalāni dadyācchāyāyāmabhīṣṭāni jagatpateḥ ..
naktaṃ praṇamyāyatane havirbhuñjīta vāgyataḥ .. 15 ..
1.145.d:
फलानि दद्याच्छायायामभीष्टानि जगत्पतेः ॥
नक्तं प्रणम्यायतने हविर्भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ॥ 15 ॥
1.145.m: one should offer the favored fruits of the Lord of the world in the shade. / Having bowed down in the sanctuary at night, one should eat sacrificial food with speech restrained.

1.145.s:
brāhmaṇāya dvitīye'hni śayyāṃ dayātsadakṣiṇām..
evaṃ karoti yaḥ samyaṅnaro māsacatuṣṭayam..16..
1.145.d:
ब्राह्मणाय द्वितीयेऽह्नि शय्यां दयात्सदक्षिणाम्॥
एवं करोति यः सम्यङ्नरो मासचतुष्टयम्॥16॥
1.145.m: On the second day, one should give a bed accompanied by a sacrificial fee to a brahmin. / The man who performs this properly for four months—

1.145.s:
tasya janmatraye dālbhya gṛhabhaṅgo na jāyate..
aśūnyaśayanaścāsau dharmakarmārthasādhakaḥ ..17..
1.145.d:
तस्य जन्मत्रये दाल्भ्य गृहभङ्गो न जायते॥
अशून्यशयनश्चासौ धर्मकर्मार्थसाधकः ॥17॥
1.145.m: for him, O Dālbhya, no ruin of the household occurs for three births. / His bed will not be empty, and he will accomplish dharma, ritual, and wealth;

1.145.s:
bhavatyavyākṛtaiśvaryaḥ puruṣo nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
nārī ca dālbhya dharmajña vratametadyathāvidhi ..18..
1.145.d:
भवत्यव्याकृतैश्वर्यः पुरुषो नात्र संशयः ॥
नारी च दाल्भ्य धर्मज्ञ व्रतमेतद्यथाविधि ॥18॥
1.145.m: the man will possess unobstructed sovereignty; of this there is no doubt. / And the woman, O Dālbhya who know dharma, who performs this observance according to rule—

1.145.s:
yā karoti na sā śocyā bandhuvargasya jāyate ..
vaidhavyaṃ durbhagatvaṃ vā bhartṛvyaṅgyaṃ ca sattama..19..
1.145.d:
या करोति न सा शोच्या बन्धुवर्गस्य जायते ॥
वैधव्यं दुर्भगत्वं वा भर्तृव्यङ्ग्यं च सत्तम॥19॥
1.145.m: she does not become an object of grief to her circle of kinsfolk. / Widowhood, misfortune, or abandonment by a husband, O best of men,

1.145.s: nāpnoti janmatritayametaccīrtvā pativratā .. 1.145.20 ..
1.145.d: नाप्नोति जन्मत्रितयमेतच्चीर्त्वा पतिव्रता ॥ 1.145.20 ॥
1.145.m: a devoted wife does not incur for three births, having performed this.

1.146.s:
dālbhya uvāca ..
upavāsāśritaṃ samyaglokadvayaphalapradam ..
kathitaṃ bhavatā sarvaṃ yatpṛṣṭo'si mayā dvija .. 1 ..
1.146.d:
दाल्भ्य उवाच ॥
उपवासाश्रितं सम्यग्लोकद्वयफलप्रदम् ॥
कथितं भवता सर्वं यत्पृष्टोऽसि मया द्विज ॥ 1 ॥
1.146.m: Dālbhya said: / Everything connected with fasting that grants the fruit of both worlds / has been fully related by you as asked by me, O twice-born.

1.146.s:
anyadicchāmyahaṃ śrotuṃ tadbhavānprabavītu me ..
saṃsārahetuṃ muktiśca saṃsārānmunisattama .. 2 ..
1.146.d:
अन्यदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं तद्भवान्प्रबवीतु मे ॥
संसारहेतुं मुक्तिश्च संसारान्मुनिसत्तम ॥ 2 ॥
1.146.m: I desire to hear something else; let your honor declare that to me: / the cause of saṃsāra and liberation from saṃsāra, O best of sages.

1.146.s:
pulastya uvāca ..
avidyāprabhavaṃ karma hetubhūtaṃ dvijottama..
saṃsārasyāsya tanmuktiḥ saṃkṣepācchrūyatāṃ mama .. 3 ..
1.146.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ॥
अविद्याप्रभवं कर्म हेतुभूतं द्विजोत्तम॥
संसारस्यास्य तन्मुक्तिः संक्षेपाच्छ्रूयतां मम ॥ 3 ॥
1.146.m: Pulastya said: / Action arising from ignorance is the cause, O best of the twice-born, / of this saṃsāra; hear from me in brief about release from it.

1.146.s:
svajātivihitaṃ karma rāgadveṣavivarjitam ..
kurvataḥ kṣīyate pūrvamanyabandhaśca neṣyate .. 4 ..
1.146.d:
स्वजातिविहितं कर्म रागद्वेषविवर्जितम् ॥
कुर्वतः क्षीयते पूर्वमन्यबन्धश्च नेष्यते ॥ 4 ॥
1.146.m: For one who performs the action prescribed for his own class, free from attachment and aversion, / former [action] is destroyed, and no other bondage is accepted.

1.146.s:
apūrvasaṃbhavābhāvātkṣayaṃ yāte tu karmaṇi ..
dālbhya saṃsāravicchedaḥ kāraṇābhāvasaṃbhavaḥ .. 5 ..
1.146.d:
अपूर्वसंभवाभावात्क्षयं याते तु कर्मणि ॥
दाल्भ्य संसारविच्छेदः कारणाभावसंभवः ॥ 5 ॥
1.146.m: When action has gone to destruction due to the absence of the arising of new [action], / O Dālbhya, the cessation of saṃsāra occurs, arising from the absence of the cause.

1.146.s:
bhavatyasaṃśayaṃ cānyacchrūyatāmatra kāraṇam ..
saṃsāravicyuterdālbhya samāsādvadato mama .. 6 ..
1.146.d:
भवत्यसंशयं चान्यच्छ्रूयतामत्र कारणम् ॥
संसारविच्युतेर्दाल्भ्य समासाद्वदतो मम ॥ 6 ॥
1.146.m: This is without doubt; and hear another cause in this matter, / as I speak in summary of the severance of saṃsāra, O Dālbhya.

1.146.s:
gṛhītā karmaṇā yena puṃsā jātirdvijottama ..
tatprāyaścittabhūtaṃ vai śṛṇu karmakṣayāvaham .. 7 ..
1.146.d:
गृहीता कर्मणा येन पुंसा जातिर्द्विजोत्तम ॥
तत्प्रायश्चित्तभूतं वै शृणु कर्मक्षयावहम् ॥ 7 ॥
1.146.m: By whatever action a birth was assumed by a man, O best of the twice-born, / hear that which constitutes its expiation, bringing about the destruction of action:

1.146.s:
brāhmaṇakṣattriyaviśāṃ śūdrāntyānāṃ ca sattama ..
svajātivihitaṃ karma rāgadveṣavivarjitam .. 8 ..
1.146.d:
ब्राह्मणक्षत्त्रियविशां शूद्रान्त्यानां च सत्तम ॥
स्वजातिविहितं कर्म रागद्वेषविवर्जितम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.146.m: for brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and lowest śūdras, O best of men, / the action prescribed for one's own class, free from attachment and aversion,

1.146.s:
jātipradasyākṣayadaṃ tadevādyasya karmaṇaḥ ..
jñānakāraṇabhāvaṃ ca tadeva pratipadyate .. 9 ..
1.146.d:
जातिप्रदस्याक्षयदं तदेवाद्यस्य कर्मणः ॥
ज्ञानकारणभावं च तदेव प्रतिपद्यते ॥ 9 ॥
1.146.m: brings about the destruction of that very primal action that gave birth; / and that alone attains the status of being a cause of knowledge.

1.146.s:
pumām̐ścādhigatajñāno bhedaṃ nāpnoti sattama ..
brahmaṇā viṣṇusaṃjñena parameṇāvyayātmanā ..1.146.10..
1.146.d:
पुमाम्̐श्चाधिगतज्ञानो भेदं नाप्नोति सत्तम ॥
ब्रह्मणा विष्णुसंज्ञेन परमेणाव्ययात्मना ॥1.146.10॥
1.146.m: And the man who has attained knowledge suffers no distinction, O best of men, / from Brahman, named Viṣṇu, the supreme, imperishable Self.

1.146.s:
etatte kathitaṃ dālbhya saṃsārasya samāsataḥ ..
kāraṇaṃ bhavamuktiśca jāyate yogino yathā .. 11 ..
1.146.d:
एतत्ते कथितं दाल्भ्य संसारस्य समासतः ॥
कारणं भवमुक्तिश्च जायते योगिनो यथा ॥ 11 ॥
1.146.m: This has been told to you in summary, O Dālbhya: the cause / of saṃsāra, and how liberation from worldly existence comes to be for a yogin.

1.146.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
iti dālbhyaḥ pulastyena yathāvatpratibodhitaḥ ..
ārādhayāmāsa hariṃ lebhe kāmām̐śca vāñchitān 12 ..
1.146.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
इति दाल्भ्यः पुलस्त्येन यथावत्प्रतिबोधितः ॥
आराधयामास हरिं लेभे कामाम्̐श्च वाञ्छितान् 12 ॥
1.146.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Thus Dālbhya, properly instructed by Pulastya, / propitiated Hari and obtained his desired wishes.

1.146.s:
tathā tvamapi rājendra keśavārādhanaṃ kuru ..
ārādhya taṃ jagannāthaṃ na kaścidavasīdati .. 13 ..
1.146.d:
तथा त्वमपि राजेन्द्र केशवाराधनं कुरु ॥
आराध्य तं जगन्नाथं न कश्चिदवसीदति ॥ 13 ॥
1.146.m: So you too, O king of kings, perform the worship of Keśava; / having worshipped that Lord of the world, no one sinks into despair.

1.146.s:
etanmayoktaṃ sakalaṃ tava bhūmipa pṛcchataḥ ..
anārādhyācyutaṃ devaṃ kaḥ kāmānāpnuyānnaraḥ .. 14 ..
1.146.d:
एतन्मयोक्तं सकलं तव भूमिप पृच्छतः ॥
अनाराध्याच्युतं देवं कः कामानाप्नुयान्नरः ॥ 14 ॥
1.146.m: All this has been told by me to you as you asked, O king. / Without worshipping the god Acyuta, what man could obtain his desires?

1.146.s:
vajra uvāca ..
bhagavānavatīrṇo'bhūnmartyalokamihācyutaḥ ..
bhārāvatāraṇārthāya bhuvo bhūmipatirhariḥ ..15..
1.146.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
भगवानवतीर्णोऽभून्मर्त्यलोकमिहाच्युतः ॥
भारावतारणार्थाय भुवो भूमिपतिर्हरिः ॥15॥
1.146.m: Vajra said: / The blessed Lord, Acyuta, descended here into the mortal world; / Hari, the lord of the earth, [came] in order to remove the burden of the earth.

1.146.s:
mānuṣattve ca govindo mama pūrvapitāmahaḥ ..
cakāra prītimatulāṃ pāṇḍuputraiḥ saha dvija ..16..
1.146.d:
मानुषत्त्वे च गोविन्दो मम पूर्वपितामहः ॥
चकार प्रीतिमतुलां पाण्डुपुत्रैः सह द्विज ॥16॥
1.146.m: And while in human form, Govinda, my ancestral grandfather, / showed peerless love for the sons of Pāṇḍu, O twice-born.

1.146.s:
sārathyaṃ kṛtavām̐ścaiva teṣāṃ sarveśvaro hariḥ ..
nistīrṇo yena bhīṣmaugho kurusainyamahodadhiḥ ..17..
1.146.d:
सारथ्यं कृतवाम्̐श्चैव तेषां सर्वेश्वरो हरिः ॥
निस्तीर्णो येन भीष्मौघो कुरुसैन्यमहोदधिः ॥17॥
1.146.m: And Hari, the Lord of all, served as their charioteer, / by whom the flood that was Bhīṣma, the great ocean that was the Kuru army, was crossed.

1.146.s:
upakārī mahābhāgaḥ sa teṣāṃ sarvavastuṣu ..
keśavaḥ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ sutānāṃ janako yathā .. 18 ..
1.146.d:
उपकारी महाभागः स तेषां सर्ववस्तुषु ॥
केशवः पाण्डुपुत्राणां सुतानां जनको यथा ॥ 18 ॥
1.146.m: That illustrious Keśava was their benefactor in all matters, / to the sons of Pāṇḍu just as a father is to his sons.

1.146.s:
dhanyāste kṛtapuṇyāśca te me pāṇḍusutā matāḥ ..
viviśurye pariṣvaṅgairgovindabhujapañjaram .. 19 ..
1.146.d:
धन्यास्ते कृतपुण्याश्च ते मे पाण्डुसुता मताः ॥
विविशुर्ये परिष्वङ्गैर्गोविन्दभुजपञ्जरम् ॥ 19 ॥
1.146.m: Blessed and meritorious, in my view, are those sons of Pāṇḍu, / who entered the cage of Govinda's arms in embraces.

1.146.s:
rājyahetorarīñjaghnura kasmātpāṇḍunandanāḥ ..
saptalokaikanāthena ye bhavantyekaśāyinaḥ .. 1.146.20 ..
1.146.d:
राज्यहेतोररीञ्जघ्नुर कस्मात्पाण्डुनन्दनाः ॥
सप्तलोकैकनाथेन ये भवन्त्येकशायिनः ॥ 1.146.20 ॥
1.146.m: Did the sons of Pāṇḍu slay their enemies for the sake of a kingdom without reason, / they who shared a single bed with the sole master of the seven worlds?

1.146.s:
ātmānamanugacchāmi bhagavangatakalmaṣam ..
jātaṃ nirdhūtapāpe'smin kule viṣṇuparigrahe .. 21 ..
1.146.d:
आत्मानमनुगच्छामि भगवन्गतकल्मषम् ॥
जातं निर्धूतपापेऽस्मिन् कुले विष्णुपरिग्रहे ॥ 21 ॥
1.146.m: I consider myself free from stain, O blessed one, / having been born in this family free of sin, taken under the protection of Viṣṇu.

1.146.s:
evaṃ devavarasteṣāṃ prasādasumukho hariḥ..
pṛcchatāṃ kaccidācaṣṭa kiñcidguhyaṃ mahātmanām .. 22 ..
1.146.d:
एवं देववरस्तेषां प्रसादसुमुखो हरिः॥
पृच्छतां कच्चिदाचष्ट किञ्चिद्गुह्यं महात्मनाम् ॥ 22 ॥
1.146.m: Thus, did Hari, the best of gods, favorably inclined to grant grace, / reveal some secret to those great-souled ones as they questioned him?

1.146.s:
guhyāñjanārdanaṃ yām̐stu dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ ..
papraccha dharmānakhilām̐stānsamākhyātumarhasi .. 23 ..
1.146.d:
गुह्याञ्जनार्दनं याम्̐स्तु धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः ॥
पप्रच्छ धर्मानखिलाम्̐स्तान्समाख्यातुमर्हसि ॥ 23 ॥
1.146.m: Which secret dharmas in their entirety did Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma, / ask Janārdana about? You ought to declare them to me.

1.146.s:
dharmārthakāmamokṣeṣu yadguhyaṃ madhūsūdanaḥ ..
teṣāmavocadbhagavāñchrotumicchāmi tattvataḥ .. 24 ..
1.146.d:
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षेषु यद्गुह्यं मधूसूदनः ॥
तेषामवोचद्भगवाञ्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः ॥ 24 ॥
1.146.m: Whatever secret concerning dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa the blessed one, / the Slayer of Madhu, spoke to them, I wish to hear in truth.

1.146.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
bahūni dharmaguhyāni dharmaputrāya keśavaḥ ..
purā provāca rājendra prasādasumukho hariḥ. .. 25 ..
1.146.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
बहूनि धर्मगुह्यानि धर्मपुत्राय केशवः ॥
पुरा प्रोवाच राजेन्द्र प्रसादसुमुखो हरिः॥। 25 ॥
1.146.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Long ago, O king of kings, Keśava, / Hari, favorably inclined to grant grace, spoke many secrets of dharma to the son of Dharma.

1.146.s:
śaratalpagatādbhīṣmāddharmāñchrutvā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ ..
pṛṣṭavānyajjagannāthaṃ tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu .. 26 ..
1.146.d:
शरतल्पगताद्भीष्माद्धर्माञ्छ्रुत्वा युधिष्ठिरः ॥
पृष्टवान्यज्जगन्नाथं तन्मे निगदतः शृणु ॥ 26 ॥
1.146.m: Having heard the dharmas from Bhīṣma lying on the bed of arrows, / Yudhiṣṭhira asked the Lord of the World something; hear that from me as I speak.

1.146.s:
pañcamenāśvamedhena yadā snāto yudhiṣṭhiraḥ ..
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca .. ..
bhagavanvaiṣṇavā dharmāḥ kiṃphalāḥ kiṃparāyaṇāḥ .. 27 ..
1.146.d:
पञ्चमेनाश्वमेधेन यदा स्नातो युधिष्ठिरः ॥
युधिष्ठिर उवाच ॥ ॥
भगवन्वैष्णवा धर्माः किंफलाः किंपरायणाः ॥ 27 ॥
1.146.m: When Yudhiṣṭhira took his bath after the fifth horse sacrifice— / Yudhiṣṭhira said: / O blessed one, what fruits do the Vaiṣṇava dharmas yield, and what is their supreme goal?

1.146.s:
kiṃ kṛtyamadhikṛtyaite bhavatotpāditāḥ purā ..
yadi te pāṇḍavasneho vidyate madhusūdana .. 28 ..
1.146.d:
किं कृत्यमधिकृत्यैते भवतोत्पादिताः पुरा ॥
यदि ते पाण्डवस्नेहो विद्यते मधुसूदन ॥ 28 ॥
1.146.m: With reference to what duty were these produced by you of old? / If there is affection in you for the Pāṇḍavas, O Slayer of Madhu,

1.146.s:
śrotavyāste mayā dharmāstatastānkathayākhilān ..
pavitrāścaiva ye dharmāḥ sarvapāpapraṇāśanāḥ .. 29 ..
1.146.d:
श्रोतव्यास्ते मया धर्मास्ततस्तान्कथयाखिलान् ॥
पवित्राश्चैव ये धर्माः सर्वपापप्रणाशनाः ॥ 29 ॥
1.146.m: those dharmas must be heard by me; therefore tell them all to me, / and also those purifying dharmas that destroy all sins,

1.146.s:
tava vaktracyutā deva sarvadharmeṣvanuttamāḥ ..
yāñchrutvā brahmahā goghnaḥ pitṛghno gurutalpagaḥ .. 1.146.30 ..
1.146.d:
तव वक्त्रच्युता देव सर्वधर्मेष्वनुत्तमाः ॥
याञ्छ्रुत्वा ब्रह्महा गोघ्नः पितृघ्नो गुरुतल्पगः ॥ 1.146.30 ॥
1.146.m: fallen from your mouth, O Lord, unexcelled among all dharmas, / by hearing which a slayer of a brahmin, a slayer of a cow, a slayer of a father, one who violates the teacher's bed,

1.146.s:
surāpo vā kṛtaghnaśca mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ ..
etanme kathitaṃ sarvaṃ sabhāmadhye surottama .. 31 ..
1.146.d:
सुरापो वा कृतघ्नश्च मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः ॥
एतन्मे कथितं सर्वं सभामध्ये सुरोत्तम ॥ 31 ॥
1.146.m: or a drinker of liquor, or an ungrateful person, is freed from all sins. / All this was declared to me in the midst of the assembly, O best of gods,

1.146.s:
vasiṣṭhādyairmahābhāgairmunibhirbhāvitātmabhiḥ ..
tato'haṃ tava deveśa pādamūlamupāgataḥ .. 32 ..
1.146.d:
वसिष्ठाद्यैर्महाभागैर्मुनिभिर्भावितात्मभिः ॥
ततोऽहं तव देवेश पादमूलमुपागतः ॥ 32 ॥
1.146.m: by illustrious sages headed by Vasiṣṭha whose minds were purified; / therefore, O Lord of gods, I have approached the base of your feet.

1.146.s:
dharmānkathaya tāndeva yadyahaṃ bhavataḥ priyaḥ ..
śrutvā me mānavāndharmānvāsiṣṭhānvā mahāphalān .. 33 ..
1.146.d:
धर्मान्कथय तान्देव यद्यहं भवतः प्रियः ॥
श्रुत्वा मे मानवान्धर्मान्वासिष्ठान्वा महाफलान् ॥ 33 ॥
1.146.m: Tell me those dharmas, O God, if I am dear to you. / Having heard the dharmas of Manu and those of Vasiṣṭha, yielding great fruit,

1.146.s:
parāśarakṛtām̐ścaiva tathā'treyasya dhīmataḥ ..
śrutvā śaṅkhasya gārgyasya likhitasya yamasya ca .. 34 ..
1.146.d:
पराशरकृताम्̐श्चैव तथाऽत्रेयस्य धीमतः ॥
श्रुत्वा शङ्खस्य गार्ग्यस्य लिखितस्य यमस्य च ॥ 34 ॥
1.146.m: and those composed by Parāśara, and likewise of the wise son of Atri; / having heard those of Śaṅkha, of Gārgya, of Likhita, and of Yama;

1.146.s:
jābāleśca mahābāhormunerdvaipāyanasya ca ..
umāmaheśvarāścaiva jātidharmāśca pāvanāḥ .. 35 ..
1.146.d:
जाबालेश्च महाबाहोर्मुनेर्द्वैपायनस्य च ॥
उमामहेश्वराश्चैव जातिधर्माश्च पावनाः ॥ 35 ॥
1.146.m: and of Jābāli, and of the mighty-armed sage Dvaipāyana; / and those of Umā and Maheśvara, and the purifying dharmas of caste;

1.146.s:
guṇasya guṇabāhośca kāśyapeyāstathaiva ca ..
bahvāyanakṛtāścaiva śākuneyāstathaiva ca .. 36 ..
1.146.d:
गुणस्य गुणबाहोश्च काश्यपेयास्तथैव च ॥
बह्वायनकृताश्चैव शाकुनेयास्तथैव च ॥ 36 ॥
1.146.m: and of Guṇa and Guṇabāhu, and likewise those of the son of Kaśyapa; / and those composed by Bahvāyana, and likewise those of the son of Śakuni;

1.146.s:
agastyagītā maudgalyāḥ śāṇḍilyāḥ saurabhāstathā ..
bhṛgoraṅgirasaścaiva kaśyapoddālakoditāḥ .. 37 ..
1.146.d:
अगस्त्यगीता मौद्गल्याः शाण्डिल्याः सौरभास्तथा ॥
भृगोरङ्गिरसश्चैव कश्यपोद्दालकोदिताः ॥ 37 ॥
1.146.m: those sung by Agastya, those of Mudgala, those of Śāṇḍilya, and those of Surabhi; / those of Bhṛgu and of Aṅgiras, and those proclaimed by Kaśyapa and Uddālaka;

1.146.s:
sumantā jaiminīyāśca pailasya ca mahātmanaḥ ..
vaiśampāyanagītāśca pippalādakṛtāśca ye .. 38 ..
1.146.d:
सुमन्ता जैमिनीयाश्च पैलस्य च महात्मनः ॥
वैशम्पायनगीताश्च पिप्पलादकृताश्च ये ॥ 38 ॥
1.146.m: those of Sumantu and Jaimini, and of the great-souled Paila; / and those sung by Vaiśampāyana, and those composed by Pippalāda;

1.146.s:
aindrāśca vāruṇāścaiva kauberā vātsyapoṇakāḥ ..
āpastambakṛtā dharmāstathā gopālakasya ca .. 39 ..
1.146.d:
ऐन्द्राश्च वारुणाश्चैव कौबेरा वात्स्यपोणकाः ॥
आपस्तम्बकृता धर्मास्तथा गोपालकस्य च ॥ 39 ॥
1.146.m: and those of Indra, and of Varuṇa, and of Kubera, the Vātsyapoṇakas; / the dharmas composed by Āpastamba, and likewise of Gopālaka;

1.146.s:
bhṛgvaṅgiraḥkṛtāścaiva saurā hārītakāstathā ..
śrībhagavānuvāca ..
śṛṇu rājanmahābāho dharmātmankurunandana ..1.146.40..
1.146.d:
भृग्वङ्गिरःकृताश्चैव सौरा हारीतकास्तथा ॥
श्रीभगवानुवाच ॥
शृणु राजन्महाबाहो धर्मात्मन्कुरुनन्दन ॥1.146.40॥
1.146.m: and those composed by Bhṛgu and Aṅgiras, those belonging to Sūrya, and those of Hārīta— / The Blessed Lord said: / Listen, O king, O mighty-armed one, O righteous-minded scion of Kuru.

1.146.s:
dharmavṛddhikaraṃ vacmi vṛṣabhasya tu lakṣaṇam ..
ṛṣabhaḥ sa samudrākhyaḥ satataṃ kulavardhanaḥ .. 41 ..
1.146.d:
धर्मवृद्धिकरं वच्मि वृषभस्य तु लक्षणम् ॥
ऋषभः स समुद्राख्यः सततं कुलवर्धनः ॥ 41 ॥
1.146.m: I declare the characteristics of a bull, which cause dharma to increase. / That bull known as Samudra always makes a family prosper.

1.146.s:
mallikāpuṣpacitraśca dhanyo bhavati puṅgavaḥ ..
kāmalairmāṇḍalaiścāpi citro bhavati bhogadaḥ .. 42 ..
1.146.d:
मल्लिकापुष्पचित्रश्च धन्यो भवति पुङ्गवः ॥
कामलैर्माण्डलैश्चापि चित्रो भवति भोगदः ॥ 42 ॥
1.146.m: And an excellent bull variegated like the jasmine flower is auspicious; / and one variegated with pleasant circular spots brings enjoyment.

1.146.s:
atasīpuṣpavarṇaśca tathā dhanyataraḥ smṛtaḥ ..
ete dhanyāstathā dhanyānkīrtayiṣyāmi te nṛpa .. 43 ..
1.146.d:
अतसीपुष्पवर्णश्च तथा धन्यतरः स्मृतः ॥
एते धन्यास्तथा धन्यान्कीर्तयिष्यामि ते नृप ॥ 43 ॥
1.146.m: And one the color of the flax flower is likewise held to be more auspicious. / These are auspicious, and other auspicious ones I shall mention to you, O king.

1.146.s:
kṛṣṇatālvoṣṭha daśanā rūkṣaśṛṅgaśaphāśca ye ..
avyaktavarṇā hrasvāśca vyāghrabhasmanibhāśca ye .. 44 ..
1.146.d:
कृष्णताल्वोष्ठ दशना रूक्षशृङ्गशफाश्च ये ॥
अव्यक्तवर्णा ह्रस्वाश्च व्याघ्रभस्मनिभाश्च ये ॥ 44 ॥
1.146.m: Those with black palate, lips, and teeth, and rough horns and hooves; / and those of indistinct color, and dwarfish, and resembling a tiger or ashes;

1.146.s:
dhvāṅkṣagṛdhrasavarṇāśca tathā mūṣakasannibhāḥ ..
kubjāḥ kāṇāstathā khañjāḥ kekarākṣāstathaiva ca .. 45 ..
1.146.d:
ध्वाङ्क्षगृध्रसवर्णाश्च तथा मूषकसन्निभाः ॥
कुब्जाः काणास्तथा खञ्जाः केकराक्षास्तथैव च ॥ 45 ॥
1.146.m: and those having the color of a crow or a vulture, and likewise resembling a mouse; / the hunchbacked, the one-eyed, and the lame, and likewise the squint-eyed;

1.146.s:
viṣamaśvetapādāśca udbhrāntanayanastathā ..
na te vṛṣāḥ proktavyā na ca dhāryāstathā gṛhe .. 46 ..
1.146.d:
विषमश्वेतपादाश्च उद्भ्रान्तनयनस्तथा ॥
न ते वृषाः प्रोक्तव्या न च धार्यास्तथा गृहे ॥ 46 ॥
1.146.m: and those with unevenly white feet, and with rolling eyes— / those bulls are not to be set free, nor should they be kept in the home.

1.146.s: moktavyānāṃ ca dhāryāṇāṃ bhūyo vakṣyāmi lakṣaṇam .. 47 ..
1.146.d: मोक्तव्यानां च धार्याणां भूयो वक्ष्यामि लक्षणम् ॥ 47 ॥
1.146.m: And the characteristics of those to be set free and to be kept, I shall declare further.

1.146.s:
svastikākāraśṛṅgāśca meghaughasadṛśasvanāḥ ..
mahāpramāṇāśca tathā mattamātaṅgagāminaḥ .. .. 48 ..
1.146.d:
स्वस्तिकाकारशृङ्गाश्च मेघौघसदृशस्वनाः ॥
महाप्रमाणाश्च तथा मत्तमातङ्गगामिनः ॥ ॥ 48 ॥
1.146.m: Those with horns shaped like a svastika, and sounds resembling a mass of clouds; / and of large proportions, and walking like an intoxicated elephant;

1.146.s:
mahoraskā mahocchvāsā mahābalaparākramāḥ ..
śiraḥ karṇau lalāṭaṃ ca vāladhiścaraṇāni ca .. 49 ..
1.146.d:
महोरस्का महोच्छ्वासा महाबलपराक्रमाः ॥
शिरः कर्णौ ललाटं च वालधिश्चरणानि च ॥ 49 ॥
1.146.m: broad-chested, drawing deep breaths, possessing great strength and valor; / the head, the ears, the forehead, the tail, and the feet,

1.146.s:
netrapārśve ca kṛṣṇāni śasyante candramastviṣaḥ ..
cihnānyetāni śasyante kṛṣṇasya tu viśeṣataḥ .. 1.146.50 ..
1.146.d:
नेत्रपार्श्वे च कृष्णानि शस्यन्ते चन्द्रमस्त्विषः ॥
चिह्नान्येतानि शस्यन्ते कृष्णस्य तु विशेषतः ॥ 1.146.50 ॥
1.146.m: and the corners of the eyes [being] black, are praised in one who has the luster of the moon; / and these marks are praised especially in a black one.

1.146.s:
bhūmiṃ karṣati lāṃgūlātpraśastaḥ sthūlavāladhiḥ ..
purastānna tathā nīco vṛṣabhaśca praśasyate .. 51 ..
1.146.d:
भूमिं कर्षति लांगूलात्प्रशस्तः स्थूलवालधिः ॥
पुरस्तान्न तथा नीचो वृषभश्च प्रशस्यते ॥ 51 ॥
1.146.m: A bull whose thick tail drags along the ground by its tip is praised; / and a bull that is not low in the front is praised.

1.146.s:
śaktidhvajapatākābhā yeṣāṃ rājirvirājate ..
anaḍvāhastu te dhanyā ṛddhisiddhijayāvahāḥ .. 52 ..
1.146.d:
शक्तिध्वजपताकाभा येषां राजिर्विराजते ॥
अनड्वाहस्तु ते धन्या ऋद्धिसिद्धिजयावहाः ॥ 52 ॥
1.146.m: Those on whom a streak shines resembling a spear, a banner, or a flag— / those oxen are auspicious, bringing prosperity, perfection, and victory.

1.146.s:
pradakṣiṇaṃ nivartante svayaṃ ye vinivartitāḥ ..
samunnataśirogrīvā dhanyāste kośavardhanāḥ .. 53 ..
1.146.d:
प्रदक्षिणं निवर्तन्ते स्वयं ये विनिवर्तिताः ॥
समुन्नतशिरोग्रीवा धन्यास्ते कोशवर्धनाः ॥ 53 ॥
1.146.m: Those who, when turned around, turn of their own accord to the right, / with raised head and neck, are auspicious, increasing the treasury.

1.146.s:
raktaśṛṅgāgranayanāḥ śvetavarṇā bhavantyapi ..
śaphaiḥ pravālasadṛśairnāsti dhanyatarastataḥ .. 54 ..
1.146.d:
रक्तशृङ्गाग्रनयनाः श्वेतवर्णा भवन्त्यपि ॥
शफैः प्रवालसदृशैर्नास्ति धन्यतरस्ततः ॥ 54 ॥
1.146.m: Those with red tips of horns and eyes, even if white in color, / with hooves resembling coral—there is none more auspicious than that.

1.146.s:
ete dhanyāḥ prayatnena moktavyā yadi vā vṛṣāḥ ..
dhāritāśca tathā muktā dhanadhānyavivardhanāḥ .. 55 ..
1.146.d:
एते धन्याः प्रयत्नेन मोक्तव्या यदि वा वृषाः ॥
धारिताश्च तथा मुक्ता धनधान्यविवर्धनाः ॥ 55 ॥
1.146.m: These auspicious bulls should be set free with effort, or, / if kept or set free, they increase wealth and grain.

1.146.s:
caraṇāni mukhaṃ pucchaṃ yasya śvetāni gopateḥ ..
lākṣārasasavarṇaśca taṃ nīlamiti nirdiśet .. 56..
1.146.d:
चरणानि मुखं पुच्छं यस्य श्वेतानि गोपतेः ॥
लाक्षारससवर्णश्च तं नीलमिति निर्दिशेत् ॥ 56॥
1.146.m: That lord of cattle whose feet, face, and tail are white, / and who has the color of lac-juice, one should designate as 'blue'.

1.146.s:
vṛṣa eva sa moktavyo na sandhāryo gṛhe bhavet ..
yadarthameṣā carati gāthā loke purātanī .. 57 ..
1.146.d:
वृष एव स मोक्तव्यो न सन्धार्यो गृहे भवेत् ॥
यदर्थमेषा चरति गाथा लोके पुरातनी ॥ 57 ॥
1.146.m: That very bull is to be set free; he should not be kept in the house, / for which purpose this ancient verse is current in the world:

1.146.s:
eṣṭavyā bahavaḥ putrā yadyeko'pi gayāṃ vrajet ..
yajeta vāśvamedhena nīlaṃ vā vṛṣamutsṛjeta ..58..
1.146.d:
एष्टव्या बहवः पुत्रा यद्येकोऽपि गयां व्रजेत् ॥
यजेत वाश्वमेधेन नीलं वा वृषमुत्सृजेत ॥58॥
1.146.m: "Many sons are to be desired, in case even one goes to Gayā, / or performs a horse sacrifice, or sets free a dark bull."

1.146.s:
evaṃ vṛṣaṃ lakṣaṇasaṃprayuktaṃ gṛhodbhavaṃ krītamathāpi rājan ..
muktvā na śocenmaraṇaṃ mahātmā mokṣe vidhiṃ cāhamato vidhāsye .. 59 ..
1.146.d:
एवं वृषं लक्षणसंप्रयुक्तं गृहोद्भवं क्रीतमथापि राजन् ॥
मुक्त्वा न शोचेन्मरणं महात्मा मोक्षे विधिं चाहमतो विधास्ये ॥ 59 ॥
1.146.m: Having set free such a bull endowed with [auspicious] marks, whether born in his own house or purchased, O king, / a high-souled man does not grieve over death; and I shall now explain the rite for its release.

1.146.s: iti śrīviṣṇudharmottare prathamakhaṇḍe mārkaṇḍeyavajrasaṃvāde vṛṣalakṣaṇavarṇano nāma ṣaṭcatvāriṃśaduttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. .. 146 ..
1.146.d: इति श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे प्रथमखण्डे मार्कण्डेयवज्रसंवादे वृषलक्षणवर्णनो नाम षट्चत्वारिंशदुत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ॥ ॥ 146 ॥
1.146.m: Thus ends the one hundred and forty-sixth chapter, named "Description of the Marks of a Bull," in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the first book of the venerable Viṣṇudharmottara.

1.147.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
āśvayuk kṛṣṇapakṣasya pañcadaśyāṃ narādhipa ..
kārtikepyathavā māsi vṛṣotsargaṃ tu kārayet .. 1 ..
1.147.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
आश्वयुक् कृष्णपक्षस्य पञ्चदश्यां नराधिप ॥
कार्तिकेप्यथवा मासि वृषोत्सर्गं तु कारयेत् ॥ 1 ॥
1.147.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / On the fifteenth [tithi] of the dark fortnight of Āśvayuja, O lord of men, / or in the month of Kārttika, one should perform the setting free of a bull.

1.147.s:
grahaṇe dve mahāpuṇye tathā caivāyanadvayam ..
viṣuvaddvitayaṃ caiva mṛtāho bāndhavasya ca .. 2..
1.147.d:
ग्रहणे द्वे महापुण्ये तथा चैवायनद्वयम् ॥
विषुवद्द्वितयं चैव मृताहो बान्धवस्य च ॥ 2॥
1.147.m: At the two very holy eclipses, and likewise at the two solstices, / at the two equinoxes, and on the anniversary of the death of a relative,

1.147.s:
mṛtāho yasya tasyārthe tasminnahani śaṅkaram ..
susamiddhe gavāṃ madhye paristīrya hutāśanam .. 3 ..
1.147.d:
मृताहो यस्य तस्यार्थे तस्मिन्नहनि शङ्करम् ॥
सुसमिद्धे गवां मध्ये परिस्तीर्य हुताशनम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.147.m: for the sake of the one whose day of death it is, on that day, [one performs the rite] to Śaṅkara. / Having enclosed the sacrificial fire around, well kindled, in the midst of the cattle,

1.147.s:
payasā śrapayedvidvām̐ścaruṃ pauṣṇaṃ samāhitaḥ ..
pūṣā gā anvetu naśca pūṣṇe hutvā narādhipa .. 4 ..
1.147.d:
पयसा श्रपयेद्विद्वाम्̐श्चरुं पौष्णं समाहितः ॥
पूषा गा अन्वेतु नश्च पूष्णे हुत्वा नराधिप ॥ 4 ॥
1.147.m: a wise man, collected in mind, should cook a caru dedicated to Pūṣan with milk. / Having sacrificed to Pūṣan with "May Pūṣan follow our cows," O lord of men,

1.147.s:
iha rāḍiti hutvā ca japedrudrānsamāhitaḥ ..
tathaiva pauruṣaṃ sūktaṃ kūṣmāṇḍāni narādhipa .. 5 ..
1.147.d:
इह राडिति हुत्वा च जपेद्रुद्रान्समाहितः ॥
तथैव पौरुषं सूक्तं कूष्माण्डानि नराधिप ॥ 5 ॥
1.147.m: and having sacrificed with "May he rule here," collected in mind, he should recite the Rudra [hymns], / and likewise the Pauruṣasūkta and the Kūṣmāṇḍa [mantras], O lord of men.

1.147.s:
tataḥ koṣṇena vṛṣabhamayaskāraḥ suśilpavān ..
śūlena dakṣiṇe pārśve vāme cakreṇa nirdahet .. 6 ..
1.147.d:
ततः कोष्णेन वृषभमयस्कारः सुशिल्पवान् ॥
शूलेन दक्षिणे पार्श्वे वामे चक्रेण निर्दहेत् ॥ 6 ॥
1.147.m: Then, with lukewarm [irons], a skilled blacksmith / should brand the bull on its right flank with a trident and on its left with a discus.

1.147.s:
aṅkitaṃ snāpayetpaścātsnāne tasya tathā paṭhet ..
hiraṇyavarṇeti ṛcaścatasro manujeśvara .. 7 ..
1.147.d:
अङ्कितं स्नापयेत्पश्चात्स्नाने तस्य तथा पठेत् ॥
हिरण्यवर्णेति ऋचश्चतस्रो मनुजेश्वर ॥ 7 ॥
1.147.m: Once it is marked, he should then bathe it; and at its bathing he should recite, / O ruler of men, the four verses beginning with "Golden-coloured,"

1.147.s:
āpo hi ṣṭheti tisraśca śanno devīti cāpyatha.
vatsataryaścatasraśca taṃ vṛṣaṃ ca narādhipa..8..
1.147.d:
आपो हि ष्ठेति तिस्रश्च शन्नो देवीति चाप्यथ।
वत्सतर्यश्चतस्रश्च तं वृषं च नराधिप॥8॥
1.147.m: the three verses beginning with "You waters are indeed," and then "May the divine [waters] bring us bliss." / Four heifers and that bull, O lord of men,

1.147.s:
alaṅkuryāttataḥ paścādgandhamālyaiśca śaktitaḥ..
kiṅkiṇībhiśca ramyābhistathā cīnāṃśukaiḥ śubhaḥ .. 9 ..
1.147.d:
अलङ्कुर्यात्ततः पश्चाद्गन्धमाल्यैश्च शक्तितः॥
किङ्किणीभिश्च रम्याभिस्तथा चीनांशुकैः शुभः ॥ 9 ॥
1.147.m: he should then decorate, according to his means, with perfumes and garlands, / with delightful little bells, and with splendid Chinese silks.

1.147.s:
tataḥ kartā japenmantramimaṃ prayatamānasaḥ ..
vṛṣo hi bhagavāndharmaścatuṣpādaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ..
vṛṇomi tamahaṃ bhaktyā sa me rakṣatu sarvataḥ ..1.147.10 ..
1.147.d:
ततः कर्ता जपेन्मन्त्रमिमं प्रयतमानसः ॥
वृषो हि भगवान्धर्मश्चतुष्पादः प्रकीर्तितः ॥
वृणोमि तमहं भक्त्या स मे रक्षतु सर्वतः ॥1.147.10 ॥
1.147.m: Then the sacrificer, with a purified mind, should recite this mantra: / "For the bull is the four-footed Lord Dharma, as is proclaimed; / with devotion I choose him; may he protect me on all sides."

1.147.s:
evaṃ yuvānaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ dadāmi gavāṃ patiṃ yūthapatiṃ sadharmam ..
anena sārdhaṃ carata prakāmaṃ yathā tathā prāpnuta vatsataryaḥ .. .. 11 ..
1.147.d:
एवं युवानं वृषभं ददामि गवां पतिं यूथपतिं सधर्मम् ॥
अनेन सार्धं चरत प्रकामं यथा तथा प्राप्नुत वत्सतर्यः ॥ ॥ 11 ॥
1.147.m: "Thus do I grant this young bull, lord of cows, leader of the herd, possessing dharma. / Roam at will along with him, O heifers; attain [your desires] in every way."

1.147.s:
evaṃ yuvānaṃ gopatiṃ vo dadāmi anena krīḍantīścaratīḥ priyeṇa ..
sahāsmābhiḥ prajayā mā tanūbhirmā vadhāma dviṣataṃ somarājan .. 12..
1.147.d:
एवं युवानं गोपतिं वो ददामि अनेन क्रीडन्तीश्चरतीः प्रियेण ॥
सहास्माभिः प्रजया मा तनूभिर्मा वधाम द्विषतं सोमराजन् ॥ 12॥
1.147.m: "Thus do I give you this young lord of cows. Frolicking with this beloved, roam about. / Together with us, with [our] offspring, and with [our] bodies, let us not destroy an enemy, O King Soma."

1.147.s:
mantraṃ pitā vatsa iti pratītaṃ japeta karṇe vṛṣabhasya savye ..
pracālayettaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ tatastu pūrvāṃ diśaṃ vatsataryaśca sarvāḥ ..13..
1.147.d:
मन्त्रं पिता वत्स इति प्रतीतं जपेत कर्णे वृषभस्य सव्ये ॥
प्रचालयेत्तं वृषभं ततस्तु पूर्वां दिशं वत्सतर्यश्च सर्वाः ॥13॥
1.147.m: He should recite the well-known mantra "Father, calf..." in the right ear of the bull. / Then he should drive that bull and all the heifers toward the eastern direction.

1.147.s:
vāsoyugaṃ grahīturatha pradeyaṃ suvarṇayuktaṃ saghṛtaṃ ca kāṃsyam ..
śilpapradhānasya tathaiva satyaṃ deyaṃ yathā tuṣṭimupaiti rājan .. 14 ..
1.147.d:
वासोयुगं ग्रहीतुरथ प्रदेयं सुवर्णयुक्तं सघृतं च कांस्यम् ॥
शिल्पप्रधानस्य तथैव सत्यं देयं यथा तुष्टिमुपैति राजन् ॥ 14 ॥
1.147.m: A pair of garments is then to be given to the recipient, along with a bronze vessel containing gold and clarified butter; / and likewise, O king, a proper [fee] is to be given to the master artisan so that he is satisfied.

1.147.s:
viprāstathānnaṃ dadhisarpiṣā yutaṃ saṃbhojanīyāḥ payasā ca miśram ..
utsṛṣṭamātre vṛṣabhe vrajanti tṛptiṃ parāṃ tasya pitāmahā ye .. 15 ..
1.147.d:
विप्रास्तथान्नं दधिसर्पिषा युतं संभोजनीयाः पयसा च मिश्रम् ॥
उत्सृष्टमात्रे वृषभे व्रजन्ति तृप्तिं परां तस्य पितामहा ये ॥ 15 ॥
1.147.m: Likewise, brahmins are to be fed with food mixed with curds and clarified butter, and blended with milk. / The moment the bull is set free, his ancestors attain supreme satisfaction.

1.147.s:
yasmim̐staḍāge sa jalaṃ tṛṣārtaḥ pātuṃ samāgacchati tatpitṝṇām ..
divyāmbupūrṇaṃ kalaśaṃ mahīpate lokaṃ paraṃ tṛptimantaḥ prayānti.. 16 ..
1.147.d:
यस्मिम्̐स्तडागे स जलं तृषार्तः पातुं समागच्छति तत्पितॄणाम् ॥
दिव्याम्बुपूर्णं कलशं महीपते लोकं परं तृप्तिमन्तः प्रयान्ति॥ 16 ॥
1.147.m: In whatever pond he comes to drink water when afflicted with thirst, / a jar filled with celestial water [is provided] for his ancestors, O king, and satisfied, they attain the higher world.

1.147.s:
saridvarāṃ kāñcidathopayāti tṛṣṇānvitastasya pitāmahānām ..
tṛptiṃ vidhatte saritāṃ variṣṭhā sudīrghakālaṃ vimalāmbuvāhaiḥ .. 17 ..
1.147.d:
सरिद्वरां काञ्चिदथोपयाति तृष्णान्वितस्तस्य पितामहानाम् ॥
तृप्तिं विधत्ते सरितां वरिष्ठा सुदीर्घकालं विमलाम्बुवाहैः ॥ 17 ॥
1.147.m: Or if, overcome with thirst, he approaches an excellent river, / that foremost of rivers brings satisfaction to his ancestors for a very long time with its streams of pure water.

1.147.s:
darpeṇa pūrṇaḥ saviṣāṇaghātairdharāṃ yadā dhārayate narendra ..
pitṝṃstadā tasya tadannakūṭaṃ dhruvaṃ sa yātīti na saṃśayo'tra .. 18 ..
1.147.d:
दर्पेण पूर्णः सविषाणघातैर्धरां यदा धारयते नरेन्द्र ॥
पितॄंस्तदा तस्य तदन्नकूटं ध्रुवं स यातीति न संशयोऽत्र ॥ 18 ॥
1.147.m: When, full of pride, he tears up the earth with blows from his horns, O ruler of men, / then that [earth] becomes a heap of food for his ancestors; he surely goes [to heaven], there is no doubt of this.

1.147.s:
romṇāṃ ca tulyāni śatāni rājanbhoktā tathā tasya divaṃ prayāti ..
saṃvatsarāṇāṃ paripūrṇakāmaḥ saṃsevyamānastridaśāṅganābhiḥ .. 19 ..
sāmavedīya vṛṣotsargavidhiḥ
1.147.d:
रोम्णां च तुल्यानि शतानि राजन्भोक्ता तथा तस्य दिवं प्रयाति ॥
संवत्सराणां परिपूर्णकामः संसेव्यमानस्त्रिदशाङ्गनाभिः ॥ 19 ॥
सामवेदीय वृषोत्सर्गविधिः
1.147.m:
And for hundreds of years equal to [the number of] its hairs, O king, the agent goes to heaven, / his desires fulfilled, being attended upon by the celestial women.
The Rite of Setting Free a Bull According to the Sāmaveda.

1.148.s:
.. vajra uvāca ..
caritaṃ budhaputrasya mārkaṇḍeya mayā śrutam ..
śrutaḥ śrāddhavidhiḥ puṇyaḥ sarvapāpapraṇāśanaḥ .. 1 ..
1.148.d:
॥ वज्र उवाच ॥
चरितं बुधपुत्रस्य मार्कण्डेय मया श्रुतम् ॥
श्रुतः श्राद्धविधिः पुण्यः सर्वपापप्रणाशनः ॥ 1 ॥
1.148.m: Vajra said: / The life of the son of Budha has been heard by me, O Mārkaṇḍeya; / the sacred rite of śrāddha, which destroys all sins, has been heard.

1.148.s:
dhenvāḥ prasūyamānāyāḥ phalaṃ dāne tathā śrutam ..
kṛṣṇājinapradānaṃ ca vṛṣotsargastathaiva ca .. 2 ..
1.148.d:
धेन्वाः प्रसूयमानायाः फलं दाने तथा श्रुतम् ॥
कृष्णाजिनप्रदानं च वृषोत्सर्गस्तथैव च ॥ 2 ॥
1.148.m: Likewise, the fruit of giving a cow in the act of calving has been heard, / as well as the gift of a black antelope skin and the setting free of a bull.

1.148.s:
śrutvā rūpaṃ narendrasya budhaputrasya bhārgava ..
kautūhalaṃ samutpannaṃ tanmamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ .. 3 ..
1.148.d:
श्रुत्वा रूपं नरेन्द्रस्य बुधपुत्रस्य भार्गव ॥
कौतूहलं समुत्पन्नं तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः ॥ 3 ॥
1.148.m: Having heard of the beauty of the ruler of men, the son of Budha, O Bhārgava, / curiosity has arisen; tell me, as I ask.

1.148.s:
kena karmavipākena sa tu rājā purūravāḥ ..
avāpa tādṛśaṃ rūpaṃ saubhāgyamapi cottamam .. 4 ..
1.148.d:
केन कर्मविपाकेन स तु राजा पुरूरवाः ॥
अवाप तादृशं रूपं सौभाग्यमपि चोत्तमम् ॥ 4 ॥
1.148.m: By what ripening of actions did that King Purūravas / attain such beauty, and also supreme good fortune,

1.148.s:
devāṃstribhuvana śreṣṭhāngandharvāṃśca manoramān ..
urvaśī saṃgatā tyaktvā sarvabhāvena taṃ nṛpam .. 5 ..
1.148.d:
देवांस्त्रिभुवन श्रेष्ठान्गन्धर्वांश्च मनोरमान् ॥
उर्वशी संगता त्यक्त्वा सर्वभावेन तं नृपम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.148.m: [such that] Urvaśī, leaving the gods who are the best in the three worlds and the charming gandharvas, / united with that king with her whole being?

1.148.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
śṛṇu karmavipākena yena rājā purūravāḥ ..
purūravā iti khyāto madreṣvāsīnmahīpatiḥ .. 6 ..
1.148.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
शृणु कर्मविपाकेन येन राजा पुरूरवाः ॥
पुरूरवा इति ख्यातो मद्रेष्वासीन्महीपतिः ॥ 6 ॥
1.148.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Hear by what ripening of actions King Purūravas / was [first] a ruler of the earth renowned as Purūravas among the Madras.

1.148.s:
cāśuṣasyānvaye jātaścākṣuṣasyāntare manoḥ ..
sarvairnṛpaguṇairyuktaḥ kevalaṃ rūpa varjitaḥ .. 7 ..
1.148.d:
चाशुषस्यान्वये जातश्चाक्षुषस्यान्तरे मनोः ॥
सर्वैर्नृपगुणैर्युक्तः केवलं रूप वर्जितः ॥ 7 ॥
1.148.m: He was born in the lineage of Cākṣuṣa during the interval of the Manu Cākṣuṣa, / endowed with all the virtues of a king, but lacking only beauty.

1.148.s:
vajra uvāca ..
purūravā madrapatiḥ karmaṇā kena bhārgava ..
babhūva karmaṇā kena kurūpaśca tathā dvija .. 8 ..
1.148.d:
वज्र उवाच ॥
पुरूरवा मद्रपतिः कर्मणा केन भार्गव ॥
बभूव कर्मणा केन कुरूपश्च तथा द्विज ॥ 8 ॥
1.148.m: Vajra said: / By what action, O Bhārgava, did he become Purūravas, the ruler of the Madras? / And by what action did he become ugly, O twice-born?

1.148.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
dvijagrāme dvijaśreṣṭho nāmnaivā''sītpurūravāḥ ..
nadyāḥ kūle mahārāja pūrvajanmani pārthivaḥ .. 9 ..
1.148.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
द्विजग्रामे द्विजश्रेष्ठो नाम्नैवा'ऽसीत्पुरूरवाः ॥
नद्याः कूले महाराज पूर्वजन्मनि पार्थिवः ॥ 9 ॥
1.148.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / In a village of twice-born [people], he was an eminent twice-born named Purūravas / on the bank of a river, O great king, [before he became] a monarch in his previous birth.

1.148.s:
sa tu madrapatirnāmnā yo'bhūdrājā purūravāḥ ..
asmiñjanmanyasau vipro dvādaśīṣu sadānagha .. 1.148.10 ..
1.148.d:
स तु मद्रपतिर्नाम्ना योऽभूद्राजा पुरूरवाः ॥
अस्मिञ्जन्मन्यसौ विप्रो द्वादशीषु सदानघ ॥ 1.148.10 ॥
1.148.m: He who became the ruler of the Madras, King Purūravas by name, / in that birth, as a brahmin, constantly on the twelfth [tithis], O sinless one,

1.148.s:
upoṣya pūjayāmāsa rājyakāmo janārdanam ..
cakāra sopavāsaṃ ca snānamabhyaṅgapūrvakam .. 11 ..
1.148.d:
उपोष्य पूजयामास राज्यकामो जनार्दनम् ॥
चकार सोपवासं च स्नानमभ्यङ्गपूर्वकम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.148.m: fasted and worshipped Janārdana, desiring kingship; / and while fasting, he took a bath preceded by an oil massage.
Having obtained kingship free from thorns among the Madras as the fruit of his fasting, / because of the oil massage while fasting he was then born devoid of beauty.

1.148.s:
upoṣito narastasmātsnānamabhyaṅgapūrvakam ..
varjayettatprayatnena rūpaghnaṃ tatparaṃ nṛṇām .. 13 ..
1.148.d:
उपोषितो नरस्तस्मात्स्नानमभ्यङ्गपूर्वकम् ॥
वर्जयेत्तत्प्रयत्नेन रूपघ्नं तत्परं नृणाम् ॥ 13 ॥
1.148.m: Therefore, a person who is fasting should carefully avoid / a bath preceded by an oil massage; for humans, it is an absolute destroyer of beauty.

1.148.s:
etatte kathitaṃ tasya yadvṛttaṃ pūrvajanmani ..
madreśvaratve caritaṃ śṛṇu tasya mahīpateḥ .. 14 ..
1.148.d:
एतत्ते कथितं तस्य यद्वृत्तं पूर्वजन्मनि ॥
मद्रेश्वरत्वे चरितं शृणु तस्य महीपतेः ॥ 14 ॥
1.148.m: This has been told to you regarding what happened in his previous birth. / Hear the deeds of that ruler of the earth in his status as the lord of the Madras.

1.148.s:
tasya rājaguṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ samupetasya pārthiva ..
janānurāgo naivāsīdrūpahīnasya yādava .. 15 ..
1.148.d:
तस्य राजगुणैः सर्वैः समुपेतस्य पार्थिव ॥
जनानुरागो नैवासीद्रूपहीनस्य यादव ॥ 15 ॥
1.148.m: Though he was endowed with all the virtues of a king, O ruler of the earth, / because he was devoid of beauty, there was no affection from the people, O Yādava.

1.148.s:
rūpakāmaḥ sa madreśastapase kṛtaniścayaḥ ..
rājyaṃ mantrigataṃ kṛtvā jagāma himaparvatam .. 16 ..
1.148.d:
रूपकामः स मद्रेशस्तपसे कृतनिश्चयः ॥
राज्यं मन्त्रिगतं कृत्वा जगाम हिमपर्वतम् ॥ 16 ॥
1.148.m: Desiring beauty, that lord of the Madras, having resolved upon austerity, / placed his kingdom in the hands of his ministers and went to the Snow Mountain.

1.148.s:
vyavasāyadvitīyastu padbhyāmeva mahāyaśāḥ ..
ūrdhvaṃ saṃtīrya sa nadaṃ viṣayānte svakīṃ nadīm ..
irāvatīmiti khyātāṃ dadarśātimanoharām .. 17 ..
1.148.d:
व्यवसायद्वितीयस्तु पद्भ्यामेव महायशाः ॥
ऊर्ध्वं संतीर्य स नदं विषयान्ते स्वकीं नदीम् ॥
इरावतीमिति ख्यातां ददर्शातिमनोहराम् ॥ 17 ॥
1.148.m: With resolve alone as his companion, on foot, the highly renowned [king], / having crossed higher up the river at the border of his realm, saw his own river, / renowned as the Irāvatī, exceedingly charming.

1.148.s:
tuhinagiribhavāṃ mahoghavegāṃ tuhinasagarbhasamānaśītalodām ..
tuhinasadṛśavarṇaphenayuktāṃ tuhinayaśāḥ saritaṃ dadarśa rājā .. 18 ..
1.148.d:
तुहिनगिरिभवां महोघवेगां तुहिनसगर्भसमानशीतलोदाम् ॥
तुहिनसदृशवर्णफेनयुक्तां तुहिनयशाः सरितं ददर्श राजा ॥ 18 ॥
1.148.m: Born of the snowy mountains, with a great, swift current, possessing waters as cold as the womb of ice, / bearing foam colored like snow, the king, whose fame was like snow, beheld the river.

1.149.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
sa dadarśa nadīṃ puṇyāṃ ramyāṃ haimavatīṃ śubhām ..
gandharvagaṇasaṃkīrṇāṃ nityaṃ śakreṇa sevitām .. 1 ..
1.149.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
स ददर्श नदीं पुण्यां रम्यां हैमवतीं शुभाम् ॥
गन्धर्वगणसंकीर्णां नित्यं शक्रेण सेविताम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.149.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / He saw the auspicious, lovely, blessed river born of the Himalayas, / thronged by hosts of Gandharvas, and constantly attended by Śakra,

1.149.s:
surebhamadasiṃdūrairyasyāṃ rājirvirājate ..
madhyena śakracāpābhā tasyāṃ majjati sarvadā .. 2 ..
1.149.d:
सुरेभमदसिंदूरैर्यस्यां राजिर्विराजते ॥
मध्येन शक्रचापाभा तस्यां मज्जति सर्वदा ॥ 2 ॥
1.149.m: in which a streak shines forth from the vermilion and rut of celestial elephants, / resembling Śakra's rainbow along the middle, where he constantly bathes.

1.149.s:
tapasviśaraṇāyātāṃ mukhyabrāhmaṇasevitām ..
dadarśa śītapānīyāṃ mahārājaḥ purūravāḥ .. 3 ..
1.149.d:
तपस्विशरणायातां मुख्यब्राह्मणसेविताम् ॥
ददर्श शीतपानीयां महाराजः पुरूरवाः ॥ 3 ॥
1.149.m: A refuge to ascetics, frequented by prominent brahmins, / endowed with cool waters, the great king Purūravas beheld [her],

1.149.s:
plutahaṃsāvalīchannāṃ kāśacāmaravījitām ..
sābhiṣekāmiva sa tāṃ paśyanprītiṃ parāṃ yayau .. 4 ..
1.149.d:
प्लुतहंसावलीछन्नां काशचामरवीजिताम् ॥
साभिषेकामिव स तां पश्यन्प्रीतिं परां ययौ ॥ 4 ॥
1.149.m: covered by flocks of swimming swans, fanned by kāśa reeds as if by chowries; / seeing her, as if consecrated [for coronation], he attained supreme delight.

1.149.s:
puṇyāṃ suśītalāṃ hṛdyāṃ manasaḥ prītivardhinīm ..
kṣayavṛddhiyutāṃ saumyāṃ somamūrtimivāparām .. 5 ..
1.149.d:
पुण्यां सुशीतलां हृद्यां मनसः प्रीतिवर्धिनीम् ॥
क्षयवृद्धियुतां सौम्यां सोममूर्तिमिवापराम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.149.m: Sacred, very cool, delightful, increasing the pleasure of the mind, / subject to decrease and increase, gentle like a second form of the moon;

1.149.s:
suśītaśīghrapānīyāṃ dvijapuñjaniṣevitām ..
sutāṃ himavataḥ śreṣṭhāṃ cañcadvīcivirājitām .. 6 ..
1.149.d:
सुशीतशीघ्रपानीयां द्विजपुञ्जनिषेविताम् ॥
सुतां हिमवतः श्रेष्ठां चञ्चद्वीचिविराजिताम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.149.m: possessing very cool and swift waters, attended by flocks of birds, / the excellent daughter of the Himalayas, adorned with shimmering waves;

1.149.s:
amṛtasvādusalilāṃ tāpasairupaśobhitām ..
svargārohaṇaniḥśreṇīṃ sarvakalmaṣanāśinīm .. 7 ..
1.149.d:
अमृतस्वादुसलिलां तापसैरुपशोभिताम् ॥
स्वर्गारोहणनिःश्रेणीं सर्वकल्मषनाशिनीम् ॥ 7 ॥
1.149.m: having waters sweet as nectar, graced by ascetics, / a ladder for ascending to heaven, destroying all sins;

1.149.s:
agryāṃ samudramahiṣīṃ mahiṣīgaṇagāhitām ..
hitāṃ sarvasya lokasya kasya nautsukyakāriṇīm .. 8 ..
1.149.d:
अग्र्यां समुद्रमहिषीं महिषीगणगाहिताम् ॥
हितां सर्वस्य लोकस्य कस्य नौत्सुक्यकारिणीम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.149.m: the foremost queen of the ocean, plunged into by herds of female buffaloes, / beneficial to all the world—whom would she not fill with longing?

1.149.s:
gokulākulatīrāṃ tāṃ ramyāṃ śaivālavarjitām ..
haṃsasārasasaṃghuṣṭairjalajaiḥ sevitāṃ śubhaiḥ .. 9 ..
1.149.d:
गोकुलाकुलतीरां तां रम्यां शैवालवर्जिताम् ॥
हंससारससंघुष्टैर्जलजैः सेवितां शुभैः ॥ 9 ॥
1.149.m: Her banks crowded with herds of cows, charming, free of moss, / frequented by auspicious waterbirds resounding with swans and crane-birds;

1.149.s:
āvartanābhigambhīrāṃ dvīporujaghanasthalām ..
nīlanīrajanetrāṃ tāmutphullakamalānanām .. 1.149.10 ..
1.149.d:
आवर्तनाभिगम्भीरां द्वीपोरुजघनस्थलाम् ॥
नीलनीरजनेत्रां तामुत्फुल्लकमलाननाम् ॥ 1.149.10 ॥
1.149.m: deep in the navel of her whirlpools, with islands as her thighs and hips, / having blue lotuses for eyes, with an open lotus for her face;

1.149.s:
himābhaphenavasanāṃ cakravākādharāṃ śubhām ..
balākāpaṅktidaśanāṃ calanmatsyāvalibhruvam.. 11.. svajaloddhatamātaṅgaramyakumbhapayodharām ..
1.149.d:
हिमाभफेनवसनां चक्रवाकाधरां शुभाम् ॥
बलाकापङ्क्तिदशनां चलन्मत्स्यावलिभ्रुवम्॥ 11॥ स्वजलोद्धतमातङ्गरम्यकुम्भपयोधराम् ॥
1.149.m: having foam like snow for her garment, ruddy geese for her auspicious lips, / rows of herons for her teeth, lines of darting fish for her brows, / her breasts the lovely frontal globes of elephants plunging in her waters;

1.149.s: haṃsanūpurasaṃghuṣṭāṃ mṛṇālavalayāvalīm .. 12 ..
1.149.d: हंसनूपुरसंघुष्टां मृणालवलयावलीम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.149.m: resounding with swans for her anklets, with rows of lotus-fibers for her bracelets,

1.149.s:
yasyāṃ rūpamadonmattagandharvānugataḥ sadā ..
madhyāhnasamaye rājankrīḍatyapsarasāṃ gaṇaḥ .. 13 ..
1.149.d:
यस्यां रूपमदोन्मत्तगन्धर्वानुगतः सदा ॥
मध्याह्नसमये राजन्क्रीडत्यप्सरसां गणः ॥ 13 ॥
1.149.m: where, O king, accompanied by Gandharvas maddened by the pride of beauty, / the host of Apsarases plays at midday;

1.149.s:
tāmapsarovinirmuktānvahantī kusumāñśubhān ..
svatīradrumasaṃbhūtānnānāvarṇānsugandhinaḥ .. 14 ..
1.149.d:
तामप्सरोविनिर्मुक्तान्वहन्ती कुसुमाञ्शुभान् ॥
स्वतीरद्रुमसंभूतान्नानावर्णान्सुगन्धिनः ॥ 14 ॥
1.149.m: carrying auspicious, fragrant flowers of various colors, / discarded by the Apsarases or fallen from the trees on her banks;

1.149.s:
taraṅgaśatasaṃkrāntasūryamaṇḍaladurdaśam ..
surebhajanitāghātavapradvayavibhūṣitām .. 15 ..
1.149.d:
तरङ्गशतसंक्रान्तसूर्यमण्डलदुर्दशम् ॥
सुरेभजनिताघातवप्रद्वयविभूषिताम् ॥ 15 ॥
1.149.m: hard to look upon because of the sun's orb reflected in hundreds of waves, / adorned with both banks scarred by the blows struck by celestial elephants;

1.149.s:
śakrebhagaṇḍasalilairdevastrīkuca candanaiḥ ..
saṃyutaṃ salilaṃ yasyāḥ ṣaṭpadairupasevyate .. 16 ..
1.149.d:
शक्रेभगण्डसलिलैर्देवस्त्रीकुच चन्दनैः ॥
संयुतं सलिलं यस्याः षट्पदैरुपसेव्यते ॥ 16 ॥
1.149.m: whose water, combined with the rut-fluid of Śakra's elephant / and sandal from the breasts of divine women, is attended by bees;

1.149.s:
yasyāstīrabhavā vṛkṣāḥ sugandhikusumānvitāḥ ..
tathā prakṛṣṭabhramarā bhramaraiste nirākulāḥ .. 17 ..
1.149.d:
यस्यास्तीरभवा वृक्षाः सुगन्धिकुसुमान्विताः ॥
तथा प्रकृष्टभ्रमरा भ्रमरैस्ते निराकुलाः ॥ 17 ॥
1.149.m: whose trees growing on the banks are endowed with fragrant blossoms, / and, having many bees, are untroubled by those swarming bees;

1.149.s:
yasyāstīre ratiṃ yānti sadā kāmavaśānugāḥ ..
tapodhanāśca ṛṣayastathā devāḥ savāsavāḥ .. 18 ..
1.149.d:
यस्यास्तीरे रतिं यान्ति सदा कामवशानुगाः ॥
तपोधनाश्च ऋषयस्तथा देवाः सवासवाः ॥ 18 ॥
1.149.m: on whose bank those subject to the sway of desire always find delight, / as do rich ascetics, sages, and gods along with Indra;

1.149.s:
labhante yatplutāṅgāstu devebhyaḥ pratimānanāḥ ..
striyaśca nāke bahulāḥ padmendupratimānanāḥ .. 19 ..
1.149.d:
लभन्ते यत्प्लुताङ्गास्तु देवेभ्यः प्रतिमाननाः ॥
स्त्रियश्च नाके बहुलाः पद्मेन्दुप्रतिमाननाः ॥ 19 ॥
1.149.m: plunging their limbs in which, [men] obtain honors from the gods, / and in heaven, many women whose faces resemble lotuses and the moon;

1.149.s:
yā bibharti sadā toyaṃ devasaṃghairapīḍitam ..
pulindamṛgavṛndaiśca vyādhasaṃghairapīḍitam .. 1.149.20 ..
1.149.d:
या बिभर्ति सदा तोयं देवसंघैरपीडितम् ॥
पुलिन्दमृगवृन्दैश्च व्याधसंघैरपीडितम् ॥ 1.149.20 ॥
1.149.m: who always carries water unpolluted by hosts of gods, / and unpolluted by herds of Pulinda deer or bands of hunters;

1.149.s:
satāmarasapānīyāṃ satārāgaganāmalām ..
sa tāṃ paśyanyayau rājā satāmīpsitakāmadām .. 21..
1.149.d:
सतामरसपानीयां सतारागगनामलाम् ॥
स तां पश्यन्ययौ राजा सतामीप्सितकामदाम् ॥ 21॥
1.149.m: having water filled with red lotuses, pure as the sky filled with stars— / beholding her, who grants the desires wished by the virtuous, the king went on.

1.149.s:
yasyāstīraruhaiḥ kāśaiḥ phullaiścandrāṃśusannibhaiḥ ..
rājadbhirvivṛtākāśai ramyaistatkṣīrasaṃsthitaiḥ ..22..
1.149.d:
यस्यास्तीररुहैः काशैः फुल्लैश्चन्द्रांशुसन्निभैः ॥
राजद्भिर्विवृताकाशै रम्यैस्तत्क्षीरसंस्थितैः ॥22॥
1.149.m: By the blooming kāśa reeds growing on her banks, resembling rays of the moon, / shining, covering the open sky, charming, and standing in her milk-like [waters],

1.149.s:
yā ca sadā divi sevyati devairyā ca sadā bhuvi sevyati vipraiḥ ..
yā ca sadā sakalāghavināśaṃ bhaktajanasya karotyacireṇa ..23..
1.149.d:
या च सदा दिवि सेव्यति देवैर्या च सदा भुवि सेव्यति विप्रैः ॥
या च सदा सकलाघविनाशं भक्तजनस्य करोत्यचिरेण ॥23॥
1.149.m: she who is always attended in heaven by the gods, and always on earth by brahmins, / and who always swiftly brings about the destruction of all sins for her devoted folk;

1.149.s:
yā ca gatā saritāṃ hi kadambairyā ca nutā satataṃ hi mahīnaiḥ ..
yā ca yutā śatatoyakadamvairyā ca gatā satataṃ himahīnaiḥ .. 24 ..
1.149.d:
या च गता सरितां हि कदम्बैर्या च नुता सततं हि महीनैः ॥
या च युता शततोयकदम्वैर्या च गता सततं हिमहीनैः ॥ 24 ॥
1.149.m: she who is reached by clusters of streams, and constantly praised by the great, / endowed with a multitude of hundreds of waters, and ever free of snow;

1.149.s:
yuktāpi kesarigaṇaiḥ karivṛndayātā sannāgayuktasalilāpi suvarṇayuktā ..
sūryāṃśutāpaparivṛddhivivṛddhiśīlā śītāṃśutulyayaśasā dadṛśe nṛpeṇa .. 25 ..
1.149.d:
युक्तापि केसरिगणैः करिवृन्दयाता सन्नागयुक्तसलिलापि सुवर्णयुक्ता ॥
सूर्यांशुतापपरिवृद्धिविवृद्धिशीला शीतांशुतुल्ययशसा ददृशे नृपेण ॥ 25 ॥
1.149.m: though frequented by prides of lions, trodden by herds of elephants; though its waters contain good snakes, it also possesses gold; / naturally swelling through the increase of heat from the sun's rays—[she] was seen by the king whose fame equaled the cool-rayed moon.

1.149.s: iti śrīviṣṇudharmottare prathamakhaṇḍe mārkaṇḍeyavajrasaṃvāde irāvatīvarṇano nāmaiko napañcāśaduttaraśatatamo'dhyāya .. 149 ..
1.149.d: इति श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे प्रथमखण्डे मार्कण्डेयवज्रसंवादे इरावतीवर्णनो नामैको नपञ्चाशदुत्तरशततमोऽध्याय ॥ 149 ॥
1.149.m: Thus ends the one hundred and forty-ninth chapter, entitled "Description of the Irāvatī," in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra in the first book of the venerable Viṣṇudharmottara.

1.150.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ālokayannadīṃ puṇyāṃ tatsamīrahataklamaḥ ..
sa gacchanneva dadṛśe himavantaṃ mahāgirim .. 1 ..
1.150.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
आलोकयन्नदीं पुण्यां तत्समीरहतक्लमः ॥
स गच्छन्नेव ददृशे हिमवन्तं महागिरिम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.150.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Looking upon the sacred river, his weariness dispelled by its breeze, / as he walked on, he beheld the great mountain Himavat,

1.150.s:
khamullikhadbhirbahubhirvṛtaṃ śṛṅgaiḥ supāṇḍuraiḥ..
pakṣiṇāmatha saṃcārairvinā siddhagatiṃ śubhām ..2 ..
1.150.d:
खमुल्लिखद्भिर्बहुभिर्वृतं शृङ्गैः सुपाण्डुरैः॥
पक्षिणामथ संचारैर्विना सिद्धगतिं शुभाम् ॥2 ॥
1.150.m: surrounded by many very pale peaks that scraped the sky, / with no path for birds, [having only] the auspicious path of the Siddhas,

1.150.s:
nadīprapātasaṃjātamahāśabdaiḥ samantataḥ ..
asaṃśrutānyaśabdantaṃ śītatoyaṃ manoramam .. 3 ..
1.150.d:
नदीप्रपातसंजातमहाशब्दैः समन्ततः ॥
असंश्रुतान्यशब्दन्तं शीततोयं मनोरमम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.150.m: where no other sounds were heard on all sides / above the great noises produced by the river's waterfalls, having cool waters, charming,

1.150.s:
devadāruvanairnīlaiḥ kṛtādhovasanaṃ śubham ..
meghottarīyaṃ taṃ śailaṃ dadṛśe sa narādhipaḥ .. 4 ..
1.150.d:
देवदारुवनैर्नीलैः कृताधोवसनं शुभम् ॥
मेघोत्तरीयं तं शैलं ददृशे स नराधिपः ॥ 4 ॥
1.150.m: wearing an auspicious lower garment made of dark deodar forests / and an upper garment of clouds—that mountain the lord of men beheld:

1.150.s:
śvenameghakṛtoṣṇīṣaṃ candrārkamukuṭaṃ kvacit ..
himānuliptasarvāṅgaṃ kvaciddhātuvicitritam .. 5 ..
1.150.d:
श्वेनमेघकृतोष्णीषं चन्द्रार्कमुकुटं क्वचित् ॥
हिमानुलिप्तसर्वाङ्गं क्वचिद्धातुविचित्रितम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.150.m: wearing a turban made of white clouds, with the moon and sun as a diadem in places, / with all its limbs smeared with snow, and variegated with minerals in places;

1.150.s:
candanenānuliptāṅgadattapañcāṅguliṃ yathā ..
śītapradaṃ nidāghe'pi śilāviṣamasaṃkaṭam .. 6 ..
1.150.d:
चन्दनेनानुलिप्ताङ्गदत्तपञ्चाङ्गुलिं यथा ॥
शीतप्रदं निदाघेऽपि शिलाविषमसंकटम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.150.m: like one whose limbs are smeared with sandal paste and marked with five-finger prints; / giving coolness even in summer, rugged and impenetrable with rocks;

1.150.s:
sālaktakairapsarasāṃ mudritaṃ caraṇaiḥ kvacit ..
kvacidaspṛṣṭasūryāṃśuṃ kvacicca tamasā vṛtam .. 7 ..
1.150.d:
सालक्तकैरप्सरसां मुद्रितं चरणैः क्वचित् ॥
क्वचिदस्पृष्टसूर्यांशुं क्वचिच्च तमसा वृतम् ॥ 7 ॥
1.150.m: imprinted in places with the red-lac-stained feet of Apsarases, / in places untouched by the rays of the sun, and in places shrouded in darkness;

1.150.s:
darīmukhaiḥ kvacidbhīmaiḥ pibantamanilaṃ bahu ..
kvacidvidyādharagaṇaiḥ krīḍadbhirupaśobhitam .. 8 ..
1.150.d:
दरीमुखैः क्वचिद्भीमैः पिबन्तमनिलं बहु ॥
क्वचिद्विद्याधरगणैः क्रीडद्भिरुपशोभितम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.150.m: drinking much wind in places through fearful cavernous mouths, / adorned in places with playing hosts of Vidyādharas;

1.150.s:
upagītaṃ tathā mukhyaiḥ kinnarāṇāṃ gaṇaiḥ kvacit ..
āpānabhūmau ca gaṇairgandharvāpsarasāṃ kvacit .. 9 ..
1.150.d:
उपगीतं तथा मुख्यैः किन्नराणां गणैः क्वचित् ॥
आपानभूमौ च गणैर्गन्धर्वाप्सरसां क्वचित् ॥ 9 ॥
1.150.m: sung to in places by prominent troupes of Kinnaras, / and in places by groups of Gandharvas and Apsarases in drinking places;

1.150.s:
gītādibhiḥ samākīrṇaṃ gandharvīṇāṃ manoharam ..
niruddhapavanairdeśairnīlaśādvalamaṇḍitaiḥ .. 1.150.10 ..
1.150.d:
गीतादिभिः समाकीर्णं गन्धर्वीणां मनोहरम् ॥
निरुद्धपवनैर्देशैर्नीलशाद्वलमण्डितैः ॥ 1.150.10 ॥
1.150.m: delightful, crowded with songs and music of Gandharva women, / with places sheltered from the wind and adorned with dark-green turf;

1.150.s:
kvacicca kusumairyuktaṃ cātyantaruciraiḥ śubham ..
tapasviśaraṇaṃ śailaṃ kāmināmapi durlabham .. 11 ..
1.150.d:
क्वचिच्च कुसुमैर्युक्तं चात्यन्तरुचिरैः शुभम् ॥
तपस्विशरणं शैलं कामिनामपि दुर्लभम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.150.m: and in places endowed with exceedingly bright, auspicious blossoms— / the mountain, a refuge for ascetics, difficult to reach even for lovers;

1.150.s:
mṛgayūthānucaritaṃ dantibhinnamahādrumam ..
yatra siṃhaninādena trastānāṃ bhairavaṃ ravam .. 12 ..
1.150.d:
मृगयूथानुचरितं दन्तिभिन्नमहाद्रुमम् ॥
यत्र सिंहनिनादेन त्रस्तानां भैरवं रवम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.150.m: frequented by herds of deer, its great trees shattered by elephants, / where, having heard the terrifying roar of those terrified by the lion's roar,

1.150.s:
śrutvotpaśyati vibhrāntaṃ gajānāmākulaṃ kulam ..
tapaśca tāpasairyasya kūladeśeṣvalaṃkṛtam .. 13 ..
1.150.d:
श्रुत्वोत्पश्यति विभ्रान्तं गजानामाकुलं कुलम् ॥
तपश्च तापसैर्यस्य कूलदेशेष्वलंकृतम् ॥ 13 ॥
1.150.m: one sees the bewildered, agitated herd of elephants; / and on whose slopes penance is adorned by ascetics.

1.150.s:
ratnairyataḥ samutpannaistrailokyaṃ cāpyalaṃkṛtam ..
ahīnaśaraṇaṃ nityamahīnajanasevitam .. 14 ..
1.150.d:
रत्नैर्यतः समुत्पन्नैस्त्रैलोक्यं चाप्यलंकृतम् ॥
अहीनशरणं नित्यमहीनजनसेवितम् ॥ 14 ॥
1.150.m: from which arose the jewels that also adorn the three worlds; / a constant, faultless refuge resorted to by noble people;

1.150.s:
ahīnaḥ paśyati girimahīnaṃ ratnasampadam ..
alpena tapasā yatra siddhiḥ prāpyeta tāpasaiḥ .. 15 ..
1.150.d:
अहीनः पश्यति गिरिमहीनं रत्नसम्पदम् ॥
अल्पेन तपसा यत्र सिद्धिः प्राप्येत तापसैः ॥ 15 ॥
1.150.m: the flawless [king] beheld that mountain possessed of boundless wealth of gems, / where ascetics attain perfection with little austerity;

1.150.s:
yaśca darśanamātreṇa sarvakalmaṣanāśanaḥ ..
mahāprapātasaṃpātaprabhītakhagabandhubhi. . 16 ..
1.150.d:
यश्च दर्शनमात्रेण सर्वकल्मषनाशनः ॥
महाप्रपातसंपातप्रभीतखगबन्धुभि॥ 16 ॥
1.150.m: and which destroys all sins merely by being seen; / whose feathered flocks were frightened by the descent into the great chasms;

1.150.s:
vāyunīta sadāvṛṣṭiḥ kṛtadeśaṃ kvacitkvacit ..
alabdhajaladaiḥ śṛṅgaiḥ kvaciccātisamucchritaiḥ .. 17 ..
1.150.d:
वायुनीत सदावृष्टिः कृतदेशं क्वचित्क्वचित् ॥
अलब्धजलदैः शृङ्गैः क्वचिच्चातिसमुच्छ्रितैः ॥ 17 ॥
1.150.m: where rain was constantly carried by the wind to make [wet] regions here and there, / and where, with exceedingly lofty peaks, clouds were not reached in some places;

1.150.s:
nityārkatāpaviṣamairagamyairmanasā yutam ..
devadāru mahāvṛkṣapuñjaśākhānirantaraiḥ .. 18 ..
1.150.d:
नित्यार्कतापविषमैरगम्यैर्मनसा युतम् ॥
देवदारु महावृक्षपुञ्जशाखानिरन्तरैः ॥ 18 ॥
1.150.m: endowed with [heights] inaccessible even to the mind, uneven with perpetual scorching of the sun, / dense with clusters of branches of great devadāru trees;

1.150.s:
samastabhuvanākāraiḥ pradeśairupaśobhitam ..
himacchannamahāśṛṃgaṃ prapātamitanirjharam ..
śabdalabhyāmbuviṣamaṃ himasaṃruddhakandaram .. 19 ..
1.150.d:
समस्तभुवनाकारैः प्रदेशैरुपशोभितम् ॥
हिमच्छन्नमहाशृंगं प्रपातमितनिर्झरम् ॥
शब्दलभ्याम्बुविषमं हिमसंरुद्धकन्दरम् ॥ 19 ॥
1.150.m: adorned with regions having the form of all the worlds; / with great peaks covered in snow, with waterfalls and measured torrents, / difficult on account of waters heard only by sound, with caves blocked by snow.

1.150.s:
dṛṣṭvaiva tāṃ cārunitambabhūmiṃ mahānubhāvaḥ sa mahīndranāthaḥ ..
babhrāma tatraiva mudā sametaḥ sthānaṃ tataḥ kiñcidathā sasāda .. 1.150.20 ..
1.150.d:
दृष्ट्वैव तां चारुनितम्बभूमिं महानुभावः स महीन्द्रनाथः ॥
बभ्राम तत्रैव मुदा समेतः स्थानं ततः किञ्चिदथा ससाद ॥ 1.150.20 ॥
1.150.m: Having beheld that beautiful slope, that noble lord of the earth / wandered right there, filled with joy, and then reached a certain place.

1.151.s:
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
tasyaiva parvatendrasya pradeśaṃ sumanoharam ..
agamyaṃ mānuṣairanyairdaivayogādupāgataḥ .. 1 ..
1.151.d:
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
तस्यैव पर्वतेन्द्रस्य प्रदेशं सुमनोहरम् ॥
अगम्यं मानुषैरन्यैर्दैवयोगादुपागतः ॥ 1 ॥
1.151.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / By the decree of fate, he arrived at a delightful region of that lord of mountains, / inaccessible to other mortals,

1.151.s:
irāvatī saricchreṣṭhā yasmāddeśā dvinirgatā ..
meghaśyāmaṃ ca taṃ deśaṃ drumakhaṇḍairanekaśaḥ .. 2 ..
1.151.d:
इरावती सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा यस्माद्देशा द्विनिर्गता ॥
मेघश्यामं च तं देशं द्रुमखण्डैरनेकशः ॥ 2 ॥
1.151.m: from which region the Irāvatī, the best of rivers, flows forth; / a region dark as a cloud with numerous groves of trees:

1.151.s:
sālaistālaistamālaiśca karṇikāraiḥ saśālmalaiḥ ..
nyagrodhaiśca tathāśvatthaiḥ śirīṣaiḥ śiṃśapādrumaiḥ .. 3 ..
1.151.d:
सालैस्तालैस्तमालैश्च कर्णिकारैः सशाल्मलैः ॥
न्यग्रोधैश्च तथाश्वत्थैः शिरीषैः शिंशपाद्रुमैः ॥ 3 ॥
1.151.m: with sāla, tāla, tamāla, and karṇikāra trees, with śālmali trees, / with nyagrodha, aśvattha, śirīṣa, and śiṃśapā trees,

1.151.s:
śleṣmātakairāmalakairharītakavibhītakaiḥ ..
ramyaiścandanavṛkṣaiśca kapitthai raktacandanaiḥ ..4..
1.151.d:
श्लेष्मातकैरामलकैर्हरीतकविभीतकैः ॥
रम्यैश्चन्दनवृक्षैश्च कपित्थै रक्तचन्दनैः ॥4॥
1.151.m: with śleṣmātaka, āmalaka, harītakī, and vibhītaka trees, / with lovely sandalwood trees, kapittha trees, and red sandalwood,

1.151.s:
vaṭamāhiṣakākṣoṭairaśvakarṇaistathārjunaiḥ ..
hastikarṇaiḥ sapanasaiḥ kovidāraiḥ supuṣpitaiḥ ..5..
1.151.d:
वटमाहिषकाक्षोटैरश्वकर्णैस्तथार्जुनैः ॥
हस्तिकर्णैः सपनसैः कोविदारैः सुपुष्पितैः ॥5॥
1.151.m: with vaṭa, māhiṣa, akṣoṭa, aśvakarṇa, and arjuna trees, / with hastikarṇa, panasa, and beautifully flowered kovidāra trees,

1.151.s:
devadārumahāvṛkṣaistathā kālīyakadrumaiḥ ..
padmakaiścandanairbilvaiḥ kuṭajairharicandanaiḥ .. 6 ..
1.151.d:
देवदारुमहावृक्षैस्तथा कालीयकद्रुमैः ॥
पद्मकैश्चन्दनैर्बिल्वैः कुटजैर्हरिचन्दनैः ॥ 6 ॥
1.151.m: with great devadāru trees and kālīyaka trees, / with padmaka, sandalwood, bilva, kuṭaja, and haricandana trees,

1.151.s:
prācīnāgurukaiścaiva sthūṇikaiḥ samaśaṇḍikaiḥ ..
kharjūrairnārikeraiśca priyālvāmrātakeṅgudaiḥ ..7..
1.151.d:
प्राचीनागुरुकैश्चैव स्थूणिकैः समशण्डिकैः ॥
खर्जूरैर्नारिकेरैश्च प्रियाल्वाम्रातकेङ्गुदैः ॥7॥
1.151.m: with prācīnāguru, sthūṇika, and samaśaṇḍika trees, / with date palms, coconut palms, and priyāla, āmrātaka, and inguda trees,

1.151.s:
terumānairvaṭerbhanyaiḥ kāśmīraiḥ phalibhistathā ..
jātīphalaiḥ pūgaphalaiḥ kaṭphalairlavalīphalaiḥ .. 8 ..
1.151.d:
तेरुमानैर्वटेर्भन्यैः काश्मीरैः फलिभिस्तथा ॥
जातीफलैः पूगफलैः कट्फलैर्लवलीफलैः ॥ 8 ॥
1.151.m: with terumāna, vaṭerbha, kāśmīra, and fruited phalin trees, / with nutmegs, areca nuts, katphala fruits, and lavalī fruits,

1.151.s:
mandāraiḥ kovidāraiśca kiṃśukaiḥ kusumāṃśubhiḥ ..
palāśaiḥ śamisūllāsairvetasairamlavetasaiḥ .. 9 ..
1.151.d:
मन्दारैः कोविदारैश्च किंशुकैः कुसुमांशुभिः ॥
पलाशैः शमिसूल्लासैर्वेतसैरम्लवेतसैः ॥ 9 ॥
1.151.m: with mandāras, kovidāras, and kiṃśukas radiant with blossoms, / with palāśas, bright with śamī trees, and canes and sour canes,

1.151.s:
raktātiraṅganāriṅgairiṃgudaiḥ sapriyaṃgubhiḥ ..
raktāśokaistathā'śokairārukaiḥ sacirārukaiḥ..1.151.10..
1.151.d:
रक्तातिरङ्गनारिङ्गैरिंगुदैः सप्रियंगुभिः ॥
रक्ताशोकैस्तथाऽशोकैरारुकैः सचिरारुकैः॥1.151.10॥
1.151.m: with raktātiraṅga, nāriṅga, inguda, and priyaṅgu trees, / with red aśokas and aśokas, and āruka along with cirāruka trees,

1.151.s:
mucukundaistathā kundairāṭarūṣaparūṣakaiḥ ..
kiṃkarātaiḥ kirātaiśca ketakaiśca saketakaiḥ..11..
1.151.d:
मुचुकुन्दैस्तथा कुन्दैराटरूषपरूषकैः ॥
किंकरातैः किरातैश्च केतकैश्च सकेतकैः॥11॥
1.151.m: with mucukundas, kundas, āṭarūṣa, and parūṣaka trees, / with kiṃkarāta, kirāta, and ketaka along with saketaka trees,

1.151.s:
śobhāñjanairañjanaiśca mukūlakanikocakaiḥ ..
supūrṇacāruvasanairdrumaiḥ śreṣṭhaistathāsanaiḥ .. 12 ..
1.151.d:
शोभाञ्जनैरञ्जनैश्च मुकूलकनिकोचकैः ॥
सुपूर्णचारुवसनैर्द्रुमैः श्रेष्ठैस्तथासनैः ॥ 12 ॥
1.151.m: with śobhāñjana, añjana, mukūlaka, and nikocaka trees, / with excellent asana trees looking like fine, beautiful garments,

1.151.s:
manmathasya śarākāraissahakārairmanoharaiḥ ..
pītayūthikayā rājañśvetayūthikayā tathā ..13..
1.151.d:
मन्मथस्य शराकारैस्सहकारैर्मनोहरैः ॥
पीतयूथिकया राजञ्श्वेतयूथिकया तथा ॥13॥
1.151.m: with delightful mango trees having the shape of the arrows of the god of love, / O king, with yellow jasmine and white jasmine,

1.151.s:
jātyā campakajātyā ca tumburaiścāpyudumbaraiḥ ..
māṣaiścoccaissalakucaistilambalakuśambalaiḥ .. 14 ..
1.151.d:
जात्या चम्पकजात्या च तुम्बुरैश्चाप्युदुम्बरैः ॥
माषैश्चोच्चैस्सलकुचैस्तिलम्बलकुशम्बलैः ॥ 14 ॥
1.151.m: with jātī and campaka-jātī, with tumburu and udumbara trees, / with māṣas and tall lakuca, tilambala, and kuśambala trees,

1.151.s:
tathā supuṣpāva raṇairvaraṇaiḥ kāmivallabhaiḥ..
puṣpākulaiśca bakulaiḥ pāribhadrakabhadrakaiḥ..15..
1.151.d:
तथा सुपुष्पाव रणैर्वरणैः कामिवल्लभैः॥
पुष्पाकुलैश्च बकुलैः पारिभद्रकभद्रकैः॥15॥
1.151.m: and with varaṇa trees beloved of lovers, veiled with beautiful flowers, / with bakulas teeming with blossoms, and pāribhadraka and bhadraka trees,

1.151.s:
dhārākadaṃbaiḥ kuṭajaiḥ kadaṃbairgirikūṭajaiḥ..
ākrāntasarvakakubhaiḥ kakubhaiḥ kamanīyakaiḥ.. ..16..
1.151.d:
धाराकदंबैः कुटजैः कदंबैर्गिरिकूटजैः॥
आक्रान्तसर्वककुभैः ककुभैः कमनीयकैः॥ ॥16॥
1.151.m: with stream-side kadambas, kuṭajas, mountain-ridge kadambas, / and with lovely kakubha trees pervading every quarter,

1.151.s:
karkandhubadarairnīpaiḥ dīpairiva mahojjvalaiḥ ..
raktaiḥ pālīvataiḥ śvetairdāḍimaiścaṇyakadrumaiḥ ..17 ..
1.151.d:
कर्कन्धुबदरैर्नीपैः दीपैरिव महोज्ज्वलैः ॥
रक्तैः पालीवतैः श्वेतैर्दाडिमैश्चण्यकद्रुमैः ॥17 ॥
1.151.m: with karkandhu, badara, and nīpa trees, greatly blazing like lamps, / with red and white pālīvatas, pomegranates, and caṇyaka trees,

1.151.s:
pratānaiḥ pippalīnāṃ ca nāgavalyāśca bhāgaśaḥ ..
maricasya tathā gulmairnavamallikayā tathā .. 18 ..
1.151.d:
प्रतानैः पिप्पलीनां च नागवल्याश्च भागशः ॥
मरिचस्य तथा गुल्मैर्नवमल्लिकया तथा ॥ 18 ॥
1.151.m: and in parts with spreads of long pepper and betel pepper, / as well as thickets of black pepper and navamallikā,

1.151.s:
mṛdvīkāmaṇḍalairmukhyairatimuktakamaṇḍalaiḥ ..
trapusairvārukānāṃ ca pratānaiḥ saphalaiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 19 ..
1.151.d:
मृद्वीकामण्डलैर्मुख्यैरतिमुक्तकमण्डलैः ॥
त्रपुसैर्वारुकानां च प्रतानैः सफलैः शुभैः ॥ 19 ॥
1.151.m: with prime clusters of grapes and clusters of atimuktaka, / with gourds and cucumbers, their vines bearing auspicious fruit,

1.151.s:
kūṣmāṇḍānāṃ pratānaiśca alābūnāṃ tathā kvacit..
cirbhaṭasya pratānaiśca paṭolaiḥ kāravellakaiḥ .. 1.151.20 ..
1.151.d:
कूष्माण्डानां प्रतानैश्च अलाबूनां तथा क्वचित्॥
चिर्भटस्य प्रतानैश्च पटोलैः कारवेल्लकैः ॥ 1.151.20 ॥
1.151.m: and with vines of ash gourds and bottle gourds in places, / and vines of melons, pointed gourds, and bitter gourds,

1.151.s:
karkoṭakaiḥ pratānaiśca vārtākairbṛhatīphalaiḥ ..
kahlārairmūlakairmukhyaiḥ śākaiśca vividhaistathā ..21..
1.151.d:
कर्कोटकैः प्रतानैश्च वार्ताकैर्बृहतीफलैः ॥
कह्लारैर्मूलकैर्मुख्यैः शाकैश्च विविधैस्तथा ॥21॥
1.151.m: and with creepers of karkoṭaka, eggplants, and bṛhatī fruits, / with excellent kahlāra water-lilies, radishes, and various vegetables,

1.151.s:
suvarcalābhiḥ sarvābhiḥ sarṣapābhistathaiva ca ..
kākolīkṣīrakākolī chatrayā cāticchatrayā ..22 .
1.151.d:
सुवर्चलाभिः सर्वाभिः सर्षपाभिस्तथैव च ॥
काकोलीक्षीरकाकोली छत्रया चातिच्छत्रया ॥22 ।
1.151.m: with all kinds of suvarcalā and mustard greens, / with kākolī, kṣīrakākolī, chatrā, and atichatrā,

1.151.s:
kākamācīmahābaddhiśaśakarddalakandalaiḥ ..
tathā kṣīrikaśākena kālaśākena cāpyatha .. 23 ..
1.151.d:
काकमाचीमहाबद्धिशशकर्द्दलकन्दलैः ॥
तथा क्षीरिकशाकेन कालशाकेन चाप्यथ ॥ 23 ॥
1.151.m: with kākamācī, mahābaddhi, tubers of śaśakarddala, / and also with kṣīrika greens and kāla greens,

1.151.s:
śimbidhānyaistathā dhānyaiḥ sarvairniravaśeṣataḥ ..
oṣadhībhirvicitrābhidīpyamānābhireva ca .. 24 ..
1.151.d:
शिम्बिधान्यैस्तथा धान्यैः सर्वैर्निरवशेषतः ॥
ओषधीभिर्विचित्राभिदीप्यमानाभिरेव च ॥ 24 ॥
1.151.m: with pulse grains and grains of all kinds without exception, / and with diverse medicinal herbs, verily shining bright,

1.151.s:
kandairvidāryā ca tathā tarūṭaiḥ svādusaṃyutaiḥ ..
suniṣaṇṇāśaṭīśeṣārājakṣayakavāstukaiḥ .. 25 ..
1.151.d:
कन्दैर्विदार्या च तथा तरूटैः स्वादुसंयुतैः ॥
सुनिषण्णाशटीशेषाराजक्षयकवास्तुकैः ॥ 25 ॥
1.151.m: with tubers and vidārī, and with tarūṭas endowed with sweet taste, / with suniṣaṇṇa, śaṭī, śeṣā, rājakṣayaka, and vāstuka,

1.151.s:
āyuṣyābhiryaśasyābhirvarṇyābhiśca narādhipa ..
jarāmṛtyubhayaghnābhiḥ kṣudbhayaghnābhireva ca .. 26 ..
1.151.d:
आयुष्याभिर्यशस्याभिर्वर्ण्याभिश्च नराधिप ॥
जरामृत्युभयघ्नाभिः क्षुद्भयघ्नाभिरेव च ॥ 26 ॥
1.151.m: giving long life, giving fame, improving complexion, O ruler of men, / destroying fear of old age and death, and destroying fear of hunger,

1.151.s:
saubhāgyajananībhiśca vṛṣyābhiścāpyanekaśaḥ ..
vetraveṇulatābhiśca tathā kīcakaveṇubhiḥ .. 27..
1.151.d:
सौभाग्यजननीभिश्च वृष्याभिश्चाप्यनेकशः ॥
वेत्रवेणुलताभिश्च तथा कीचकवेणुभिः ॥ 27॥
1.151.m: bringing good fortune and aphrodisiac in many ways; / with creepers of cane and bamboo, and with whistling bamboos,

1.151.s:
kāśaiḥ śaśāṅkasaṃkāśaiḥ śaragulmaistathā kvacit ..
kuśagulmaistathā ramyairgulmaiścekṣumanoharaiḥ .. 28 ..
1.151.d:
काशैः शशाङ्कसंकाशैः शरगुल्मैस्तथा क्वचित् ॥
कुशगुल्मैस्तथा रम्यैर्गुल्मैश्चेक्षुमनोहरैः ॥ 28 ॥
1.151.m: with kāśa grass resembling the moon, and thickets of śara reeds here and there, / with lovely clusters of kuśa grass, and charming clumps of sugarcane,

1.151.s:
kārpāsayā tuvaryā ca dukūlena śubhena ca ..
tathā ca kadalīkhaṇḍairmanohāribhiruttamaiḥ .. 29 ..
1.151.d:
कार्पासया तुवर्या च दुकूलेन शुभेन च ॥
तथा च कदलीखण्डैर्मनोहारिभिरुत्तमैः ॥ 29 ॥
1.151.m: with cotton, pigeon pea, and auspicious fine cloth [yielding plants], / and also with delightful, excellent groves of plantains,

1.151.s:
tathā marakataprakhyaiḥ pradeśaiḥ śādvalānvitaiḥ ..
irāpuṣpasamāyuktaiḥ kuṅkumasya ca bhāgaśaḥ .. 1.151.30 ..
1.151.d:
तथा मरकतप्रख्यैः प्रदेशैः शाद्वलान्वितैः ॥
इरापुष्पसमायुक्तैः कुङ्कुमस्य च भागशः ॥ 1.151.30 ॥
1.151.m: and with grassy regions resembling emeralds, / joined with irā flowers and patches of saffron,

1.151.s:
tagarātiviṣāmāṃsīgranthiparṇīsurāgadaiḥ ..
suvarṇapuṣpaiśca tathā bhūmipuṣpaistathā paraiḥ .. 31 ..
1.151.d:
तगरातिविषामांसीग्रन्थिपर्णीसुरागदैः ॥
सुवर्णपुष्पैश्च तथा भूमिपुष्पैस्तथा परैः ॥ 31 ॥
1.151.m: with tagara, ativiṣā, māṃsī, granthiparṇī, and surāgada, / with golden flowers and other ground flowers,

1.151.s:
jambīrikābhūstṛṇaiśca sarasaiḥ sṛmukaistathā ..
śṛṅgaverājamodābhiḥ kuṭherakapriyālukaiḥ .. 32 ..
1.151.d:
जम्बीरिकाभूस्तृणैश्च सरसैः सृमुकैस्तथा ॥
शृङ्गवेराजमोदाभिः कुठेरकप्रियालुकैः ॥ 32 ॥
1.151.m: with citronella, fragrant grass, juicy sṛmuka, / with ginger, celery, kuṭheraka, and priyāluka,

1.151.s:
jalajaiśca tathā padmairnānāvarṇaiḥ sugandhibhiḥ ..
udayādityasaṃkāśaiḥ pūrṇacandranibhaistathā .. 33 ..
1.151.d:
जलजैश्च तथा पद्मैर्नानावर्णैः सुगन्धिभिः ॥
उदयादित्यसंकाशैः पूर्णचन्द्रनिभैस्तथा ॥ 33 ॥
1.151.m: with water-born lotuses of various colors and sweet fragrance, / resembling the rising sun and like the full moon,

1.151.s:
tapanīyasavarṇaiśca atasīpuṣpasannibhaiḥ ..
śukapatranibhaiścānyaiḥ sthalapadmaiśca bhāgaśaḥ .. 34 ..
1.151.d:
तपनीयसवर्णैश्च अतसीपुष्पसन्निभैः ॥
शुकपत्रनिभैश्चान्यैः स्थलपद्मैश्च भागशः ॥ 34 ॥
1.151.m: possessing the color of refined gold, resembling linseed blossoms, / others resembling parrot feathers, and with land lotuses in sections,

1.151.s:
pañcavarṇaiḥ samākīrṇaṃ bahuvaṇaistathaiva ca ..
duṣṭadṛṣṭyāhitamudaiḥ kusumaiścandrasannibhaiḥ .. 35 ..
1.151.d:
पञ्चवर्णैः समाकीर्णं बहुवणैस्तथैव च ॥
दुष्टदृष्ट्याहितमुदैः कुसुमैश्चन्द्रसन्निभैः ॥ 35 ॥
1.151.m: scattered with five colors, and also of many colors, / with blossoms resembling the moon that impart joy to the gaze of evil eyes.

1.151.s:
tathā vahniśikhākārai rājanraktotpalaiḥ śubhaiḥ ..
nīlotpalaiḥ sakahlārairdurjjātakakaśerukaiḥ .. 36 ..
1.151.d:
तथा वह्निशिखाकारै राजन्रक्तोत्पलैः शुभैः ॥
नीलोत्पलैः सकह्लारैर्दुर्ज्जातककशेरुकैः ॥ 36 ॥
1.151.m: And likewise with auspicious red water lilies resembling flames of fire, O king, / blue water lilies, kahlāra lilies, and poorly sprung kaśeruka tubers;

1.151.s:
śṛṅgāṭakairmṛṇālaiśca kāvāṭai rākṣasotpalaiḥ ..
jalajaiḥ sthalajairmūlaiḥ phalaiḥ puṣpairaśeṣataḥ .. 37 ..
1.151.d:
शृङ्गाटकैर्मृणालैश्च कावाटै राक्षसोत्पलैः ॥
जलजैः स्थलजैर्मूलैः फलैः पुष्पैरशेषतः ॥ 37 ॥
1.151.m: with water caltrops and lotus stalks, kāvāṭas, rākṣasotpala lilies, / with water-born and land-born roots, fruits, and flowers without exception,

1.151.s:
vividhaiścaiva nīvārairmunibhojyairnarādhipa ..
na taddhānyaṃ na tatsasyaṃ na tacchākaṃ na tatphalam .. 38 ..
1.151.d:
विविधैश्चैव नीवारैर्मुनिभोज्यैर्नराधिप ॥
न तद्धान्यं न तत्सस्यं न तच्छाकं न तत्फलम् ॥ 38 ॥
1.151.m: and with diverse wild grains fit for the food of sages, O ruler of men. / There was no grain, no crop, no vegetable, no fruit,

1.151.s:
na tanmūlaṃ na tatkandaṃ na tatpuṣpaṃ narādhipa ..
nāgalokodbhavaṃ yacca nākalokodbhavaṃ ca yat .. 39 ..
1.151.d:
न तन्मूलं न तत्कन्दं न तत्पुष्पं नराधिप ॥
नागलोकोद्भवं यच्च नाकलोकोद्भवं च यत् ॥ 39 ॥
1.151.m: no root, no tuber, no flower, O ruler of men, / born in the world of nāgas or born in the heavenly realm,

1.151.s:
anūpabandhanotthaṃ ca tanna yatrāsti yādava ..
sadā puṣpaphalaṃ sarvamajasramṛtuyogataḥ .. 1.151.40 ..
1.151.d:
अनूपबन्धनोत्थं च तन्न यत्रास्ति यादव ॥
सदा पुष्पफलं सर्वमजस्रमृतुयोगतः ॥ 1.151.40 ॥
1.151.m: or growing tied to marshes, that was not found there, O Yādava. / Everything bore flowers and fruit at all times, constantly through the union of the seasons.

1.151.s:
maheśvaraḥ sa dadṛśe tapaso'rthāya vo gataḥ ..
dadṛśe ca tathā tatra nānārūpānpatatriṇaḥ .. 41 ..
1.151.d:
महेश्वरः स ददृशे तपसोऽर्थाय वो गतः ॥
ददृशे च तथा तत्र नानारूपान्पतत्रिणः ॥ 41 ॥
1.151.m: He, a great lord, was seen gone there for the purpose of ascetic penance. / And there he likewise saw birds of various forms:

1.151.s:
mayūrāñśatapatrām̐śca kalavācakakokilān ..
tathā kādambakānhaṃsānkukkuṭāñjalakukkuṭān ..82..
1.151.d:
मयूराञ्शतपत्राम्̐श्च कलवाचककोकिलान् ॥
तथा कादम्बकान्हंसान्कुक्कुटाञ्जलकुक्कुटान् ॥82॥
1.151.m: peacocks, woodpeckers, sweet-singing cuckoos, / as well as teal, geese, roosters, and water fowl,

1.151.s:
kṛkarānbarkaśāñśyāmāṃstittirānsakapiñjalān ..
dhārtarāṣṭrānplavānmadgūnkalaviṅkāñchukānbakān .. 43 ..
1.151.d:
कृकरान्बर्कशाञ्श्यामांस्तित्तिरान्सकपिञ्जलान् ॥
धार्तराष्ट्रान्प्लवान्मद्गून्कलविङ्काञ्छुकान्बकान् ॥ 43 ॥
1.151.m: kṛkara partridges, barkaśas, syāmā birds, francolins with kapiñjala francolins, / dhārtarāṣṭra geese, plava water-birds, cormorants, sparrows, parrots, and herons,

1.151.s:
caṭakāṃścakravākāṃśca āṭakāṃṣṭiṭṭibhānsaṭān ..
putrapriyāṃllohapṛṣṭāngonandagirivartakān .. 44 ..
1.151.d:
चटकांश्चक्रवाकांश्च आटकांष्टिट्टिभान्सटान् ॥
पुत्रप्रियांल्लोहपृष्टान्गोनन्दगिरिवर्तकान् ॥ 44 ॥
1.151.m: house sparrows and ruddy sheldrakes, āṭis, lapwings, saṭas, / putrapriyas, lohapṛṣṭhas, gonandas, and mountain quail,

1.151.s:
pārāvatānkāmalāṃśca śārakāñjīvajīvakān ..
lāvavartakavattīrānraktadharmaprabhadrakān ..45..
1.151.d:
पारावतान्कामलांश्च शारकाञ्जीवजीवकान् ॥
लाववर्तकवत्तीरान्रक्तधर्मप्रभद्रकान् ॥45॥
1.151.m: pigeons, kāmalas, starlings, jīvañjīvaka birds, / lāvaka and vartaka quail, and vattīras, raktadharmas, and prabhadrakas,

1.151.s:
tāmracūḍānvarṇacūḍānkoyaṣṭīnkhañjarīṭakān ..
ṛṣiputrānsahārītānkukkuṭānkāṣṭhakukkuṭān .. 46 ..
1.151.d:
ताम्रचूडान्वर्णचूडान्कोयष्टीन्खञ्जरीटकान् ॥
ऋषिपुत्रान्सहारीतान्कुक्कुटान्काष्ठकुक्कुटान् ॥ 46 ॥
1.151.m: red-crested cocks, variegated-crested birds, lapwings, wagtails, / ṛṣiputras, along with green pigeons, roosters, and woodpeckers,

1.151.s:
laṭvām̐llaṭeṣūngokṣveḍāṃstathā kuṅkumacūḍakān ..
