bhṛṅgarājāñchārapādānbhūliṅgānpiṇḍimālavān..47..
1.151.d:
लट्वाम्̐ल्लटेषून्गोक्ष्वेडांस्तथा कुङ्कुमचूडकान् ॥
भृङ्गराजाञ्छारपादान्भूलिङ्गान्पिण्डिमालवान्॥47॥
1.151.m: laṭvā sparrows, laṭeṣus, gokṣveḍas, as well as saffron-crested birds, / racket-tailed drongos, spotted-legged birds, bhūliṅgas, and piṇḍimālavs,

1.151.s:
maṃjūlīyakadātyūhagopaputrāntsavañjulān ..
bhāradvājāṃstathā cāṣānsuvarṇānrajanīyakān ..48..
1.151.d:
मंजूलीयकदात्यूहगोपपुत्रान्त्सवञ्जुलान् ॥
भारद्वाजांस्तथा चाषान्सुवर्णान्रजनीयकान् ॥48॥
1.151.m: maṃjūlīyakas, watercocks, cowherd-boys' birds, along with vañjulas, / bhāradvāja larks, and rollers, golden oriole-like birds, and nightjars.

1.151.s:
etāṃścānyāṃśca hi bahūnpakṣisaṃghānmanoharān ..
śvāpadānvividhākārānmṛgāṃścaiva mahāmṛgān .. 49 ..
1.151.d:
एतांश्चान्यांश्च हि बहून्पक्षिसंघान्मनोहरान् ॥
श्वापदान्विविधाकारान्मृगांश्चैव महामृगान् ॥ 49 ॥
1.151.m: These and many other delightful flocks of birds [he saw], / and beasts of prey of diverse shapes, and deer and large wild animals:

1.151.s:
vyāghrānkesariṇaḥ siṃhānvīcinaḥ śarabhānvṛkān ..
ṛkṣāṃstarakṣūnbandhūkāngolāṅgūlānsavānarān .. 1.151.50 ..
1.151.d:
व्याघ्रान्केसरिणः सिंहान्वीचिनः शरभान्वृकान् ॥
ऋक्षांस्तरक्षून्बन्धूकान्गोलाङ्गूलान्सवानरान् ॥ 1.151.50 ॥
1.151.m: tigers, maned lions, leopards, śarabhas, wolves, / bears, hyenas, bandhūkas, langurs, along with monkeys,

1.151.s:
śaśām̐llokācchaśapalānmārjārānmāyavaḥ śunaḥ ..
mṛṣikānnākulānkācānsiṃhānnoḍrasuromakān .. 51 ..
1.151.d:
शशाम्̐ल्लोकाच्छशपलान्मार्जारान्मायवः शुनः ॥
मृषिकान्नाकुलान्काचान्सिंहान्नोड्रसुरोमकान् ॥ 51 ॥
1.151.m: hares, foxes, jackals, cats, wild dogs, / mice, mongooses, kācas, lions, otters, and suromakas,

1.151.s:
tathā mattāṃśca mātaṅgānmahiṣāngavayānvṛ ṣān..
caramānsṛmarāṃścaiva tathā gorānnakhānapi ..52..
1.151.d:
तथा मत्तांश्च मातङ्गान्महिषान्गवयान्वृ षान्॥
चरमान्सृमरांश्चैव तथा गोरान्नखानपि ॥52॥
1.151.m: as well as intoxicated elephants, buffaloes, gavaya oxen, bulls, / carama and sṛmara antelopes, as well as wild oxen and nakhas,

1.151.s:
urabhrāṃśca tathā meṣānsāraṅgānatha karkaśān ..
rurūnjamṛṣpadānṛṣpānmarkaṭānkarkaṭānmṛgān ..
nīlāṃścaiva mahānīlānkarālamṛgamārdakān ..53..
1.151.d:
उरभ्रांश्च तथा मेषान्सारङ्गानथ कर्कशान् ॥
रुरून्जमृष्पदानृष्पान्मर्कटान्कर्कटान्मृगान् ॥
नीलांश्चैव महानीलान्करालमृगमार्दकान् ॥53॥
1.151.m: sheep as well as rams, sāraṅga deer, rough beasts, / ruru deer, jamṛṣpadas, ṛṣpas, monkeys, karkaṭa deer, / nīlagai and mahānīlas, terrible deer-destroying predators,

1.151.s: śvadaṃṣṭrānrāmaśarabhānkoḍakākapaśambarān ..54..
1.151.d: श्वदंष्ट्रान्रामशरभान्कोडकाकपशम्बरान् ॥54॥
1.151.m: śvadaṃṣṭras, rāmaśarabhas, koḍakākas, and sambars,

1.151.s:
karālānkṛtamālāṃśca kālapucchām̐stathāruṇān ..
uṣṭrāngajānvarāhām̐śca turagānkharagardabhān.. 55 ..
1.151.d:
करालान्कृतमालांश्च कालपुच्छाम्̐स्तथारुणान् ॥
उष्ट्रान्गजान्वराहाम्̐श्च तुरगान्खरगर्दभान्॥ 55 ॥
1.151.m: terrible kṛtamālas, black-tailed deer, and reddish deer, / camels, elephants, boars, horses, and asses.

1.151.s:
etānpaśyansa madreśo viruddhāṃśca parasparam ..
aviruddhānvane tasminnirvṛtiṃ ca parāṃ yayau .... 56 ..
1.151.d:
एतान्पश्यन्स मद्रेशो विरुद्धांश्च परस्परम् ॥
अविरुद्धान्वने तस्मिन्निर्वृतिं च परां ययौ ॥॥ 56 ॥
1.151.m: Beholding these, naturally hostile to each other, / free from hostility in that forest, the lord of Madra attained supreme bliss.

1.151.s:
tadāśramapade mukhyo babhūvātriḥ purā nṛpa ..
tatprasādātsadā yuktaṃ sthāvarairjaṅgamaistathā .. 57 ..
1.151.d:
तदाश्रमपदे मुख्यो बभूवात्रिः पुरा नृप ॥
तत्प्रसादात्सदा युक्तं स्थावरैर्जङ्गमैस्तथा ॥ 57 ॥
1.151.m: In ancient times, O king, Atri had been the leader in that hermitage; / by his grace, it was ever filled with immovable and moving beings.

1.151.s:
hiṃsanti na tathā'nyonyaṃ hiṃsakāstu parasparam ..
kravyādāḥ prāṇinastatra sarve kṣīraphalāśanāḥ .. 58..
1.151.d:
हिंसन्ति न तथाऽन्योन्यं हिंसकास्तु परस्परम् ॥
क्रव्यादाः प्राणिनस्तत्र सर्वे क्षीरफलाशनाः ॥ 58॥
1.151.m: Harmful creatures did not harm one another there; / all the flesh-eating creatures there ate milk and fruit.

1.151.s:
nirmitāstatra ratyarthamatriṇā sumahātmanā ..
śilānāṃ nimnadeśeṣu tatra gāvaḥ svayaṃ nṛpa .. 59 ..
1.151.d:
निर्मितास्तत्र रत्यर्थमत्रिणा सुमहात्मना ॥
शिलानां निम्नदेशेषु तत्र गावः स्वयं नृप ॥ 59 ॥
1.151.m: They were made to dwell there for delight by the great-souled Atri; / in the low places of the rocks, O king, cows of their own accord

1.151.s:
payaḥ kṣaranti taddivyamamṛtasvādusannibham ..
kvacidrājamahiṣyaśca kvacidrājā ca bhāgaśaḥ .. 1.151.60 ..
1.151.d:
पयः क्षरन्ति तद्दिव्यममृतस्वादुसन्निभम् ॥
क्वचिद्राजमहिष्यश्च क्वचिद्राजा च भागशः ॥ 1.151.60 ॥
1.151.m: flowed that divine milk resembling the taste of nectar. / In some places queen consorts and in some places the king, each in turn,

1.151.s:
śilāḥ kṣīreṇa saṃpūrṇā dadhnā cānyatra yādava ..
sa paśyanparamāṃ prītimavāpa vasudhādhipaḥ ..61..
1.151.d:
शिलाः क्षीरेण संपूर्णा दध्ना चान्यत्र यादव ॥
स पश्यन्परमां प्रीतिमवाप वसुधाधिपः ॥61॥
1.151.m: saw rocks filled with milk, and elsewhere with curd, O Yādava; / seeing this, the lord of the earth attained supreme joy.

1.151.s:
sarāṃsi tatra divyāni nadyaśca vimalodakāḥ ..
mṛṇālakāni divyāni śītalāni ca bhāgaśaḥ .. 62 ..
1.151.d:
सरांसि तत्र दिव्यानि नद्यश्च विमलोदकाः ॥
मृणालकानि दिव्यानि शीतलानि च भागशः ॥ 62 ॥
1.151.m: There were divine lakes and rivers of clear water, / and divine, cool lotus stalks everywhere.

1.151.s:
kandarāṇi ca śailasya sukhasevyāni yādava ..
himapāto na tatrāsti samantātpañcayojanam .. 63 ..
1.151.d:
कन्दराणि च शैलस्य सुखसेव्यानि यादव ॥
हिमपातो न तत्रास्ति समन्तात्पञ्चयोजनम् ॥ 63 ॥
1.151.m: And the mountain caves were pleasant to inhabit, O Yādava; / there was no snowfall there within five yojanas all around.

1.151.s:
upatyakāsu śailasya śikhareṣu tu vidyate ..
tatrāpi rājañchikharaṃ parvatendrasya pāṇḍuram .. 64 ..
1.151.d:
उपत्यकासु शैलस्य शिखरेषु तु विद्यते ॥
तत्रापि राजञ्छिखरं पर्वतेन्द्रस्य पाण्डुरम् ॥ 64 ॥
1.151.m: Snow was on the mountain slopes and on the peaks, / and there too, O king, was a pale peak of the lord of mountains.

1.151.s:
himapātaṃ sadā tatra ghanāḥ kurvanti saṃhatāḥ ..
tatrāsti cāparaṃ śṛṅgaṃ yatra toyaṃ ghanā ghanāḥ .. 65 ..
1.151.d:
हिमपातं सदा तत्र घनाः कुर्वन्ति संहताः ॥
तत्रास्ति चापरं शृङ्गं यत्र तोयं घना घनाः ॥ 65 ॥
1.151.m: Dense clouds constantly caused snowfall there; / and there was another peak where dense clouds

1.151.s:
nityamevābhivarṣanti śilābhiḥ śikharaṃ kharam ..
tadāśramaṃ manohāri yatra kāmadharā dharāḥ .. 66 ..
1.151.d:
नित्यमेवाभिवर्षन्ति शिलाभिः शिखरं खरम् ॥
तदाश्रमं मनोहारि यत्र कामधरा धराः ॥ 66 ॥
1.151.m: showered water perpetually upon the sharp peak with rocks. / That hermitage was enchanting, where the trees granted desires.

1.151.s:
suramukhyopabho gyatvācchākhinaḥ saphalāḥ sadā. ..
sadopagītabhramaraṃ surastrīsevitāmaram .. 67 ..
1.151.d:
सुरमुख्योपभो ग्यत्वाच्छाखिनः सफलाः सदा॥।
सदोपगीतभ्रमरं सुरस्त्रीसेवितामरम् ॥ 67 ॥
1.151.m: Because they were enjoyed by the chief gods, the trees always bore fruit; / it was constantly sung by black bees, and immortals attended by celestial nymphs.

1.151.s:
sarvapāpakṣayakaraṃ śailasyeva mahākaram ..
vānaraiḥ krīḍamānaiśca deśe deśe narādhipa..68..
1.151.d:
सर्वपापक्षयकरं शैलस्येव महाकरम् ॥
वानरैः क्रीडमानैश्च देशे देशे नराधिप॥68॥
1.151.m: It caused the destruction of all sins, like a great tax of the mountain. / And by the playing monkeys in region after region, O ruler of men,

1.151.s:
haṃsapuñjāḥ kṛtāstatra candrabimbasamaprabhāḥ..
tadāśramasamantācca himasaṃruddhakandaram..69..
1.151.d:
हंसपुञ्जाः कृतास्तत्र चन्द्रबिम्बसमप्रभाः॥
तदाश्रमसमन्ताच्च हिमसंरुद्धकन्दरम्॥69॥
1.151.m: heaps of geese were made there, possessing splendor like the orb of the moon. / And all around that hermitage, the caves were blocked by snow,

1.151.s:
śailavāṭaiḥ parivṛtamagamyaṃ manujaiḥ sadā..
pūrvārādhitadeveśo mahārājaḥ purūravāḥ..1.151.70..
1.151.d:
शैलवाटैः परिवृतमगम्यं मनुजैः सदा॥
पूर्वाराधितदेवेशो महाराजः पुरूरवाः॥1.151.70॥
1.151.m: surrounded by mountain fences, forever impassable to men. / The great king Purūravas, who had previously worshipped the Lord of gods,

1.151.s:
tadāśramamanuprāpto devadevaprasādataḥ..
tadāśramaṃ śramaśamanaṃ manoharaṃ manoharaiḥ kusumaśatairalaṃkṛtam..
kṛtaṃ ca tatsvayamatha cātriṇā śubhaṃ śubhapradaṃ taṃ dadṛśe sa madrarāṭ..71..
1.151.d:
तदाश्रममनुप्राप्तो देवदेवप्रसादतः॥
तदाश्रमं श्रमशमनं मनोहरं मनोहरैः कुसुमशतैरलंकृतम्॥
कृतं च तत्स्वयमथ चात्रिणा शुभं शुभप्रदं तं ददृशे स मद्रराट्॥71॥
1.151.m: arrived at that hermitage by the grace of the God of gods. / The king of Madra saw that hermitage which relieves fatigue, enchanting, adorned with hundreds of captivating flowers, / auspicious, made by Atri himself, and bestowing auspiciousness.

1.152.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca..
tatra yau tau mahāśṛṅgau mahāvarṣamahāhimau..
tṛtīyaṃ tu tayormadhye śṛṅgamatyantamucchritam .. 1 ..
1.152.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच॥
तत्र यौ तौ महाशृङ्गौ महावर्षमहाहिमौ॥
तृतीयं तु तयोर्मध्ये शृङ्गमत्यन्तमुच्छ्रितम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.152.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / There were two great peaks there, one of heavy rain and one of heavy snow; / but between them was a third peak, exceedingly lofty,

1.152.s:
nityātapaṃ taptaśilaṃ sadā bhagativarjitam ..
tasyādhastādda(?)kṣagaṇe deśe bhāge ca paścime .. 2 ..
1.152.d:
नित्यातपं तप्तशिलं सदा भगतिवर्जितम् ॥
तस्याधस्ताद्द(?)क्षगणे देशे भागे च पश्चिमे ॥ 2 ॥
1.152.m: with perpetual sunshine, hot rocks, and forever free from frost. / Below it, on the southern side and in the western region,

1.152.s:
jātīlatāparikṣiptaṃ vivaraṃ cārudarśanam..
dṛṣṭvaiva kautukāviṣṭastaṃ viveśa mahīpatiḥ..3..
1.152.d:
जातीलतापरिक्षिप्तं विवरं चारुदर्शनम्॥
दृष्ट्वैव कौतुकाविष्टस्तं विवेश महीपतिः॥3॥
1.152.m: surrounded by jasmine creepers, was an opening of beautiful appearance. / As soon as he saw it, filled with curiosity, the ruler of the earth entered it.

1.152.s:
tamasā cātinibiḍaṃ nalvamātraṃ mahīpatiḥ..
nalvamātramatikramya svaprabhābharaṇojvalam .... 4 ..
1.152.d:
तमसा चातिनिबिडं नल्वमात्रं महीपतिः॥
नल्वमात्रमतिक्रम्य स्वप्रभाभरणोज्वलम् ॥॥ 4 ॥
1.152.m: It was exceedingly dense with darkness for just a nalva's distance; / passing beyond just the distance of a nalva, it was bright with the adornment of its own radiance,

1.152.s:
samucchritamathātyantaṃ gambhīraṃ parivartulam ..
na tatra sūryastapati na virājati candramāḥ .. 5 ..
1.152.d:
समुच्छ्रितमथात्यन्तं गम्भीरं परिवर्तुलम् ॥
न तत्र सूर्यस्तपति न विराजति चन्द्रमाः ॥ 5 ॥
1.152.m: exceedingly high, deep, and completely circular. / The sun did not shine there, nor did the moon appear,

1.152.s:
tathāpi divasākāraṃ prākāśyaṃ tadaharniśam ..
krośādhikaparīmāṇaṃ sarasā ca virājitam ..6..
1.152.d:
तथापि दिवसाकारं प्राकाश्यं तदहर्निशम् ॥
क्रोशाधिकपरीमाणं सरसा च विराजितम् ॥6॥
1.152.m: yet day and night it was luminous with the appearance of daylight. / Measuring more than a krośa, it was adorned with a lake;

1.152.s:
samantātsarasastasya śailalagnā tu vedikā..
sauvarṇai rājatairvṛkṣairvidrumairapi śobhitā .. 7 ..
1.152.d:
समन्तात्सरसस्तस्य शैललग्ना तु वेदिका॥
सौवर्णै राजतैर्वृक्षैर्विद्रुमैरपि शोभिता ॥ 7 ॥
1.152.m: all around that lake was an altar-terrace adjoining the mountain, / adorned with golden, silver, and coral trees.

1.152.s:
nānā māṇikyakusumaiḥ svaprabhābharaṇojjvalaiḥ ..
tasminsarasi padmāni padmarāgacchadāni ca .. 8 ..
1.152.d:
नाना माणिक्यकुसुमैः स्वप्रभाभरणोज्ज्वलैः ॥
तस्मिन्सरसि पद्मानि पद्मरागच्छदानि च ॥ 8 ॥
1.152.m: with various ruby blossoms blazing with ornaments of their own luster. / In that lake there are lotuses whose petals are rubies,

1.152.s:
vajrakesarajālāni sugandhīni tathāpyati ..
patrairmarakatairnīlavaidūryaiśca mahīpate .. 9 ..
1.152.d:
वज्रकेसरजालानि सुगन्धीनि तथाप्यति ॥
पत्रैर्मरकतैर्नीलवैदूर्यैश्च महीपते ॥ 9 ॥
1.152.m: whose clusters of filaments are diamonds, yet highly fragrant, / with leaves of emerald, sapphire, and cat's eye, O king,

1.152.s:
karṇikāśca tathāśeṣā jātarūpasya pārthiva ..
tasminsarasi yā bhūmirna sā kardamasaṅkulā .. 1.152.10 ..
1.152.d:
कर्णिकाश्च तथाशेषा जातरूपस्य पार्थिव ॥
तस्मिन्सरसि या भूमिर्न सा कर्दमसङ्कुला ॥ 1.152.10 ॥
1.152.m: and all their pericarps of gold, O ruler of the earth. / The ground in that lake is not mixed with mud;

1.152.s:
nānāratnairupacitā jalajānāṃ samāśrayā ..
kapardakānāṃ śuktīnāṃ śaṅkhānāṃ ca mahīpate .. 11 ..
1.152.d:
नानारत्नैरुपचिता जलजानां समाश्रया ॥
कपर्दकानां शुक्तीनां शङ्खानां च महीपते ॥ 11 ॥
1.152.m: it is heaped with various gems, an abode of water creatures, / of cowries, oysters, and conches, O lord of the earth,

1.152.s:
makarāṇāṃ ca matsyānāṃ paiṇḍānāṃ kacchapaiḥ saha ..
tatra maratakakhaṇḍāni vajrāṇi ca sahasraśaḥ ..12..
1.152.d:
मकराणां च मत्स्यानां पैण्डानां कच्छपैः सह ॥
तत्र मरतकखण्डानि वज्राणि च सहस्रशः ॥12॥
1.152.m: and of sea monsters, fish, shoals of creatures, along with tortoises. / There emerald fragments and diamonds are present by the thousands,

1.152.s:
padmarāgendranīlāni mahānīlāni pārthiva ..
puṣparāgāṇi ramyāṇi tathā karketakāni ca ..13..
1.152.d:
पद्मरागेन्द्रनीलानि महानीलानि पार्थिव ॥
पुष्परागाणि रम्याणि तथा कर्केतकानि च ॥13॥
1.152.m: rubies, sapphires, great sapphires, O ruler of the earth, / lovely topazes, and chrysoberyls,

1.152.s:
turūkasya ca khaṇḍāni tathā śepa(?)sya bhāgaśaḥ ..
gajāvarttasya mukhyasya rudhirākhyasya cāpyatha .. 14 ..
1.152.d:
तुरूकस्य च खण्डानि तथा शेप(?)स्य भागशः ॥
गजावर्त्तस्य मुख्यस्य रुधिराख्यस्य चाप्यथ ॥ 14 ॥
1.152.m: and fragments of turquoise, and portions of jasper(?), / of excellent gajāvarta and of the stone called rudhira,

1.152.s:
sūryendukāntayoścaiva pīlorbhallātakasya ca ..
jyotīrasasya ramyasya śaṅkhakasya ca bhāgaśaḥ .. 15 ..
1.152.d:
सूर्येन्दुकान्तयोश्चैव पीलोर्भल्लातकस्य च ॥
ज्योतीरसस्य रम्यस्य शङ्खकस्य च भागशः ॥ 15 ॥
1.152.m: of sunstone and moonstone, of pīlu and bhallātaka, / of delightful jyotīrasa, and portions of conch-stone,

1.152.s:
masāragavalaṅkānāṃ sphaṭikasya tathaiva ca..
gomedapittakānāṃ ca dhūlī marakatasya ca .. 16..
1.152.d:
मसारगवलङ्कानां स्फटिकस्य तथैव च॥
गोमेदपित्तकानां च धूली मरकतस्य च ॥ 16॥
1.152.m: of masāra, buffalo horn, and likewise of crystal, / of hessonite and gall-stones, and dust of emerald,

1.152.s:
vaidūryasaugandhikayostathā rājamaṇernṛpa ..
khañjasya caiva mukhyasya tathā brahmamaṇerapi ..17..
1.152.d:
वैदूर्यसौगन्धिकयोस्तथा राजमणेर्नृप ॥
खञ्जस्य चैव मुख्यस्य तथा ब्रह्ममणेरपि ॥17॥
1.152.m: of cat's eye and saugandhika, and also of rājamaṇi, O king, / of the excellent khañja, and also of brahmamaṇi,

1.152.s:
muktāphalānāṃ mukhyānāṃ tārāvigrahadhāriṇām ..
sukhoṣṇaṃ caiva tattoyaṃ snānācchītavināśanam ..18..
1.152.d:
मुक्ताफलानां मुख्यानां ताराविग्रहधारिणाम् ॥
सुखोष्णं चैव तत्तोयं स्नानाच्छीतविनाशनम् ॥18॥
1.152.m: and of excellent pearls bearing the appearance of stars. / And that water is pleasantly warm, dispelling cold through bathing.

1.152.s:
vaidūryasya śilāmadhye sarasastasya śobhanā..
pramāṇena tathā sā ca dve ca rājandhanuḥśate..19..
1.152.d:
वैदूर्यस्य शिलामध्ये सरसस्तस्य शोभना॥
प्रमाणेन तथा सा च द्वे च राजन्धनुःशते॥19॥
1.152.m: In the middle of that lake is a splendid slab of cat's eye; / and it measures, O king, two hundred bows [in length],

1.152.s:
caturasrā tathā ramyā tapasā nirmitātriṇā ..
biladvārasame deśe ketustatra hiraṇmayaḥ ..1.152.20..
1.152.d:
चतुरस्रा तथा रम्या तपसा निर्मितात्रिणा ॥
बिलद्वारसमे देशे केतुस्तत्र हिरण्मयः ॥1.152.20॥
1.152.m: square, delightful, fashioned by Atri through ascetic power. / In a place level with the entrance to the cave, there stands a golden standard.

1.152.s:
pradeśaḥ sa tu rājendra dvīpe tasminmanohare ..
tathā puṣkariṇī ramyā tasminrājañchilātale ..21..
1.152.d:
प्रदेशः स तु राजेन्द्र द्वीपे तस्मिन्मनोहरे ॥
तथा पुष्करिणी रम्या तस्मिन्राजञ्छिलातले ॥21॥
1.152.m: That region, O best of kings, is upon that charming island. / Likewise there is a delightful lotus pond, O king, upon that rock surface,

1.152.s:
suśītāmalapānīyā jalajaiśca virājitā ..
ākāśavimalā rājaṃścaturasrā manoharā .. 22 ..
1.152.d:
सुशीतामलपानीया जलजैश्च विराजिता ॥
आकाशविमला राजंश्चतुरस्रा मनोहरा ॥ 22 ॥
1.152.m: with very cool, pure water, adorned with lotuses, / pure as the sky, O king, four-cornered and delightful.

1.152.s:
tasyāstadudakaṃ svādu laghu śītaṃ sugandhi ca ..
na kṣiṇoti tathā kāyaṃ kukṣimāpūrayatyapi ..23..
1.152.d:
तस्यास्तदुदकं स्वादु लघु शीतं सुगन्धि च ॥
न क्षिणोति तथा कायं कुक्षिमापूरयत्यपि ॥23॥
1.152.m: Its water is sweet, light, cool, and fragrant; / it does not emaciate the body, and it fills the belly;

1.152.s:
tṛptiṃ vidhatte paramāṃ śarīre ca mahatsukham ..
madhye ca tasyāḥ sukṛtaṃ prāsādaṃ tapasātriṇā .. 24 ..
1.152.d:
तृप्तिं विधत्ते परमां शरीरे च महत्सुखम् ॥
मध्ये च तस्याः सुकृतं प्रासादं तपसात्रिणा ॥ 24 ॥
1.152.m: it produces supreme contentment and great comfort in the body. / In the middle of it is a well-made temple fashioned by Atri through ascetic power,

1.152.s:
rukmasetupraveśaṃ tatsarvaratnamayaṃ śubham ..
śaśāṅkaraśmisaṅkāśaṃ prāsādaṃ rājataṃ hitam ..25..
1.152.d:
रुक्मसेतुप्रवेशं तत्सर्वरत्नमयं शुभम् ॥
शशाङ्करश्मिसङ्काशं प्रासादं राजतं हितम् ॥25॥
1.152.m: approached by an entrance bridge of gold, auspicious and made of every gem, / a beneficial silver temple resembling the rays of the moon,

1.152.s:
ramyaṃ vaidūryasopānaṃ vidrumāmalatārakam ..
indranīlamahācakrañjātarūpavibhūṣitam..26..
1.152.d:
रम्यं वैदूर्यसोपानं विद्रुमामलतारकम् ॥
इन्द्रनीलमहाचक्रञ्जातरूपविभूषितम्॥26॥
1.152.m: with delightful steps of cat's eye and spotless studs of coral, / having a great discus of sapphire adorned with gold,

1.152.s:
padmarāgamahāstaṃbhaṃ tathā marakatavedikam ..
vajrāṃśujālaiśchuritaṃ ramyaṃ dṛṣṭimanoharam ..27..
1.152.d:
पद्मरागमहास्तंभं तथा मरकतवेदिकम् ॥
वज्रांशुजालैश्छुरितं रम्यं दृष्टिमनोहरम् ॥27॥
1.152.m: with great pillars of ruby and a pedestal of emerald, / inlaid with webs of diamond rays, delightful and charming to the sight.

1.152.s:
prāsāde tatra bhagavāndevadevo janārdanaḥ ..
bhogibhogāvalīsuptaḥ sarvālaṅkārabhūṣitaḥ .. 28 ..
1.152.d:
प्रासादे तत्र भगवान्देवदेवो जनार्दनः ॥
भोगिभोगावलीसुप्तः सर्वालङ्कारभूषितः ॥ 28 ॥
1.152.m: In that temple, the blessed God of gods, Janārdana, / is asleep upon the coils of the serpent, adorned with all ornaments.

1.152.s:
jānumākuñcitastvekaṃ devadevasya cakriṇaḥ ..
phaṇīndrasanniviṣṭāṃghri dvitīyaśca tathā nṛpa .. 29 ..
1.152.d:
जानुमाकुञ्चितस्त्वेकं देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः ॥
फणीन्द्रसन्निविष्टांघ्रि द्वितीयश्च तथा नृप ॥ 29 ॥
1.152.m: One knee of the God of gods who holds the discus is bent, / and His second foot rests upon the king of serpents, O king;

1.152.s:
lakṣmyutsaṅgagatāṃghristu śeṣabhogaprasāritaḥ ..
phaṇīndrabhogavinyastabāhukūrparaśobhitaḥ .. 1.152.30 ..
1.152.d:
लक्ष्म्युत्सङ्गगतांघ्रिस्तु शेषभोगप्रसारितः ॥
फणीन्द्रभोगविन्यस्तबाहुकूर्परशोभितः ॥ 1.152.30 ॥
1.152.m: the [other] foot is placed in Lakṣmī's lap, extended along the serpent's coil; / He is adorned with His arm and elbow resting on the coils of the serpent king,

1.152.s:
svāṅgulīpṛṣṭhavinyasta devaśīrṣadharaṃ vibhum..
ekaṃ tu devadevasya dvitīyaṃ saṃprasāritam .. 31 ..
1.152.d:
स्वाङ्गुलीपृष्ठविन्यस्त देवशीर्षधरं विभुम्॥
एकं तु देवदेवस्य द्वितीयं संप्रसारितम् ॥ 31 ॥
1.152.m: the all-pervading Lord supporting His divine head placed upon the back of His fingers. / One [arm] of the God of gods is extended,

1.152.s:
samākuñcitajānusthamaṇibandhasuśobhitam ..
kiñcidākuñcitaṃ caiva nābhideśe karasthitam ..32..
1.152.d:
समाकुञ्चितजानुस्थमणिबन्धसुशोभितम् ॥
किञ्चिदाकुञ्चितं चैव नाभिदेशे करस्थितम् ॥32॥
1.152.m: splendid with its wrist placed on the bent knee; / slightly bent, His hand rests in the region of His navel.

1.152.s:
tṛtīyaṃ ca bhujaṃ tasya caturthaṃ tu tathā śṛṇu ..
āttasantānakusumaṃ prāṇadeśānusarpiṇam ..33..
1.152.d:
तृतीयं च भुजं तस्य चतुर्थं तु तथा शृणु ॥
आत्तसन्तानकुसुमं प्राणदेशानुसर्पिणम् ॥33॥
1.152.m: That is His third arm; now hear of the fourth: / holding a Santāna blossom, moving toward the region of His heart.

1.152.s:
lakṣmyā saṃvāhyamānāṃghriḥ phullapadmanibhaiḥ karaiḥ ..
santānamālāmukuṭahārakeyūrabhūṣitam.. 34 ..
1.152.d:
लक्ष्म्या संवाह्यमानांघ्रिः फुल्लपद्मनिभैः करैः ॥
सन्तानमालामुकुटहारकेयूरभूषितम्॥ 34 ॥
1.152.m: His feet are massaged by Lakṣmī with hands like blooming lotuses; / He is adorned with a garland of Santāna flowers, a diadem, a necklace, and armlets;

1.152.s:
bhūṣitaṃ ca tathā devamaṅgulīyakaiḥ ..
phaṇīndraphaṇavinyastacāruratnaśikhojjvalam .. 35 ..
1.152.d:
भूषितं च तथा देवमङ्गुलीयकैः ॥
फणीन्द्रफणविन्यस्तचारुरत्नशिखोज्ज्वलम् ॥ 35 ॥
1.152.m: and the God is adorned with rings, / radiant with the crested jewels of lovely gems placed on the hoods of the serpent king,

1.152.s:
ajñātavastucaritaṃ pratiṣṭhitamathātriṇā ..
siddhāntapūjyaṃ satataṃ samantātkusumārcitam..36..
1.152.d:
अज्ञातवस्तुचरितं प्रतिष्ठितमथात्रिणा ॥
सिद्धान्तपूज्यं सततं समन्तात्कुसुमार्चितम्॥36॥
1.152.m: whose real nature and deeds are unknown, consecrated there by Atri, / ever worthy of worship according to Siddhānta, worshipped all around with flowers,

1.152.s:
divyagandhāvaliptāṅgaṃ divyadhūpena dhūpitam ..
gorasaiḥ saphalairhṛdyaiḥ siddhairupahṛtaiḥ sadā .. 37 ..
1.152.d:
दिव्यगन्धावलिप्ताङ्गं दिव्यधूपेन धूपितम् ॥
गोरसैः सफलैर्हृद्यैः सिद्धैरुपहृतैः सदा ॥ 37 ॥
1.152.m: His limbs anointed with divine fragrant paste, perfumed with divine incense, / and with delightful dairy foods accompanied by fruits, continually offered by the Siddhas.

1.152.s:
saṃśobhitaṃ puraḥpārśvaṃ devamuttamaśīrṣakam..
tathā paścānmukhaṃ dṛṣṭvā vavande sa narādhipaḥ ..38..
1.152.d:
संशोभितं पुरःपार्श्वं देवमुत्तमशीर्षकम्॥
तथा पश्चान्मुखं दृष्ट्वा ववन्दे स नराधिपः ॥38॥
1.152.m: Having seen the God adorned in front and at the sides, with His supreme head / and His face turned toward the west, the ruler of men bowed down.

1.152.s:
jānubhyāṃ śirasā caiva gatvā bhūmiṃ yathāvidhi ..
nāmnāṃ sahasreṇa tathā tuṣṭāva madhusūdanam .. 39 ..
1.152.d:
जानुभ्यां शिरसा चैव गत्वा भूमिं यथाविधि ॥
नाम्नां सहस्रेण तथा तुष्टाव मधुसूदनम् ॥ 39 ॥
1.152.m: Having touched the ground according to rule with his knees and head, / he praised Madhusūdana with the thousand names.

1.152.s:
pradakṣiṇamatho cakre sa tūtthāya punaḥ punaḥ ..
ramyamāyatanaṃ dṛṣṭvā tatrovāsāśrame nṛpaḥ .. 1.152.40 ..
1.152.d:
प्रदक्षिणमथो चक्रे स तूत्थाय पुनः पुनः ॥
रम्यमायतनं दृष्ट्वा तत्रोवासाश्रमे नृपः ॥ 1.152.40 ॥
1.152.m: Then, rising up again and again, he performed circumambulation. / Having seen that delightful abode, the king dwelt there in the hermitage,

1.152.s:
viśālāṃ hi guhāṃ kāñcidāśritya sumanoharām ..
tapaścacāra tatraiva pūjayāno janārdanam ..41..
1.152.d:
विशालां हि गुहां काञ्चिदाश्रित्य सुमनोहराम् ॥
तपश्चचार तत्रैव पूजयानो जनार्दनम् ॥41॥
1.152.m: having taken shelter in a spacious, most delightful cave. / He performed austerities right there, worshipping Janārdana

1.152.s:
nānāvidhaiḥ sadā puṣpaiḥ phalairmūlaiḥ sagorasaiḥ ..
nityaṃ triṣavaṇasnāyī vahnipūjāparāyaṇaḥ .. 42 ..
1.152.d:
नानाविधैः सदा पुष्पैः फलैर्मूलैः सगोरसैः ॥
नित्यं त्रिषवणस्नायी वह्निपूजापरायणः ॥ 42 ॥
1.152.m: always with flowers of various kinds, with fruits, roots, and dairy foods, / constantly bathing at the three junctures of the day, devoted to the worship of fire,

1.152.s:
devavāpījalaiḥ kurvansatataṃ prāṇadhāraṇam ..
sarvāhāraparityāgaṃ sa kṛtvā manujeśvaraḥ .. 43 ..
1.152.d:
देववापीजलैः कुर्वन्सततं प्राणधारणम् ॥
सर्वाहारपरित्यागं स कृत्वा मनुजेश्वरः ॥ 43 ॥
1.152.m: always sustaining his life with the waters of the divine pond. / Having abandoned all food, the lord of men,

1.152.s:
anāśritaguhāśāyī kālaṃ nayati pārthivaḥ ..
tyaktāhārakriyasyāsya kevalāmbho'śinastathā ..
glānistasya samāyāti na śarīre tadadbhutam ..44..
1.152.d:
अनाश्रितगुहाशायी कालं नयति पार्थिवः ॥
त्यक्ताहारक्रियस्यास्य केवलाम्भोऽशिनस्तथा ॥
ग्लानिस्तस्य समायाति न शरीरे तदद्भुतम् ॥44॥
1.152.m: sleeping in that unbuilt cave, passed his time, the ruler of the earth. / Although he had given up the practice of eating and consumed only water, / no exhaustion came upon his body—that was a wonder.

1.152.s:
evaṃ sa rājā tapasi prasaktaḥ sampūjayandevavaraṃ sadaiva ..
tatrāśrame kālamuvāsa kaścitsvargopame duḥkhamavindamānaḥ .. 45..
1.152.d:
एवं स राजा तपसि प्रसक्तः सम्पूजयन्देववरं सदैव ॥
तत्राश्रमे कालमुवास कश्चित्स्वर्गोपमे दुःखमविन्दमानः ॥ 45॥
1.152.m: Thus that king, intent on ascetic practice, constantly worshipping the supreme God, / lived for some time in that hermitage resembling heaven, experiencing no sorrow.

1.153.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
gatvāśramapade rājā tyaktāhāraparicchadaḥ ..
krīḍāvihārairgandharvaiḥ paśyatyapsarasassaha .. 1 ..
1.153.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
गत्वाश्रमपदे राजा त्यक्ताहारपरिच्छदः ॥
क्रीडाविहारैर्गन्धर्वैः पश्यत्यप्सरसस्सह ॥ 1 ॥
1.153.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having gone to the hermitage site, the king, having abandoned food and retinue, / watched the apsarases along with the gandharvas engaged in sportive amusements.

1.153.s:
kṛtvā puṣpoccayaṃ bhūri grathayitvā tathā srajaḥ ..
agre nivedya devāya gandharvebhyastathā dadau ..2 ..
1.153.d:
कृत्वा पुष्पोच्चयं भूरि ग्रथयित्वा तथा स्रजः ॥
अग्रे निवेद्य देवाय गन्धर्वेभ्यस्तथा ददौ ॥2 ॥
1.153.m: Gathering an abundance of flowers and weaving garlands, / having offered them first to the God, he then gave them to the gandharvas.

1.153.s:
puṣpoccayaprasaktānāṃ krīḍantīnāṃ yathāsukham ..
ceṣṭā nānāvidhākārāḥ paśyannapi na paśyati .. 3 ..
1.153.d:
पुष्पोच्चयप्रसक्तानां क्रीडन्तीनां यथासुखम् ॥
चेष्टा नानाविधाकाराः पश्यन्नपि न पश्यति ॥ 3 ॥
1.153.m: Though looking at the various forms of activities / of those women intent on gathering flowers and playing at their ease, he did not [really] see them:

1.153.s:
kāścitpuṣpoccaye saktā latājālena veṣṭitāḥ ..
sakhījanena santyaktāḥ kāntena paramokṣitāḥ .. 4 ..
1.153.d:
काश्चित्पुष्पोच्चये सक्ता लताजालेन वेष्टिताः ॥
सखीजनेन सन्त्यक्ताः कान्तेन परमोक्षिताः ॥ 4 ॥
1.153.m: some engaged in gathering flowers were caught in a thicket of creepers; / left behind by their companions, they were freed by their lovers;

1.153.s:
makarandasamākrāntanayanāḥ kāścidaṅganāḥ ..
kāntaniḥśvāsavātena nīrajaskīkṛtekṣaṇāḥ .. 5 ..
1.153.d:
मकरन्दसमाक्रान्तनयनाः काश्चिदङ्गनाः ॥
कान्तनिःश्वासवातेन नीरजस्कीकृतेक्षणाः ॥ 5 ॥
1.153.m: the eyes of some women were clouded with floral nectar; / their eyes were cleared of dust by the breath of their lovers.

1.153.s:
kāciduccitya puṣpāṇi dadau kāntasya bhāminī ..
kāntasaḍgrathitaistaiśca rarāja kṛtaśekharā .. 6 ..
1.153.d:
काचिदुच्चित्य पुष्पाणि ददौ कान्तस्य भामिनी ॥
कान्तसड्ग्रथितैस्तैश्च रराज कृतशेखरा ॥ 6 ॥
1.153.m: One passionate woman, having gathered flowers, gave them to her lover; / and she shone, wearing a chaplet woven from them by her beloved.

1.153.s:
svayamuccitya saṅgranthya ramaṇakṛtaśekharā ..
kṛtakṛtyamivā''tmānaṃ mene manmathavardhinī .. 7 ..
1.153.d:
स्वयमुच्चित्य सङ्ग्रन्थ्य रमणकृतशेखरा ॥
कृतकृत्यमिवा'ऽत्मानं मेने मन्मथवर्धिनी ॥ 7 ॥
1.153.m: Having gathered and strung them herself, her crest made by her beloved, / that woman, increasing desire, considered herself to have accomplished her purpose.

1.153.s:
anyasmingahane kuñje viśeṣakusumā latā ..
kācidevaṃ raho nītā ramaṇena riraṃsunā .. 8 ..
1.153.d:
अन्यस्मिन्गहने कुञ्जे विशेषकुसुमा लता ॥
काचिदेवं रहो नीता रमणेन रिरंसुना ॥ 8 ॥
1.153.m: In another dense bower, a certain creeper bore extraordinary blossoms; / one woman was led thither in secret by her lover eager for pleasure.

1.153.s:
kāntasannāmitalatākusumāni vicinvatī ..
sarvābhyaḥ kācidātmānaṃ mene sarvaguṇādhikam .. 9 ..
1.153.d:
कान्तसन्नामितलताकुसुमानि विचिन्वती ॥
सर्वाभ्यः काचिदात्मानं मेने सर्वगुणाधिकम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.153.m: Gathering flowers from a creeper bent down by her beloved, / a certain woman considered herself superior in all virtues to all [the others].

1.153.s:
kvacitpaśyati bhūpālo nalinīṣu pṛthakpṛthak ..
krīḍyamānāstu gandharvaidaivarāmā manoramāḥ .. 1.153.10 ..
1.153.d:
क्वचित्पश्यति भूपालो नलिनीषु पृथक्पृथक् ॥
क्रीड्यमानास्तु गन्धर्वैदैवरामा मनोरमाः ॥ 1.153.10 ॥
1.153.m: Here and there the king saw, in the lotus pools, / delightful divine damsels sporting separately with the Gandharvas.

1.153.s:
kāciccātāḍayatkāntamudakena śucismitā ..
tāḍyamānā tathaivānyā kāntena ratimāyayau .. 11 ..
1.153.d:
काचिच्चाताडयत्कान्तमुदकेन शुचिस्मिता ॥
ताड्यमाना तथैवान्या कान्तेन रतिमाययौ ॥ 11 ॥
1.153.m: A woman of bright smiles struck her lover with water; / another, struck likewise by her lover, felt sexual delight.

1.153.s:
kāntā tu tāḍayāmāsa jātakhedā varāṅganā ..
adṛśyata varārohā śvāsanṛtyatpayodharā .. 12 ..
1.153.d:
कान्ता तु ताडयामास जातखेदा वराङ्गना ॥
अदृश्यत वरारोहा श्वासनृत्यत्पयोधरा ॥ 12 ॥
1.153.m: Becoming fatigued, an excellent maiden struck back at her lover; / that fair-hipped woman was seen with breasts dancing as she breathed.

1.153.s:
kāntāmbutāḍana bhraṣṭakeśapāśanibandhanā ..
śvāsākulamukhī bhāti madhupairiva padminī .. 13 ..
1.153.d:
कान्ताम्बुताडन भ्रष्टकेशपाशनिबन्धना ॥
श्वासाकुलमुखी भाति मधुपैरिव पद्मिनी ॥ 13 ॥
1.153.m: With the binding of her hair-braid loosened by the lover striking her with water, / her face agitated by breath, she shone like a lotus pool [encircled] by bees.

1.153.s:
svavaktrasadṛśaiḥ puṣpaiḥ saṃchannanalinīvane ..
channā kāciccirātprāptā kāntenānviṣya yatnataḥ .. 14 ..
1.153.d:
स्ववक्त्रसदृशैः पुष्पैः संछन्ननलिनीवने ॥
छन्ना काचिच्चिरात्प्राप्ता कान्तेनान्विष्य यत्नतः ॥ 14 ॥
1.153.m: In a lotus clump covered with flowers resembling her face, / one woman who had concealed herself was found after a long time by her lover searching diligently.

1.153.s:
snātā śītāpadeśena kācitprauḍhāṅganā bhṛśam ..
ramaṇāliṅganaṃ cakre manobhi'laṣitaṃ ciram .. 15 ..
1.153.d:
स्नाता शीतापदेशेन काचित्प्रौढाङ्गना भृशम् ॥
रमणालिङ्गनं चक्रे मनोभिऽलषितं चिरम् ॥ 15 ॥
1.153.m: A certain mature woman, having bathed, on the pretext of feeling cold, / embraced her lover intensely, as she had long desired in her heart.

1.153.s:
jalārdraṃ vasanaṃ sūkṣmamaṅgalīnaṃ śucismitā ..
dhārayantī janaṃ cakre kācittatra samanmatham ..16..
1.153.d:
जलार्द्रं वसनं सूक्ष्ममङ्गलीनं शुचिस्मिता ॥
धारयन्ती जनं चक्रे काचित्तत्र समन्मथम् ॥16॥
1.153.m: Wearing a fine garment, wet with water and clinging to her limbs, / a woman of bright smiles aroused desire in a man there.

1.153.s:
gandhamālyaguṇaiḥ kācitkānttenākṛṣya cāmbhasi ..
truṭyatsragdāmapatitaṃ ramaṇaṃ prāhasacciram ..17..
1.153.d:
गन्धमाल्यगुणैः काचित्कान्त्तेनाकृष्य चाम्भसि ॥
त्रुट्यत्स्रग्दामपतितं रमणं प्राहसच्चिरम् ॥17॥
1.153.m: Having pulled her lover into the water by strings of fragrant garlands, / a woman laughed for a long time at her beloved who had fallen as the garland broke.

1.153.s:
kācinmagnasakhīdattajānudeśanakhakṣatā ..
sambhramātkāntaramaṇamagnā sāpi nyamajjata .. 18 ..
1.153.d:
काचिन्मग्नसखीदत्तजानुदेशनखक्षता ॥
सम्भ्रमात्कान्तरमणमग्ना सापि न्यमज्जत ॥ 18 ॥
1.153.m: A woman, scratched on the knee by the nails of her friend who had submerged, / plunged [him] in agitation, and, having sunk down, submerged her beloved as well.

1.153.s:
kācitpṛṣṭhīkṛtādityā keśanistoyakāriṇī ..
śilātalagatā bhartrā dṛṣṭā kāmārtacakṣuṣā ..19..
1.153.d:
काचित्पृष्ठीकृतादित्या केशनिस्तोयकारिणी ॥
शिलातलगता भर्त्रा दृष्टा कामार्तचक्षुषा ॥19॥
1.153.m: A woman who had turned her back to the sun, squeezing water from her hair / while sitting on a flat rock, was gazed upon by her husband with eyes full of desire.

1.153.s:
hṛtamālyaṃ sulalitaṃ saṃkrāntakucakuṅkumam ..
ratāntaklāntakāntābhamabhavattatsarodakam ..1.153.20..
1.153.d:
हृतमाल्यं सुललितं संक्रान्तकुचकुङ्कुमम् ॥
रतान्तक्लान्तकान्ताभमभवत्तत्सरोदकम् ॥1.153.20॥
1.153.m: With garlands carried away, charmingly lovely, smeared with saffron from breasts, / the water of that lake came to resemble a beloved exhausted after lovemaking.

1.153.s:
susnātadevagandharvadevarāmāgaṇena ca ..
pūjyamānaṃ sa dadṛśe devadevaṃ janārdanam .. 21 ..
1.153.d:
सुस्नातदेवगन्धर्वदेवरामागणेन च ॥
पूज्यमानं स ददृशे देवदेवं जनार्दनम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.153.m: He saw the god of gods, Janārdana, being worshipped / by a host of well-bathed gods, Gandharvas, and divine women.

1.153.s:
kvacicca dadṛśe rājā latāgṛhagatāḥ striyaḥ ..
maṇḍayantyaḥ svagātrāṇi kāntasanyastamānasāḥ ..22..
1.153.d:
क्वचिच्च ददृशे राजा लतागृहगताः स्त्रियः ॥
मण्डयन्त्यः स्वगात्राणि कान्तसन्यस्तमानसाः ॥22॥
1.153.m: And here and there the king saw women in creepers' bowers / adorning their limbs, their minds fixed on their lovers.

1.153.s:
kācidādarśasuvyagrakarā dūtīmukhodgatam ..
śṛṇvatī kāntavacanamatiklāntamukhā babhau ..23 ..
1.153.d:
काचिदादर्शसुव्यग्रकरा दूतीमुखोद्गतम् ॥
शृण्वती कान्तवचनमतिक्लान्तमुखा बभौ ॥23 ॥
1.153.m: A woman whose hands were occupied with a mirror, listening / to the beloved's words spoken through the mouth of a female messenger, shone with an intensely weary face.

1.153.s:
kācitsatvaritā dūtyā bhūṣaṇānāṃ viparyayam ..
kurvāṇā naiva bubudhe manmathāviṣṭacetanā .. 24 ..
1.153.d:
काचित्सत्वरिता दूत्या भूषणानां विपर्ययम् ॥
कुर्वाणा नैव बुबुधे मन्मथाविष्टचेतना ॥ 24 ॥
1.153.m: A woman, hurried along by a messenger, / putting on her ornaments in reverse order, was not even aware of it, her mind seized by love.

1.153.s:
vāyununnāṃtasurabhi kusumotkaramaṇḍite ..
kvacitpibantyo dadṛśe pradeśe nīlaśādvale ..29.
1.153.d:
वायुनुन्नांतसुरभि कुसुमोत्करमण्डिते ॥
क्वचित्पिबन्त्यो ददृशे प्रदेशे नीलशाद्वले ॥29.
1.153.m: In some spot, on green turf adorned with heaps of fragrant flowers / carried along by the wind, [women] were seen drinking.

1.153.s:
pāyayāmāsa ramaṇaṃ svayaṃ kācidvarāṅganā ..
kācitpapau varārohā kāntapāṇi samarpitam..26..
1.153.d:
पाययामास रमणं स्वयं काचिद्वराङ्गना ॥
काचित्पपौ वरारोहा कान्तपाणि समर्पितम्॥26॥
1.153.m: A fair maiden herself made her lover drink; / another shapely-hipped woman drank what was offered from her beloved's hand.

1.153.s:
kācitsvanetrasaṃkrāntanīlotpalayutaṃ vadhūḥ..
pītvā papraccha ramaṇaṃ kva gate te mahotpale..27..
1.153.d:
काचित्स्वनेत्रसंक्रान्तनीलोत्पलयुतं वधूः॥
पीत्वा पप्रच्छ रमणं क्व गते ते महोत्पले॥27॥
1.153.m: A young bride, drinking [wine] reflected with her own eyes as blue lotuses, / asked her beloved, "Where have your two great lotuses gone?"

1.153.s:
tvayaiva pīte te nūnamityuktā ramaṇena sā ..
satyaṃ viditvā mugdhatvādbabhūva vrīḍitā ciram ..28..
1.153.d:
त्वयैव पीते ते नूनमित्युक्ता रमणेन सा ॥
सत्यं विदित्वा मुग्धत्वाद्बभूव व्रीडिता चिरम् ॥28॥
1.153.m: Told by her lover, "Surely they have been drunk by you alone," / and believing it to be true out of innocence, she became bashful for a long time.

1.153.s:
kācitkāntārpitaṃ subhrūḥ kāntapītāvaśeṣitam ..
saviśeṣarasaṃ pānaṃ papau manmathavardhanam..29..
1.153.d:
काचित्कान्तार्पितं सुभ्रूः कान्तपीतावशेषितम् ॥
सविशेषरसं पानं पपौ मन्मथवर्धनम्॥29॥
1.153.m: A fair-browed woman drank the beverage offered by her lover, left over after he drank, / possessing an extraordinary flavor and increasing desire.

1.153.s:
āpānagoṣṭhīṣu tadā tāsāṃ sa narapuṅgavaḥ ..
śuśrāva vividhaṃ gītaṃ tantrīsvaravimiśritam .. 1.153.30 ..
1.153.d:
आपानगोष्ठीषु तदा तासां स नरपुङ्गवः ॥
शुश्राव विविधं गीतं तन्त्रीस्वरविमिश्रितम् ॥ 1.153.30 ॥
1.153.m: Then, in their drinking assemblies, that bull among men / heard various songs mixed with the music of stringed instruments.

1.153.s:
pradoṣasamaye tāśca devadevaṃ janārdanam ..
rājansadopanṛtyanti nānāvādyapuraḥsarāḥ .. 31..
1.153.d:
प्रदोषसमये ताश्च देवदेवं जनार्दनम् ॥
राजन्सदोपनृत्यन्ति नानावाद्यपुरःसराः ॥ 31॥
1.153.m: At twilight, O king, those [women] continually dance before / the god of gods, Janārdana, accompanied by various musical instruments.

1.153.s:
yāmamātre gate rātrau vinirgatya guhāmukhāt ..
āyānti saṃyutāḥ kāntaiḥ svaṛddhiracitāngṛhān ..32..
1.153.d:
याममात्रे गते रात्रौ विनिर्गत्य गुहामुखात् ॥
आयान्ति संयुताः कान्तैः स्वऋद्धिरचितान्गृहान् ॥32॥
1.153.m: When only one watch of the night has passed, emerging from the mouth of the cave, / they go with their lovers to their houses built with their own supernatural powers,

1.153.s:
nānāgandhārcitatalānnānāgandhasugandhinaḥ ..
nānāvicitraśayanānkusumotkaramaṇḍitān .. 33 ..
1.153.d:
नानागन्धार्चिततलान्नानागन्धसुगन्धिनः ॥
नानाविचित्रशयनान्कुसुमोत्करमण्डितान् ॥ 33 ॥
1.153.m: whose floors are sprinkled with various perfumes, fragrant with different scents, / having diverse, wondrous couches adorned with heaps of flowers.

1.153.s:
evamapsarasāṃ paśyankrīḍitāni sa parvate ..
tapastepe mahārājaḥ keśavārpitamānasaḥ .. 34 ..
1.153.d:
एवमप्सरसां पश्यन्क्रीडितानि स पर्वते ॥
तपस्तेपे महाराजः केशवार्पितमानसः ॥ 34 ॥
1.153.m: Watching thus the sports of the Apsarases on the mountain, / the great king practiced austerities, his mind devoted to Keśava.

1.153.s:
tamūcurnṛpatiṃ gatvā gandharvāpsaraṇāṃ gaṇāḥ ..
rājansvargopamaṃ deśaṃ prāptastvamarimardana .. 35..
1.153.d:
तमूचुर्नृपतिं गत्वा गन्धर्वाप्सरणां गणाः ॥
राजन्स्वर्गोपमं देशं प्राप्तस्त्वमरिमर्दन ॥ 35॥
1.153.m: Approaching that king, hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases spoke to him: / "O King, crusher of foes, you have reached a realm equal to heaven.

1.153.s:
vayaṃ hi te pradāsyāmo manasaḥ kāṅkṣitānvarān ..
tānādāya gṛhaṃ gaccha tiṣṭheha yadi vā punaḥ .. 36 ..
1.153.d:
वयं हि ते प्रदास्यामो मनसः काङ्क्षितान्वरान् ॥
तानादाय गृहं गच्छ तिष्ठेह यदि वा पुनः ॥ 36 ॥
1.153.m: We will grant you boons desired by your mind; / take them and go home, or else remain here."

1.153.s:
purūravā uvāca..
amoghadarśanāḥ sarve bhavantastvamitaujasaḥ ..
varaṃ vitarādyaiva prasādaṃ madhusūdanāt .. 37 ..
1.153.d:
पुरूरवा उवाच॥
अमोघदर्शनाः सर्वे भवन्तस्त्वमितौजसः ॥
वरं वितराद्यैव प्रसादं मधुसूदनात् ॥ 37 ॥
1.153.m: Purūravas said: / "All of you are beings whose sight is never fruitless, possessed of unmeasured splendor; / grant today as a boon the grace of Madhusūdana."

1.153.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evamastvityathoktastaiḥ sa tu rājā purūravāḥ ..
tatrovāsa sukhī māsaṃ pūjayāno janārdanam .. 38 ..
1.153.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवमस्त्वित्यथोक्तस्तैः स तु राजा पुरूरवाः ॥
तत्रोवास सुखी मासं पूजयानो जनार्दनम् ॥ 38 ॥
1.153.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Addressed by them with "So be it," King Purūravas / dwelt there happily for a month, worshipping Janārdana.

1.153.s:
priya eva sadaivāsīdgandharvāpsarasāṃ nṛpa ..
tutoṣa sa jano rājñastasyālaulyena karmaṇā .. 39 ..
1.153.d:
प्रिय एव सदैवासीद्गन्धर्वाप्सरसां नृप ॥
तुतोष स जनो राज्ञस्तस्यालौल्येन कर्मणा ॥ 39 ॥
1.153.m: He was always dear to the Gandharvas and Apsarases, O king; / those people were pleased with the king on account of his ungreedy conduct.

1.153.s:
maghasya madhye sa nṛpaḥ praviṣṭastadāśramaṃ ratnasahasracitram..
toyāśanastatra uvāsa māsaṃ yāvatsitāntaṃ nṛpa phālgunasya .. 1.153.40 ..
1.153.d:
मघस्य मध्ये स नृपः प्रविष्टस्तदाश्रमं रत्नसहस्रचित्रम्॥
तोयाशनस्तत्र उवास मासं यावत्सितान्तं नृप फाल्गुनस्य ॥ 1.153.40 ॥
1.153.m: In the middle of Māgha, that king entered that hermitage wondrous with thousands of jewels; / living on water, he dwelt there for a month, until the end of the bright fortnight of Phālguna, O king.

1.154.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
phālgunāmalapakṣānte rājā svapne purūravāḥ ..
tasyaiva devadevasya śuśrāva gaditaṃ śubham ..1..
1.154.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
फाल्गुनामलपक्षान्ते राजा स्वप्ने पुरूरवाः ॥
तस्यैव देवदेवस्य शुश्राव गदितं शुभम् ॥1॥
1.154.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / At the end of the bright fortnight of Phālguna, King Purūravas in a dream / heard an auspicious proclamation of that very god of gods:

1.154.s:
rātryāmasyāṃ vyatītāyāṃ mantriṇā tvaṃ sameṣyasi..
tena rājansamāgamya kṛtakṛtyo bhaviṣyasi .. 2..
1.154.d:
रात्र्यामस्यां व्यतीतायां मन्त्रिणा त्वं समेष्यसि॥
तेन राजन्समागम्य कृतकृत्यो भविष्यसि ॥ 2॥
1.154.m: "When this night has passed, you will meet with your minister; / having met with him, O king, you will achieve your purpose."

1.154.s:
svapnamevaṃ sa rājarṣirdṛṣṭvā vipulavikramaḥ ..
pratyūṣakāle vidhivatsnātaḥ prāgvadatandritaḥ .. 3 ..
1.154.d:
स्वप्नमेवं स राजर्षिर्दृष्ट्वा विपुलविक्रमः ॥
प्रत्यूषकाले विधिवत्स्नातः प्राग्वदतन्द्रितः ॥ 3 ॥
1.154.m: Having seen such a dream, that royal sage of vast prowess, / diligently bathed at dawn according to rule, as before.

1.154.s:
kṛtakṛtyo yathākāmaṃ pūjayitvā janārdanam ..
svapnaṃ taddevadevasya nyavedayata dhārmikaḥ .. 4 ..
1.154.d:
कृतकृत्यो यथाकामं पूजयित्वा जनार्दनम् ॥
स्वप्नं तद्देवदेवस्य न्यवेदयत धार्मिकः ॥ 4 ॥
1.154.m: Having fulfilled his purpose and worshipped Janārdana according to his wish, / the righteous one related that dream to the god of gods.

1.154.s:
tataḥ śuśrāva vacanaṃ devatārcāsamīritam ..
evametanmahīpāla nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
.. 5 .. evaṃ prasādaṃ saṃprāpya devadevājjanārdanāt ..
1.154.d:
ततः शुश्राव वचनं देवतार्चासमीरितम् ॥
एवमेतन्महीपाल नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
॥ 5 ॥ एवं प्रसादं संप्राप्य देवदेवाज्जनार्दनात् ॥
1.154.m: Then he heard a voice spoken by the divine image: / "It is so, O ruler of earth; no doubt should be entertained here." / Having thus received favor from the god of gods, Janārdana,

1.154.s: kṛtakṛtyamivātmānaṃ mene sa narapuṅgavaḥ .. 6 ..
1.154.d: कृतकृत्यमिवात्मानं मेने स नरपुङ्गवः ॥ 6 ॥
1.154.m: that bull among men considered himself to have achieved his purpose.

1.154.s:
kṛtadevārcano rājā tadā hutahutāśanaḥ ..
jagāda suhṛdāṃ teṣāṃ prasādaṃ madhusūdanāt .. 7 ..
1.154.d:
कृतदेवार्चनो राजा तदा हुतहुताशनः ॥
जगाद सुहृदां तेषां प्रसादं मधुसूदनात् ॥ 7 ॥
1.154.m: Having performed worship of the deity and offered oblation into the fire, / the king then related to those friends the favor [received] from Madhusūdana.

1.154.s:
tamūcuśca tadā sarve rājānamaparājitam ..
vidadhātu prasannaste devadevo janārdanaḥ .. 8 ..
1.154.d:
तमूचुश्च तदा सर्वे राजानमपराजितम् ॥
विदधातु प्रसन्नस्ते देवदेवो जनार्दनः ॥ 8 ॥
1.154.m: And then they all said to that unconquered king: / "May the gracious god of gods, Janārdana, grant [this] to you.

1.154.s:
aprasanne jagannāthe deśe'sminnṛpa kasyacit ..
na gatirvidyate rājaṃstvaṃ ca deśamihāgataḥ .. 9 ..
1.154.d:
अप्रसन्ने जगन्नाथे देशेऽस्मिन्नृप कस्यचित् ॥
न गतिर्विद्यते राजंस्त्वं च देशमिहागतः ॥ 9 ॥
1.154.m: When the Lord of the World is not gracious, O king, no one / has any access to this region; and yet you, O king, have come to this realm."

1.154.s:
sukhaṃ prāpnuhi bhadrante bhūya eva hitepsitān ..
sa sādayitvā te kāmāndevaḥ sarvagataḥ prabhuḥ .. 1.154.10 ..
1.154.d:
सुखं प्राप्नुहि भद्रन्ते भूय एव हितेप्सितान् ॥
स सादयित्वा ते कामान्देवः सर्वगतः प्रभुः ॥ 1.154.10 ॥
1.154.m: "Attain happiness, blessings to you! Moreover, fulfilling your desired wishes, / having brought about your desires, the all-pervading Lord God [blesses you]."

1.154.s:
evamuktvā narendraṃ taṃ gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ ..
jagmuḥ krīḍāvihārārthaṃ yathāpūrvamarindama .. 11 ..
1.154.d:
एवमुक्त्वा नरेन्द्रं तं गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः ॥
जग्मुः क्रीडाविहारार्थं यथापूर्वमरिन्दम ॥ 11 ॥
1.154.m: Having spoken thus to that lord of men, O tamer of foes, the hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases / departed for sport and amusement just as before.

1.154.s:
athājagāma taṃ deśaṃ brahmaṇo mānasaḥ sutaḥ ..
trijagadyaśasāṃ sthānamatriḥ suragaṇārcitaḥ .. 12..
1.154.d:
अथाजगाम तं देशं ब्रह्मणो मानसः सुतः ॥
त्रिजगद्यशसां स्थानमत्रिः सुरगणार्चितः ॥ 12॥
1.154.m: Then there came to that place the mind-born son of Brahmā, / Atri, the abode of the fame of the three worlds, worshipped by the hosts of gods.

1.154.s:
tamāgataṃ munivaraṃ dṛṣṭvā rājā purūravāḥ ..
pādyārghyācamanīyādyairāsanenābhyapūjayat .. 13 ..
1.154.d:
तमागतं मुनिवरं दृष्ट्वा राजा पुरूरवाः ॥
पाद्यार्घ्याचमनीयाद्यैरासनेनाभ्यपूजयत् ॥ 13 ॥
1.154.m: Seeing that excellent sage arrived, King Purūravas / worshipped [him] with water for the feet, guest-water, water for sipping, and a seat.

1.154.s:
sampūjya ca mahābhāgamidaṃ vacanamabravīt ..
adya me saphalaṃ janma adya me saphalaṃ tapaḥ .. 14 ..
1.154.d:
सम्पूज्य च महाभागमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
अद्य मे सफलं जन्म अद्य मे सफलं तपः ॥ 14 ॥
1.154.m: And having worshipped that fortunate one, he spoke this word: / "Today my birth is fruitful; today my asceticism is fruitful,

1.154.s:
yatte devagaṇairvandyau vanditau caraṇau mayā ..
śreyaḥ prasūtivṛkṣasya prarohastava darśanama .. 15 ..
1.154.d:
यत्ते देवगणैर्वन्द्यौ वन्दितौ चरणौ मया ॥
श्रेयः प्रसूतिवृक्षस्य प्ररोहस्तव दर्शनम ॥ 15 ॥
1.154.m: in that your two feet, worthy of worship by the hosts of gods, have been venerated by me. / The sight of you is the sprouting of the tree that brings forth good fortune,

1.154.s:
sarvapāpāntakaraṇaṃ sarvakalyāṇakāraṇam ..
kiṃ vā na labhyamastīha teṣāṃ dvijavarottama .. 16 ..
1.154.d:
सर्वपापान्तकरणं सर्वकल्याणकारणम् ॥
किं वा न लभ्यमस्तीह तेषां द्विजवरोत्तम ॥ 16 ॥
1.154.m: bringing an end to all sins and causing all auspiciousness. / What indeed is unobtainable in this world, O best among foremost twice-born,

1.154.s:
amoghadarśane dṛṣṭe bhavatyamitatejasi ..
evamuktastadā rājñā saṃprasanno jagāda tam .. 17 ..
1.154.d:
अमोघदर्शने दृष्टे भवत्यमिततेजसि ॥
एवमुक्तस्तदा राज्ञा संप्रसन्नो जगाद तम् ॥ 17 ॥
1.154.m: when you of unfailing sight and boundless splendour are beheld?" / Spoken to thus by the king, [the sage], thoroughly pleased, said to him:

1.154.s:
śṛṇu rājanvaco mahyaṃ yatte vakṣyāmi suvrata ..
devadevasamādeśāddattaṃ te darśanaṃ mayā .. 18 ..
1.154.d:
शृणु राजन्वचो मह्यं यत्ते वक्ष्यामि सुव्रत ॥
देवदेवसमादेशाद्दत्तं ते दर्शनं मया ॥ 18 ॥
1.154.m: "Listen to my words, O king, which I shall speak to you, O you of virtuous vows. / By command of the God of gods, my vision has been granted to you.

1.154.s:
suprasanno hi bhagavāndevaste madhusūdanaḥ ..
dvādaśīṣu sadā rājansopavāsena nityaśa .. 19..
1.154.d:
सुप्रसन्नो हि भगवान्देवस्ते मधुसूदनः ॥
द्वादशीषु सदा राजन्सोपवासेन नित्यश ॥ 19॥
1.154.m: For the Lord God Madhusūdana is exceedingly pleased with you. / Always, O king, on the twelfth days [of the fortnights], constantly with fasting,

1.154.s:
pūjito bhagavānviṣṇusttvayātīte tu janmani ..
rājasena tu bhāvena tvayā devaḥ samarcitaḥ .. 1.154.20 ..
1.154.d:
पूजितो भगवान्विष्णुस्त्त्वयातीते तु जन्मनि ॥
राजसेन तु भावेन त्वया देवः समर्चितः ॥ 1.154.20 ॥
1.154.m: the Lord Viṣṇu was worshipped by you in a past life. / But with a passionate disposition the God was worshipped by you,

1.154.s:
avaraṃ kāmamāśritya rājannihatakaṇṭakam ..
sāttvikena tu bhāvena pūjayitvā janārdanama .. 21 ..
1.154.d:
अवरं काममाश्रित्य राजन्निहतकण्टकम् ॥
सात्त्विकेन तु भावेन पूजयित्वा जनार्दनम ॥ 21 ॥
1.154.m: resorting to a lower desire, O king, [for a kingdom] cleared of rivals. / But having worshipped Janārdana with a pure, sattvic disposition,

1.154.s:
rājyaṃ madreṣu saṃprāptaṃ nipkaṇṭakamarindama ..
dvādaśyarcāprasannena devadevena cakriṇā .. 22 ..
1.154.d:
राज्यं मद्रेषु संप्राप्तं निप्कण्टकमरिन्दम ॥
द्वादश्यर्चाप्रसन्नेन देवदेवेन चक्रिणा ॥ 22 ॥
1.154.m: sovereignty among the Madras, free from rivals, has been attained [by you], O tamer of foes. / Pleased by your worship on the twelfth day, by the God of gods, the discus-wielder,

1.154.s:
pradarśitamidaṃ sthānaṃ madīyaṃ svargasannibham ..
iha rājam̐stapastaptvā devadevaṃ janārdanam ..23..
1.154.d:
प्रदर्शितमिदं स्थानं मदीयं स्वर्गसन्निभम् ॥
इह राजम्̐स्तपस्तप्त्वा देवदेवं जनार्दनम् ॥23॥
1.154.m: this abode of mine, resembling heaven, has been shown [to you]. / Performing asceticism here, O king, having worshipped the God of gods, Janārdana,

1.154.s:
ārādhya dṛṣṭavānasmi purā vararṣagaṇānbahūn ..
prāpyānujñāṃ hṛṣīkeṣāttatkṛte vivare śubhe ..24..
1.154.d:
आराध्य दृष्टवानस्मि पुरा वरर्षगणान्बहून् ॥
प्राप्यानुज्ञां हृषीकेषात्तत्कृते विवरे शुभे ॥24॥
1.154.m: in ancient times I beheld many hosts of excellent sages. / Having obtained permission from Hṛṣīkeśa, in an auspicious cave made for that [purpose],

1.154.s:
nityaṃ sannihitā rājaṃstasyaivārcā vinirmitā ..
niyogāddevadevasya pūjyate siddhamattamaiḥ .. 25 ..
1.154.d:
नित्यं सन्निहिता राजंस्तस्यैवार्चा विनिर्मिता ॥
नियोगाद्देवदेवस्य पूज्यते सिद्धमत्तमैः ॥ 25 ॥
1.154.m: an image of him was fashioned, O king, ever-present [there]. / By the command of the God of gods, it is worshipped by the greatest among the Siddhas.

1.154.s:
neyaṃ dṛṣṭā manuṣyendra manuṣyairna ca rākṣasaiḥ ..
piśitāśaistathaivānyairdṛṣṭapūrvā kathañcana .. 26 ..
1.154.d:
नेयं दृष्टा मनुष्येन्द्र मनुष्यैर्न च राक्षसैः ॥
पिशिताशैस्तथैवान्यैर्दृष्टपूर्वा कथञ्चन ॥ 26 ॥
1.154.m: This has not been seen by mortals, O lord of men, nor by Rākṣasas / or flesh-eaters, nor by any others ever seen before.

1.154.s:
asminsvargopame deśe tvayā laulyena karmaṇā.
ārādhito jagannātho devaścakragadādharaḥ..27..
1.154.d:
अस्मिन्स्वर्गोपमे देशे त्वया लौल्येन कर्मणा।
आराधितो जगन्नाथो देवश्चक्रगदाधरः॥27॥
1.154.m: In this realm resembling heaven, with ardent longing by [such] deed / the Lord of the universe, the God who bears the discus and mace, has been worshipped by you.

1.154.s:
āsannaphalamūle'pi bahugorasasaṃyute..
kṣaudrayuktaśilāprāye samākṣikaphalairyute..28..
1.154.d:
आसन्नफलमूलेऽपि बहुगोरससंयुते॥
क्षौद्रयुक्तशिलाप्राये समाक्षिकफलैर्युते॥28॥
1.154.m: Even though fruits and roots were at hand, filled with abundant cow's milk, / abundant with rocks bearing wild honey and filled with honeyed fruits,

1.154.s:
kevalāmbhośinā taptaṃ yattvayā paramaṃ tapaḥ..
tena te'haṃ varaṃ dadmi yadabhīṣṭaṃ tavānagha..29..
1.154.d:
केवलाम्भोशिना तप्तं यत्त्वया परमं तपः॥
तेन तेऽहं वरं दद्मि यदभीष्टं तवानघ॥29॥
1.154.m: since supreme asceticism was performed by you subsisting only on water, / therefore I grant you a boon that is desired by you, O sinless one.

1.154.s:
acireṇaiva kālena tvayā rājankṛtaṃ tapaḥ..
rūpārthaṃ rūpalābhāya prāptaṃ me gadataḥ śṛṇu..1.154.30..
1.154.d:
अचिरेणैव कालेन त्वया राजन्कृतं तपः॥
रूपार्थं रूपलाभाय प्राप्तं मे गदतः शृणु॥1.154.30॥
1.154.m: Asceticism was performed by you, O king, in not a very long time; / for the sake of beauty, to gain beauty, listen to what was attained as I tell it:

1.154.s:
tadvrataṃ ye kariṣyanti manujeśvara mānavāḥ..
striyo vāpi naraśreṣṭha prāpsyante rūpamuttamam..31..
1.154.d:
तद्व्रतं ये करिष्यन्ति मनुजेश्वर मानवाः॥
स्त्रियो वापि नरश्रेष्ठ प्राप्स्यन्ते रूपमुत्तमम्॥31॥
1.154.m: Those men who will perform that vow, O lord of men, / or women too, O best of men, will attain supreme beauty,

1.154.s:
saubhāgyamatulaṃ loke lāvaṇyamapi cottamam..
dharmiṣṭatāṃ tathārogyaṃ kule janma tathottame..32..
1.154.d:
सौभाग्यमतुलं लोके लावण्यमपि चोत्तमम्॥
धर्मिष्टतां तथारोग्यं कुले जन्म तथोत्तमे॥32॥
1.154.m: incomparable good fortune in the world, and also supreme charm, / righteousness, likewise health, and birth in an excellent family.

1.154.s:
janmāntaramathāsādya svargalokaṃ tathāvidham..
svargalokātparibhraṣṭā mānuṣye guṇasaṃyutāḥ..33..
1.154.d:
जन्मान्तरमथासाद्य स्वर्गलोकं तथाविधम्॥
स्वर्गलोकात्परिभ्रष्टा मानुष्ये गुणसंयुताः॥33॥
1.154.m: Then, having attained another birth in such a heavenly world, / falling from the heavenly world, endowed with virtues in human existence,

1.154.s:
brāhmaṇā dhanasampannā bhaviṣyantyathavā nṛpāḥ..
janmāntaramathāsādya sarvesyaiva phalapradāḥ..34..
1.154.d:
ब्राह्मणा धनसम्पन्ना भविष्यन्त्यथवा नृपाः॥
जन्मान्तरमथासाद्य सर्वेस्यैव फलप्रदाः॥34॥
1.154.m: they will become wealthy brahmins or kings. / Then, having attained another birth, all [these vows] yield fruit;

1.154.s:
rūpavaṃto mahārāja ihāmutra ca te'naghāḥ..
yasmāttvayā tapastaptaṃ keśavaścātha pūjitaḥ..35..
1.154.d:
रूपवंतो महाराज इहामुत्र च तेऽनघाः॥
यस्मात्त्वया तपस्तप्तं केशवश्चाथ पूजितः॥35॥
1.154.m: they become handsome, O great king, here and in the hereafter, sinless. / Because asceticism was performed by you and Keśava was worshipped,

1.154.s:
mayā samāgataścāpi gaṃdharvaiśca sahasraśaḥ..
ihaiva kṛtvā dharmajña rūpasatraṃ mahāphalam..
divyarūpadharo bhūtvā svarāṣṭraṃ gantumarhasi..36..
1.154.d:
मया समागतश्चापि गंधर्वैश्च सहस्रशः॥
इहैव कृत्वा धर्मज्ञ रूपसत्रं महाफलम्॥
दिव्यरूपधरो भूत्वा स्वराष्ट्रं गन्तुमर्हसि॥36॥
1.154.m: and you have met with me and with Gandharvas by the thousands, / having performed right here, O knower of dharma, the Beauty Sacrifice that yields great fruit, / assuming a celestial form you ought to return to your own realm."

1.154.s:
etāvaduktaḥ sa tu madranātho mahātmanā tena narendrasiṃha..
papraccha taṃ dharmabhṛtāmvariṣṭhaḥ satrasya tasyānuśayaṃ vidhānam..37..
1.154.d:
एतावदुक्तः स तु मद्रनाथो महात्मना तेन नरेन्द्रसिंह॥
पप्रच्छ तं धर्मभृताम्वरिष्ठः सत्रस्य तस्यानुशयं विधानम्॥37॥
1.154.m: Spoken to thus by that great soul, that lion among kings, the ruler of the Madras, / foremost among upholders of dharma, asked him the traditional rule and procedure of that sacrificial session.

1.155.s:
purūravā uvāca..
śrotumicchāmi bhagavanrūpasatraṃ mahāphalam..
yatsamāptau bhaviṣyāmi divyarūpadharo mune..1..
1.155.d:
पुरूरवा उवाच॥
श्रोतुमिच्छामि भगवन्रूपसत्रं महाफलम्॥
यत्समाप्तौ भविष्यामि दिव्यरूपधरो मुने॥1॥
1.155.m: Purūravas said: / "I wish to hear, O venerable one, of the Beauty Sacrifice that yields great fruit, / upon whose completion, O sage, I shall become one endowed with a celestial form."

1.155.s:
atriruvāca .. tatsatraṃ kartukāmena cānveṣyo brāhmaṇo guruḥ ..
jyotiṣaṃ yo vijānāti itihāsāṃśca kṛtsnaśaḥ ..2 ..
1.155.d:
अत्रिरुवाच ॥ तत्सत्रं कर्तुकामेन चान्वेष्यो ब्राह्मणो गुरुः ॥
ज्योतिषं यो विजानाति इतिहासांश्च कृत्स्नशः ॥2 ॥
1.155.m: Atri said: / "By one wishing to perform that sacrificial session, a brahmin guru should be sought out / who thoroughly understands astronomy and astrology, and the epic histories in their entirety.

1.155.s:
tatpradiṣṭena vidhinā pādarkṣātprabhṛti kramāt ..
upoṣitavyaṃ nakṣatraṃ pratyekaṃ tannibodha me .. 3 ..
1.155.d:
तत्प्रदिष्टेन विधिना पादर्क्षात्प्रभृति क्रमात् ॥
उपोषितव्यं नक्षत्रं प्रत्येकं तन्निबोध मे ॥ 3 ॥
1.155.m: According to the procedure prescribed by him, beginning from the asterism of the feet in proper sequence, / a fast should be observed for each asterism; learn that from me.

1.155.s:
phālgunyāṃ samatītāyāṃ kṛṣṇapakṣāṣṭamī tu yā ..
samūlāṃ tāṃ tu samprāpya vrataṃ gṛhṇīta mānavaḥ .. 4 ..
1.155.d:
फाल्गुन्यां समतीतायां कृष्णपक्षाष्टमी तु या ॥
समूलां तां तु सम्प्राप्य व्रतं गृह्णीत मानवः ॥ 4 ॥
1.155.m: When the full moon day of Phālguna has passed, the eighth day of the dark fortnight— / having reached that [tithi] conjoined with Mūla, a person should undertake the vow.

1.155.s:
upoṣitavyaṃ nakṣatraṃ nakṣatrasya ca daivatam .
varuṇaṃ ca tathā candraṃ pūjayedvidhinā naraḥ .. 5 ..
1.155.d:
उपोषितव्यं नक्षत्रं नक्षत्रस्य च दैवतम् ।
वरुणं च तथा चन्द्रं पूजयेद्विधिना नरः ॥ 5 ॥
1.155.m: One should fast on that asterism, and the deity of the asterism, / as well as Varuṇa and the moon, a man should worship according to the rule.

1.155.s:
pūjayeddevadeveśaṃ bhagavantaṃ janārdanam ..
upoṣya saṅgaṃ devasya prayatnena ca pūjayet .. 6 ..
1.155.d:
पूजयेद्देवदेवेशं भगवन्तं जनार्दनम् ॥
उपोष्य सङ्गं देवस्य प्रयत्नेन च पूजयेत् ॥ 6 ॥
1.155.m: He should worship the Lord of the gods of gods, the venerable Janārdana. / Having fasted, he should diligently worship the body of the God.

1.155.s:
tato'gnihavanaṃ kṛtvā pūjayitvā tathā gurum ..
upavāsastu kartavyo dvitīye'hani pārthiva .. 7 ..
1.155.d:
ततोऽग्निहवनं कृत्वा पूजयित्वा तथा गुरुम् ॥
उपवासस्तु कर्तव्यो द्वितीयेऽहनि पार्थिव ॥ 7 ॥
1.155.m: Then, having offered oblations into the fire and worshipped the guru, / a fast must indeed be observed on the second day, O king.

1.155.s:
upoṣya ṛkṣe vigate snātvā sampūjya keśavam ..
kṛtvāgnihavanaṃ śaktyā pūjayitvā dvijottamān .. 8 ..
1.155.d:
उपोष्य ऋक्षे विगते स्नात्वा सम्पूज्य केशवम् ॥
कृत्वाग्निहवनं शक्त्या पूजयित्वा द्विजोत्तमान् ॥ 8 ॥
1.155.m: Having fasted, when the asterism has passed, having bathed and worshipped Keśava, / having made fire-oblations according to his ability and honoured the foremost of twice-born,

1.155.s:
haviṣyamannaṃ bhoktavyaṃ śṛṇu cāṅgakramaṃ mama ..
pādayoḥ kathitaṃ mūlaṃ prājāpatyaṃ tu jaṅghayoḥ .. 9 ..
1.155.d:
हविष्यमन्नं भोक्तव्यं शृणु चाङ्गक्रमं मम ॥
पादयोः कथितं मूलं प्राजापत्यं तु जङ्घयोः ॥ 9 ॥
1.155.m: sacrificial food should be eaten; and hear from me the sequence of the limbs: / Mūla is declared for the two feet, and Rohiṇī for the two shanks;

1.155.s:
āśvinaṃ jānuyugalaṃ coruyugmaṃ ca pārthiva ..
sahite dve tathāṣāḍhe guhye ca sahite smṛte .. 1.155.10 ..
1.155.d:
आश्विनं जानुयुगलं चोरुयुग्मं च पार्थिव ॥
सहिते द्वे तथाषाढे गुह्ये च सहिते स्मृते ॥ 1.155.10 ॥
1.155.m: Aśvinī is the pair of knees, and the pair of thighs, O king, / the two Āṣāḍhās together, and the private parts are remembered as the same two together;

1.155.s:
pūrvottare ca phālgunyau kṛttikāsu kaṭirbhavet ..
pārśvayoḥ kukṣiyutayornakṣatratritayaṃ matam .. 11 ..
1.155.d:
पूर्वोत्तरे च फाल्गुन्यौ कृत्तिकासु कटिर्भवेत् ॥
पार्श्वयोः कुक्षियुतयोर्नक्षत्रत्रितयं मतम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.155.m: Pūrva-phālgunī and Uttara-phālgunī, and at Kṛttikā is the waist. / For the two sides along with the belly, a triad of asterisms is held [to apply]:

1.155.s:
ubhe proṣṭhapade rājanrevatī ca tathā bhaveta ..
uro'nurādhāsu tathā pṛṣṭhaṃ niṣṭyāsu kīrtitam .. 12 ..
1.155.d:
उभे प्रोष्ठपदे राजन्रेवती च तथा भवेत ॥
उरोऽनुराधासु तथा पृष्ठं निष्ट्यासु कीर्तितम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.155.m: both Proṣṭhapadās, O king, and Revatī likewise. / The chest is in Anurādhā, and the back is declared in Niṣṭyā [Svātī];

1.155.s:
bhujau jñeyau viśākhāsu haste proktau tathā karau ..
aṅgulyaśca tathā proktā rājasiṃha punarvasau .. 13 ..
1.155.d:
भुजौ ज्ञेयौ विशाखासु हस्ते प्रोक्तौ तथा करौ ॥
अङ्गुल्यश्च तथा प्रोक्ता राजसिंह पुनर्वसौ ॥ 13 ॥
1.155.m: the two arms are to be known in the Viśākhās, and the two hands are stated in Hasta; / and the fingers are declared in Punarvasu, O lion among kings;

1.155.s:
āśleṣāyāṃ tathā proktā jyeṣṭhāyāṃ nṛpa kandharā ..
śravaṇau śravaṇau jñeye mukhaṃ puṣye prakīrtitam .. 14 ..
1.155.d:
आश्लेषायां तथा प्रोक्ता ज्येष्ठायां नृप कन्धरा ॥
श्रवणौ श्रवणौ ज्ञेये मुखं पुष्ये प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 14 ॥
1.155.m: the [nails] are declared in Āśleṣā, the neck, O king, in Jyeṣṭhā; / Śravaṇa is known for the two ears, and the face is proclaimed in Puṣya.

1.155.s:
dantāḥ svātau śatabhiṣā hanū proktau tathā nṛpa ..
maghāyāṃ nāsikā proktā mṛgaśīrṣe ca locane .. 15 ..
1.155.d:
दन्ताः स्वातौ शतभिषा हनू प्रोक्तौ तथा नृप ॥
मघायां नासिका प्रोक्ता मृगशीर्षे च लोचने ॥ 15 ॥
1.155.m: The teeth are stated to be in Svāti, the jaws in Śatabhiṣā, O king; / the nose is stated to be in Maghā, and the eyes in Mṛgaśīrṣa.

1.155.s:
citrā lalāṭe vijñeyā bharaṇyaśca tathā śiraḥ ..
śiroruhāstathārdrāsu batasyānte narādhipa .. 16 ..
1.155.d:
चित्रा ललाटे विज्ञेया भरण्यश्च तथा शिरः ॥
शिरोरुहास्तथार्द्रासु बतस्यान्ते नराधिप ॥ 16 ॥
1.155.m: Citrā should be known as the forehead, and Bharaṇī as the head; / the hair is likewise in Ārdrā at the end of the vow, O lord of men.

1.155.s:
māghaśuklāvasāne tu satraṃ parisamāpyate ..
yadyantarāyaṃ na bhavetkiñcicchaucanimittajam .. 17 ..
1.155.d:
माघशुक्लावसाने तु सत्रं परिसमाप्यते ॥
यद्यन्तरायं न भवेत्किञ्चिच्छौचनिमित्तजम् ॥ 17 ॥
1.155.m: At the end of the bright fortnight of Māgha, however, the sacrificial session is concluded, / if there should be no impediment arising from ritual impurity.

1.155.s:
antarāyaṃ mahārāja yadi śaucanimittajam ..
upoṣyamevopavasennakṣatramaparaṃ punaḥ .. 18 ..
1.155.d:
अन्तरायं महाराज यदि शौचनिमित्तजम् ॥
उपोष्यमेवोपवसेन्नक्षत्रमपरं पुनः ॥ 18 ॥
1.155.m: If there is an impediment arising from ritual impurity, O great king, / one should fast again during another lunar mansion that is to be fasted upon.

1.155.s:
kramaprāptaṃ hi nakṣatraṃ cāśuddhyāmapavarjitam ..
ullaṅghayanmahīpāla pratyavāyaṃ samaśnute ...39...
1.155.d:
क्रमप्राप्तं हि नक्षत्रं चाशुद्ध्यामपवर्जितम् ॥
उल्लङ्घयन्महीपाल प्रत्यवायं समश्नुते ॥.39॥।
1.155.m: For, skipping a lunar mansion arrived at in due order / that was omitted because of impurity, O protector of the earth, one incurs sin.

1.155.s:
aṅgakrameṇa sakalamṛkṣavargamupoṣitaḥ..
vratānte prayataḥ snātvā pūjayenmadhusūdanam .. 1.155.20 ..
1.155.d:
अङ्गक्रमेण सकलमृक्षवर्गमुपोषितः॥
व्रतान्ते प्रयतः स्नात्वा पूजयेन्मधुसूदनम् ॥ 1.155.20 ॥
1.155.m: Having fasted upon the entire group of asterisms in the order of the limbs, / one should, subdued and bathed at the end of the vow, worship Madhusūdana,

1.155.s:
candanāgurukarpūramṛgadarpaiḥ sakuṅkumaiḥ ..
jātīphalaiḥ sakaṃkolairlavaṅgakusumaistathā .. 21 ..
1.155.d:
चन्दनागुरुकर्पूरमृगदर्पैः सकुङ्कुमैः ॥
जातीफलैः सकंकोलैर्लवङ्गकुसुमैस्तथा ॥ 21 ॥
1.155.m: with sandalwood, agallochum, camphor, musk, along with saffron, / nutmegs, cubebs, and clove flowers;

1.155.s:
bolaguggulaniryāsaiḥ puṣpaiḥ kālodbhavaiḥ śubhaiḥ ..
dhūpo narendrāguruṇā candanena sugandhinā .. 22 ..
1.155.d:
बोलगुग्गुलनिर्यासैः पुष्पैः कालोद्भवैः शुभैः ॥
धूपो नरेन्द्रागुरुणा चन्दनेन सुगन्धिना ॥ 22 ॥
1.155.m: with myrrh and bdellium resins, and auspicious seasonal flowers; / incense [should be offered], O ruler of men, with fragrant agallochum and sandalwood.

1.155.s:
dīpāśca deyā rājendra tilatailaprapūritāḥ ..
dīpeṣu vartayaḥ kāryyā mahārañjanarañjitāḥ .. 23 ..
1.155.d:
दीपाश्च देया राजेन्द्र तिलतैलप्रपूरिताः ॥
दीपेषु वर्तयः कार्य्या महारञ्जनरञ्जिताः ॥ 23 ॥
1.155.m: Lamps filled with sesame oil should also be given, O king of kings; / the wicks in the lamps should be dyed with safflower.

1.155.s:
naivedyaṃ ca tathā kāryaṃ paramānnena bhūriṇā ..
dadhnā kṣīrāmṛtābhyāṃ ca madhunā ca guḍena ca .. 24 ..
1.155.d:
नैवेद्यं च तथा कार्यं परमान्नेन भूरिणा ॥
दध्ना क्षीरामृताभ्यां च मधुना च गुडेन च ॥ 24 ॥
1.155.m: And food offerings should be prepared with abundant sweet milk-rice, / curds, milk, and butter, and honey and jaggery,

1.155.s:
sitayā ca tathā bhakṣyaiḥ phalamūlairyathāvidhi..
apūpaiḥ pānakairhṛdyaiḥ śītalaiśca sugandhibhiḥ .. 25 ..
1.155.d:
सितया च तथा भक्ष्यैः फलमूलैर्यथाविधि॥
अपूपैः पानकैर्हृद्यैः शीतलैश्च सुगन्धिभिः ॥ 25 ॥
1.155.m: and white sugar, and similarly with eatables, fruits, and roots according to rule, / with cakes and pleasing, cool, fragrant beverages.

1.155.s:
lavaṇasya ca pātrāṇi kṛsaraṃ ca nivedayet ..
sarvabījāni rājendra bhūṣaṇāni ca śaktitaḥ .. 26 ..
1.155.d:
लवणस्य च पात्राणि कृसरं च निवेदयेत् ॥
सर्वबीजानि राजेन्द्र भूषणानि च शक्तितः ॥ 26 ॥
1.155.m: One should offer vessels of salt and rice-pulse porridge, / all kinds of grains, O king of kings, and ornaments according to one's means,

1.155.s:
mahārhāṇi ca vastrāṇi bhaktyā prayatamānasaḥ ..
tadviṣṇoḥ pagmamiti homaḥ kāryo hyanantaram .. 27 ..
1.155.d:
महार्हाणि च वस्त्राणि भक्त्या प्रयतमानसः ॥
तद्विष्णोः पग्ममिति होमः कार्यो ह्यनन्तरम् ॥ 27 ॥
1.155.m: and costly garments with devotion and a concentrated mind. / Immediately after, a fire sacrifice should be performed with the mantra beginning 'tad viṣṇoḥ paramam padam'.

1.155.s:
dvādaśākṣarakaṃ mantraṃ strīśūdreṣu vidhīyate ..
ghṛtaṃ mākṣikasaṃyuktaṃ juhuyātttilataṇḍusam .. 28 ..
1.155.d:
द्वादशाक्षरकं मन्त्रं स्त्रीशूद्रेषु विधीयते ॥
घृतं माक्षिकसंयुक्तं जुहुयात्त्तिलतण्डुसम् ॥ 28 ॥
1.155.m: For women and śūdras, the twelve-syllable mantra is prescribed. / One should offer ghee mixed with honey, along with sesame seeds and unbroken rice grains.

1.155.s:
tatastu dakṣiṇā deyā gurave nṛpasattama ..
nāgāśca madamattā vai grāmāśca vividhāstathā .. 29 ..
1.155.d:
ततस्तु दक्षिणा देया गुरवे नृपसत्तम ॥
नागाश्च मदमत्ता वै ग्रामाश्च विविधास्तथा ॥ 29 ॥
1.155.m: Then sacrificial fee should be given to the guru, O best of kings: / rutting elephants indeed, and various villages,

1.155.s:
turagāśca tathā mukhyā ratnāni vividhāni ca ..
brāhmaṇaśca pitā jñeyo rūpasatrapradarśakaḥ .. 1.155.30 ..
1.155.d:
तुरगाश्च तथा मुख्या रत्नानि विविधानि च ॥
ब्राह्मणश्च पिता ज्ञेयो रूपसत्रप्रदर्शकः ॥ 1.155.30 ॥
1.155.m: and prime horses, and various jewels. / The brahmin who reveals this sacrificial session for beauty should be regarded as a father,

1.155.s:
rūpasaubhāgyalāvaṇyajanmabhogapradāyakaḥ ..
rājyasya vā dvijatvasya bahuvittasya dāyakaḥ .... 31 ..
1.155.d:
रूपसौभाग्यलावण्यजन्मभोगप्रदायकः ॥
राज्यस्य वा द्विजत्वस्य बहुवित्तस्य दायकः ॥॥ 31 ॥
1.155.m: as one who bestows beauty, good fortune, charm, birth, and pleasures of life, / or bestows royalty, status of the twice-born, and immense wealth.

1.155.s:
na tasya niṣkṛtiḥ śakyā gantuṃ dānena bhūriṇā ..
guruprasāda evātra dakṣiṇānāṃ tu kāraṇam .. 32 ..
1.155.d:
न तस्य निष्कृतिः शक्या गन्तुं दानेन भूरिणा ॥
गुरुप्रसाद एवात्र दक्षिणानां तु कारणम् ॥ 32 ॥
1.155.m: No compensation can be made to him through lavish gifts; / the guru's favor alone is the cause behind the sacrificial fees here.

1.155.s:
tasmātprasādamākāṅkṣedrūpasatra pradarśakāta ..
avaśyaṃ tasya dātavyaṃ ghṛtapūrṇaṃ tu bhājanam .. 33 ..
1.155.d:
तस्मात्प्रसादमाकाङ्क्षेद्रूपसत्र प्रदर्शकात ॥
अवश्यं तस्य दातव्यं घृतपूर्णं तु भाजनम् ॥ 33 ॥
1.155.m: Therefore one should desire favor from the revealer of the sacrificial session for beauty. / Inevitably, a vessel filled with clarified butter must be given to him,

1.155.s:
catuṣpalaṃ tu kāṃsyasya suvarṇaṃ kāñcanasya ca ..
tataḥ paraṃ bhojanīyāḥ svaśaktyā dvijapuṅgavāḥ ..34..
1.155.d:
चतुष्पलं तु कांस्यस्य सुवर्णं काञ्चनस्य च ॥
ततः परं भोजनीयाः स्वशक्त्या द्विजपुङ्गवाः ॥34॥
1.155.m: made of four palas of bell-metal, and a suvarṇa weight of gold. / Thereafter, foremost twice-borns should be fed according to one's capacity,

1.155.s:
lavaṇakṣīramadhvājyaguḍabhakṣyasitotkaṭam ..
bhojanaṃ pānakopetaṃ paścāddeyā ca dakṣiṇā .. 3083 ..
1.155.d:
लवणक्षीरमध्वाज्यगुडभक्ष्यसितोत्कटम् ॥
भोजनं पानकोपेतं पश्चाद्देया च दक्षिणा ॥ 3083 ॥
1.155.m: a meal rich in salt, milk, honey, clarified butter, jaggery, eatables, and white sugar, / accompanied by beverages; and afterward sacrificial fee should be given.

1.155.s:
vastrayugmaṃ pradātavyaṃ brāhmaṇāya navaṃ śubham ..
brāhmaṇāya ca dātavyaṃ mahārājatarañjitam .. 36 ..
1.155.d:
वस्त्रयुग्मं प्रदातव्यं ब्राह्मणाय नवं शुभम् ॥
ब्राह्मणाय च दातव्यं महाराजतरञ्जितम् ॥ 36 ॥
1.155.m: A pair of new, auspicious garments should be given to a brahmin, / dyed with saffron, it should be given to a brahmin.

1.155.s:
saptabījāni deyāni lavaṇaṃ rūpyameva ca ..
yaccānyadapyabhīṣṭaṃ syācchatropānatkameva ca .. 37 ..
1.155.d:
सप्तबीजानि देयानि लवणं रूप्यमेव च ॥
यच्चान्यदप्यभीष्टं स्याच्छत्रोपानत्कमेव च ॥ 37 ॥
1.155.m: Seven seeds should be given, salt, silver, / and whatever else may be desired, including an umbrella and sandals.

1.155.s:
vittaśāṭhyaṃ na kartavyaṃ satradāne mahīpate ..
avaśyadeyaṃ satre'sminghṛtapūrṇaṃ ca bhājanam .. 38 ..
1.155.d:
वित्तशाठ्यं न कर्तव्यं सत्रदाने महीपते ॥
अवश्यदेयं सत्रेऽस्मिन्घृतपूर्णं च भाजनम् ॥ 38 ॥
1.155.m: One should not practice deceit regarding wealth in the giving for the sacrificial session, O protector of the earth. / In this sacrificial session, a vessel filled with clarified butter must certainly be given,

1.155.s:
catuṣpalaṃ tu kāṃsyasya suvarṇaṃ kāñcanasya ca ..
vratenānena cīrṇena dehatyāge dinaṃ gataḥ ..39..
1.155.d:
चतुष्पलं तु कांस्यस्य सुवर्णं काञ्चनस्य च ॥
व्रतेनानेन चीर्णेन देहत्यागे दिनं गतः ॥39॥
1.155.m: made of four palas of bell-metal, and a suvarṇa weight of gold. / Having performed this vow, upon giving up the body, one goes to the realm of the sun.

1.155.s:
tatroṣya suciraṃ kālaṃ mānuṣye yadi jāyate ..
rājā bhavati dharmātmā brāhmaṇo vā dhanānvitaḥ .. 1.155.40 ..
1.155.d:
तत्रोष्य सुचिरं कालं मानुष्ये यदि जायते ॥
राजा भवति धर्मात्मा ब्राह्मणो वा धनान्वितः ॥ 1.155.40 ॥
1.155.m: Dwelling there for a very long time, if born in the human world, / he becomes a righteous king or a wealthy brahmin,

1.155.s:
kule mahati sambhūto rūpeṇā'pratimo bhuvi ..
ārogyaṃ mahadāpnoti saubhāgyamapi cottamam .. 41 ..
1.155.d:
कुले महति सम्भूतो रूपेणाऽप्रतिमो भुवि ॥
आरोग्यं महदाप्नोति सौभाग्यमपि चोत्तमम् ॥ 41 ॥
1.155.m: born in a great lineage, peerless in beauty on earth; / he obtains great health and also the highest good fortune,

1.155.s:
lāvaṇyaṃ buddhi medhe ca matiṃ dharme ca śāśvatīm ..
sampūrṇacandrapratimaḥ sarvasattvavaśaṅkaraḥ .. 42 ..
1.155.d:
लावण्यं बुद्धि मेधे च मतिं धर्मे च शाश्वतीम् ॥
सम्पूर्णचन्द्रप्रतिमः सर्वसत्त्ववशङ्करः ॥ 42 ॥
1.155.m: charm, intellect, wisdom, and an eternal mind fixed on dharma. / Resembling the full moon, subduing all living beings,

1.155.s:
naro bhavati rājendra nārī cāpsarasopamā ..
subhagā darśanīyā ca lāvaṇyaguṇasaṃyutā .. 43 ..
1.155.d:
नरो भवति राजेन्द्र नारी चाप्सरसोपमा ॥
सुभगा दर्शनीया च लावण्यगुणसंयुता ॥ 43 ॥
1.155.m: the man becomes, O king of kings; and a woman becomes like an apsaras, / fortunate, lovely to behold, endowed with charm and virtues,

1.155.s:
bahudhānyā bahudhanā bahubhūpaṇasaṃyutā ..
bhartuścātyantadayitā loke khyātā ca sadguṇaiḥ ..
nityārogyavatī śāntā sarvadoṣavivarjitā ..44..
1.155.d:
बहुधान्या बहुधना बहुभूपणसंयुता ॥
भर्तुश्चात्यन्तदयिता लोके ख्याता च सद्गुणैः ॥
नित्यारोग्यवती शान्ता सर्वदोषविवर्जिता ॥44॥
1.155.m: having much grain, much wealth, endowed with many ornaments, / exceedingly beloved by her husband, famed in the world for good virtues, / endowed with constant health, tranquil, free from all flaws,

1.155.s: candrānanā nīlasarojanetrā trailokyakāntā pativallabhā ca ..45..
1.155.d: चन्द्रानना नीलसरोजनेत्रा त्रैलोक्यकान्ता पतिवल्लभा च ॥45॥
1.155.m: moon-faced, with eyes like blue lotuses, beloved of the three worlds, dear to her husband.

1.155.s: bhavatyavaśyaṃ subhagā sunīlā lāvaṇyayuktā yaśasā śriyā ca .. 46 ..
1.155.d: भवत्यवश्यं सुभगा सुनीला लावण्ययुक्ता यशसा श्रिया च ॥ 46 ॥
1.155.m: She inevitably becomes fortunate, dark and radiant, endowed with charm, fame, and splendor.

1.156.s:
.. purūravā uvāca ..
bhagavansarvadharmajña pitāmaha mahādyute ..
gurutvaṃ me vrate tasminkartumarhasi mānada .. 1 ..
1.156.d:
॥ पुरूरवा उवाच ॥
भगवन्सर्वधर्मज्ञ पितामह महाद्युते ॥
गुरुत्वं मे व्रते तस्मिन्कर्तुमर्हसि मानद ॥ 1 ॥
1.156.m: Purūravas said: / O lord, knower of all dharma, grandsire of great radiance, / O honor-giver, be pleased to act as my guru in this vow,

1.156.s:
vratāvasāne ca tathā sāmagryaṃ dvijapuṅgava ..
evaṃ śakyosmyaraṇyesminkartuṃ brahmanmahadvratam .. 2 ..
1.156.d:
व्रतावसाने च तथा सामग्र्यं द्विजपुङ्गव ॥
एवं शक्योस्म्यरण्येस्मिन्कर्तुं ब्रह्मन्महद्व्रतम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.156.m: and also [supply] the ritual paraphernalia at the conclusion of the vow, O foremost among the twice-born. / In this way, O brahmin, I shall be able to perform this great vow in this forest.

1.156.s:
atriruvāca .. tava prasādaṃ bhagavānsarvātmā madhusūdanaḥ ..
kurute'haṃ kariṣyāmi gurutvamaparājitaḥ .. 3 ..
1.156.d:
अत्रिरुवाच ॥ तव प्रसादं भगवान्सर्वात्मा मधुसूदनः ॥
कुरुतेऽहं करिष्यामि गुरुत्वमपराजितः ॥ 3 ॥
1.156.m: Atri said: / The holy Madhusūdana, the soul of all, extends his favor to you. / I, invincible, will act as the guru,

1.156.s:
vratāvasāne ca tathā sāmagryaṃ dvijapuṅgavaiḥ ..
kāmāssannihitāścānyairdeśe'sminnṛpa sarvadā .. 4 ..
1.156.d:
व्रतावसाने च तथा सामग्र्यं द्विजपुङ्गवैः ॥
कामास्सन्निहिताश्चान्यैर्देशेऽस्मिन्नृप सर्वदा ॥ 4 ॥
1.156.m: and likewise [provide] the ritual paraphernalia along with foremost twice-borns at the conclusion of the vow; / all desires are made present by others in this region at all times, O king.

1.156.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
evamuktvā sa dharmātmā saptame ca dine tadā ..
jyeṣṭhāyāṃ saptamīyoge grāhayāmāsa taṃ vratam .. 5 ..
1.156.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवमुक्त्वा स धर्मात्मा सप्तमे च दिने तदा ॥
ज्येष्ठायां सप्तमीयोगे ग्राहयामास तं व्रतम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.156.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having spoken thus, that righteous-souled one on the seventh day then, / on the conjunction of the seventh lunar day with Jyeṣṭhā, initiated him into that vow.

1.156.s:
pādarkṣāttu prabhṛtyevamṛkṣeṛkṣe narādhipaḥ ..
kārayāmāsa devasya kathitāṅgādipūjanam .. 6 ..
1.156.d:
पादर्क्षात्तु प्रभृत्येवमृक्षेऋक्षे नराधिपः ॥
कारयामास देवस्य कथिताङ्गादिपूजनम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.156.m: Beginning from the asterism presiding over the feet, under each successive asterism, the ruler of men / had worship performed of the respective limbs and other parts of the deity as prescribed,

1.156.s:
snānaṃ nakṣatranirdiṣṭaṃ nakṣatrasya ca pūjanam ..
nakṣatradaivatasyāpi somasya varuṇasya ca .. 7 ..
1.156.d:
स्नानं नक्षत्रनिर्दिष्टं नक्षत्रस्य च पूजनम् ॥
नक्षत्रदैवतस्यापि सोमस्य वरुणस्य च ॥ 7 ॥
1.156.m: the bath prescribed for the lunar mansion, and worship of the lunar mansion, / of the deity of the lunar mansion, of Soma, and of Varuṇa,

1.156.s:
pūjanaṃ ca tathā viṣṇordevadevasya cakriṇaḥ ..
homaṃ tathaiva sarveṣāṃ yathāvanmanujeśvara .. 8 ..
1.156.d:
पूजनं च तथा विष्णोर्देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः ॥
होमं तथैव सर्वेषां यथावन्मनुजेश्वर ॥ 8 ॥
1.156.m: and likewise the worship of Viṣṇu, the god of gods who holds the discus, / and similarly a fire sacrifice for all of them properly, O lord of men.

1.156.s:
māghaśuklamaghāṃ prāpya dvādaśīṃ ca tathā tithim ..
atrirvratāvasāne tamāgato brāhmaṇaiḥ saha .. 9 ..
1.156.d:
माघशुक्लमघां प्राप्य द्वादशीं च तथा तिथिम् ॥
अत्रिर्व्रतावसाने तमागतो ब्राह्मणैः सह ॥ 9 ॥
1.156.m: When the asterism Maghā and the twelfth lunar day of the bright fortnight of Māgha arrived, / Atri came to him together with brahmins at the conclusion of the vow.

1.156.s:
vratāvasāne saṃpūjya kethavāṅgārcisomajāna ..
rājyaṃ nivedayāmāsa so'treḥ sakalameva hi .. 1.156.10 ..
1.156.d:
व्रतावसाने संपूज्य केथवाङ्गार्चिसोमजान ॥
राज्यं निवेदयामास सोऽत्रेः सकलमेव हि ॥ 1.156.10 ॥
1.156.m: At the conclusion of the vow, having worshipped the limbs of Keśava, the fire, and the deities born of Soma, / he offered the entire kingdom to Atri.

1.156.s:
pratigṛhya ca tadrājyaṃ tasmādvai mantravinnṛpa ..
bhūyaḥ prādātsa tasyaiva vacanañcedamabravīt .. 11 ..
1.156.d:
प्रतिगृह्य च तद्राज्यं तस्माद्वै मन्त्रविन्नृप ॥
भूयः प्रादात्स तस्यैव वचनञ्चेदमब्रवीत् ॥ 11 ॥
1.156.m: Having accepted that kingdom from him, that knower of mantras, O king, / gave it back to him once more and spoke these words:

1.156.s:
na me rājyena kartavyaṃ kiñcidevāsti pārthiva ..
na dhanena na kāmena yājitā dhruvayājñiyāḥ .. 12 ..
1.156.d:
न मे राज्येन कर्तव्यं किञ्चिदेवास्ति पार्थिव ॥
न धनेन न कामेन याजिता ध्रुवयाज्ञियाः ॥ 12 ॥
1.156.m: "I have no need of a kingdom whatsoever, O king, / nor of wealth, nor of desire; the permanent sacrificers have been made to sacrifice.

1.156.s:
samatvaṃ rājaśārdūla svasti gaccha gṛhānprati ..
evamuktvā yayāvatrirantardhānamatheśvaraḥ .. 13 ..
1.156.d:
समत्वं राजशार्दूल स्वस्ति गच्छ गृहान्प्रति ॥
एवमुक्त्वा ययावत्रिरन्तर्धानमथेश्वरः ॥ 13 ॥
1.156.m:
Having attained equanimity, O tiger among kings, go home safely!"
Having spoken thus, the lord Atri vanished then and there.

1.156.s:
sarvairdvijagaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ tadā gatvā sa pārthivaḥ ..
devapuṣkāraṇītoye snātamātro babhūva ha .. 14 ..
1.156.d:
सर्वैर्द्विजगणैः सार्धं तदा गत्वा स पार्थिवः ॥
देवपुष्कारणीतोये स्नातमात्रो बभूव ह ॥ 14 ॥
1.156.m:
Then, having gone along with all the hosts of twice-born, that king,
the moment he bathed in the water of the divine pond, became indeed

1.156.s:
taptajāmbūnadākāro nīlakuñcitamūrdhajaḥ ..
pṛthuvakṣā mahābāhustanukukṣirmahākaṭiḥ .. 15 ..
1.156.d:
तप्तजाम्बूनदाकारो नीलकुञ्चितमूर्धजः ॥
पृथुवक्षा महाबाहुस्तनुकुक्षिर्महाकटिः ॥ 15 ॥
1.156.m:
endowed with the appearance of heated gold, with dark, curling hair,
broad-chested, mighty-armed, slender-waisted, and broad-hipped,

1.156.s:
gandharvarājapratimaḥ sarvasattvavaśaṅkaraḥ ..
rūpaṃ tu tādṛśaṃ tasya dṛṣṭvā gandharvasattamāḥ .. 16 ..
1.156.d:
गन्धर्वराजप्रतिमः सर्वसत्त्ववशङ्करः ॥
रूपं तु तादृशं तस्य दृष्ट्वा गन्धर्वसत्तमाः ॥ 16 ॥
1.156.m:
resembling a king of the Gandharvas, subduing all creatures.
Seeing such a form of his, the foremost Gandharvas

1.156.s:
tathaivāpsaraso mukhyā diṣṭyā diṣṭyeti te'buvan ..
sabhājya pārthivaṃ tena pūjitāḥ prayayuḥ sukham .. 17 ..
1.156.d:
तथैवाप्सरसो मुख्या दिष्ट्या दिष्ट्येति तेऽबुवन् ॥
सभाज्य पार्थिवं तेन पूजिताः प्रययुः सुखम् ॥ 17 ॥
1.156.m:
and likewise the principal apsarases exclaimed, "Joy! Joy!"
Having honoured the king and being honoured by him, they departed happily.

1.156.s:
nītvā saṃvatsaraṃ tatra pūrṇe saṃvatsaraṃ nṛpaḥ ..
devatāṃścāpyathāmantrya pūjayitvā yathāvidhi .. 18 ..
1.156.d:
नीत्वा संवत्सरं तत्र पूर्णे संवत्सरं नृपः ॥
देवतांश्चाप्यथामन्त्र्य पूजयित्वा यथाविधि ॥ 18 ॥
1.156.m:
Having spent a year there, when the full year had elapsed, the king,
having taken leave of the deities and worshipped them in accordance with rule,

1.156.s:
tathā puṣkariṇīṃ puṇyāṃ guhāṃ padmasarastathā ..
āśramaṃ śailamukhyaṃ ca tathaiva ca vanaspatim .. 19 ..
1.156.d:
तथा पुष्करिणीं पुण्यां गुहां पद्मसरस्तथा ॥
आश्रमं शैलमुख्यं च तथैव च वनस्पतिम् ॥ 19 ॥
1.156.m:
and likewise [bidding farewell to] the sacred lotus-pond, the cave, the lotus-lake,
the hermitage, the foremost mountain, and the great tree,

1.156.s:
gandharvāpsarasaścaiva prayayau svapuraṃ tataḥ ..
uccasaṅgamasamprāptā dṛṣṭo vaiṣayikaistataḥ .. 1.156.20 ..
1.156.d:
गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्चैव प्रययौ स्वपुरं ततः ॥
उच्चसङ्गमसम्प्राप्ता दृष्टो वैषयिकैस्ततः ॥ 1.156.20 ॥
1.156.m:
and to the Gandharvas and apsarases, then set out for his own city.
Reaching a high assembly, he was seen by the provincial inhabitants.

1.156.s:
stuto devaprasādācca bhaktyā taiścābhinanditaḥ ..
sattvaraiśca tathā kaiścidamātyānāṃ niveditaḥ .. 21 ..
1.156.d:
स्तुतो देवप्रसादाच्च भक्त्या तैश्चाभिनन्दितः ॥
सत्त्वरैश्च तथा कैश्चिदमात्यानां निवेदितः ॥ 21 ॥
1.156.m:
Praised on account of divine grace and greeted by them with devotion,
he was also announced to his ministers by some who went swiftly.

1.156.s:
amātyāścāgataṃ śrutvā labdhakāmaṃ narādhipam ..
niryayurnagarāttasmāccaturaṅgabalānvitāḥ ..22..
1.156.d:
अमात्याश्चागतं श्रुत्वा लब्धकामं नराधिपम् ॥
निर्ययुर्नगरात्तस्माच्चतुरङ्गबलान्विताः ॥22॥
1.156.m:
Hearing that the ruler of men had returned, having attained his desire,
the ministers came forth from that city accompanied by a fourfold army.

1.156.s:
rājñaḥ pratigrahārthaṃ te gaṇamukhyapuraḥsarāḥ ..
taiḥ sametya sa rājarṣiryathāvanmanujeśvara ..23..
1.156.d:
राज्ञः प्रतिग्रहार्थं ते गणमुख्यपुरःसराः ॥
तैः समेत्य स राजर्षिर्यथावन्मनुजेश्वर ॥23॥
1.156.m:
Led by the chiefs of their corps to receive the king,
meeting with them, that royal seer, O lord of men,

1.156.s:
kalpitena gajendreṇa patākādhvajaśobhinā ..
praviveśa puraṃ hṛṣṭaḥ śākalaṃ nāma nāmataḥ .. 24 ..
1.156.d:
कल्पितेन गजेन्द्रेण पताकाध्वजशोभिना ॥
प्रविवेश पुरं हृष्टः शाकलं नाम नामतः ॥ 24 ॥
1.156.m:
delighted, mounted upon an appointed lordly elephant adorned with banners and flags,
entered the city known by the name of Śākala.

1.156.s:
rājñaḥ praveśe tatpauraiḥ sitacandanavāriṇā ..
bahuvarṇaistathā puṣpaiyathāsthāne vibhūṣitam .. 25..
1.156.d:
राज्ञः प्रवेशे तत्पौरैः सितचन्दनवारिणा ॥
बहुवर्णैस्तथा पुष्पैयथास्थाने विभूषितम् ॥ 25॥
1.156.m:
At the entrance of the king, it was adorned by its citizens in every place
with white sandalwood-water and multi-coloured flowers,

1.156.s:
candanāgurusārāṇāṃ dhūpanaiḥ surabhīkṛtam ..
mahocchritapatākāḍhyaṃ mālyadāmapariṣkṛtam.. 26 ..
1.156.d:
चन्दनागुरुसाराणां धूपनैः सुरभीकृतम् ॥
महोच्छ्रितपताकाढ्यं माल्यदामपरिष्कृतम्॥ 26 ॥
1.156.m:
made fragrant by fumigations of essences of sandalwood and agallochum,
rich in lofty flags, and decorated with garlands and wreaths,

1.156.s:
mālyamodakahastaiśca paurajānapadairyutam ..
atīva janasaṃbādhamatīva sumanoharam .. 27 ..
1.156.d:
माल्यमोदकहस्तैश्च पौरजानपदैर्युतम् ॥
अतीव जनसंबाधमतीव सुमनोहरम् ॥ 27 ॥
1.156.m:
filled with citizens and country folk bearing garlands and sweetmeats in their hands,
exceedingly crowded with people, and exceedingly enchanting.

1.156.s:
prāsādavarasaṃsthāśca gavākṣakagatāstathā ..
vedikāsthāśca paśyanti striyastaṃ manmathārditāḥ .. 28 ..
1.156.d:
प्रासादवरसंस्थाश्च गवाक्षकगतास्तथा ॥
वेदिकास्थाश्च पश्यन्ति स्त्रियस्तं मन्मथार्दिताः ॥ 28 ॥
1.156.m:
Standing upon excellent mansions, stationed at the lattice windows,
and standing on balconies, the women, afflicted by love, looked upon him.

1.156.s:
sa muṣṇanyoṣitāṃ cittaṃ dṛśaśca manujādhipaḥ ..
lājācandanacūrṇaiśca kīryamāṇaḥ samantataḥ .. 29 ..
1.156.d:
स मुष्णन्योषितां चित्तं दृशश्च मनुजाधिपः ॥
लाजाचन्दनचूर्णैश्च कीर्यमाणः समन्ततः ॥ 29 ॥
1.156.m:
Stealing the hearts and eyes of the women, that ruler of men,
strewed on all sides with parched grain and sandalwood-powder,

1.156.s:
puṣpaiśca strīkaronmuktaiḥ pūryamāṇo narādhipaḥ ..
abhigamya ca tatrāsau devatāyatanāṃstataḥ .. 1.156.30 ..
1.156.d:
पुष्पैश्च स्त्रीकरोन्मुक्तैः पूर्यमाणो नराधिपः ॥
अभिगम्य च तत्रासौ देवतायतनांस्ततः ॥ 1.156.30 ॥
1.156.m:
showered with flowers released from the hands of women, that ruler of men,
having approached the shrines of the deities there,

1.156.s:
praviveśa gṛhaṃ śrīmacchāradābhracayopamam ..
tatrābhigamanaṃ kṛtvā devatānāṃ yathāvidhi .. 31 ..
1.156.d:
प्रविवेश गृहं श्रीमच्छारदाभ्रचयोपमम् ॥
तत्राभिगमनं कृत्वा देवतानां यथाविधि ॥ 31 ॥
1.156.m:
entered his splendid palace resembling a mass of autumn clouds.
Having paid homage to the deities there according to rule,

1.156.s:
saṃpūjya brāhmaṇānbhaktyā vividhairdhanasañcayaiḥ ..
sabhāsthaṃ sāntvayāmāsa paurajānapadaṃ janam .. 32 ..
1.156.d:
संपूज्य ब्राह्मणान्भक्त्या विविधैर्धनसञ्चयैः ॥
